41e87f8e62cd17f2.text: Manchester United have reportedly added Borussia Dortmund centre-back Joane Gadou to their defensive shortlist for 2027. The post Joane Gadou: Man United know what it would take to beat Arsenal and Liverpool to Dortmund gem appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
41e87f8e62cd17f2.content: In 2027, Manchester United are expected to pull off a major defensive overhaul. After rebuilding the attack and midfield in successive summers, the back line is next to take centre stage as INEOS look to assemble a dream team. The transfer strategy aside, the Red Devils’ defensive struggles, which have cost them win after win, leave Ineos with no choice but to execute that plan to the letter. There is already a clear suggestion of which defenders are on United’s radar. Nathan Collins , Maxi Araujo and Calvin Bassey have reportedly been linked, but the list keeps growing. Joane Gadou added to Man United’s wishlist Now, according to Bild as cited by Sport Witness , Borussia Dortmund centre-back Joane Gadou has been added to the Red Devils’ defensive options. Gadou has enjoyed a rapid rise at Dortmund since his summer move from RB Salzburg. At just 19, he is already establishing himself as a dominant, assertive centre-back who wins his duels, shows real personality, and is excellent at playing out from the back. On Tuesday night, Arsenal saw first-hand what a rare talent he is, as the Frenchman produced an outstanding display against the English champions. Joane Gadou, are we serious? pic.twitter.com/0gTCzEpxRN — Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 25, 2026 Dortmund’s equaliser began with a surging run forward by Gadou before he provided the assist for goalscorer Maximilian Beier. Dortmund name their price It is now being reported in Germany: “Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United will need €80m if they wish to sign Joane Gadou from Borussia Dortmund in future.” With the young defender contracted to BVB until at least 2031: “Dortmund’s leadership are sitting back comfortably for the time being. They would be more than happy to sit back and watch a bidding war develop for their future superstar.” Whether United are prepared to pay that sum for the Dortmund gem remains to be seen. However, given the youngster’s trajectory, if he maintains it, any club that wants him will have to break the bank. 115a26749fe73a0a.title: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty
115a26749fe73a0a.text: Manchester United should trigger Archie Brown’s £19 million release clause to solve their left-back shortage, the article argues. The post Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
115a26749fe73a0a.content: Not signing a left-back has come back to bite Manchester United. An injury to the club’s only natural left-back, Luke Shaw , has forced them to rely on makeshift options, several of whom have struggled badly. The position has become the Red Devils’ clearest weakness. Luke Shaw injury 2026-27 Injury or suspension: Muscle injury · From: 2026-10-11 · To: 2026-11-22 Stat Luke Shaw Days out 43 Matches missed 7 Source: Transfermarkt · Updated 26 Nov 2026 Last week United chief executive Omar Berrada told Sky Sports : “It’s widely reported we looked for reinforcement in the left-back position… could we have signed an additional defender? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value. There’s no point spending £40–50m on players we don’t think improve the team.” As the winter transfer window approaches, United are therefore expected to stick to that transfer principle: They will not sign just any left-back; they want someone who genuinely improves the side. Archie Brown could be that player. The Fenerbahçe left-back has long been linked with Old Trafford, yet United have never acted on their interest. Tempting Archie Brown release clause A golden opportunity has now arisen. German transfer journalist Florian Plettenberg reports that Brown has a €23 million (£19 million) release clause that can be triggered this winter, and the 24-year-old is keen on a move to the Premier League. Archie Brown has a release clause worth around €23m, valid for both the winter and summer transfer windows. The 23 y/o is a regular starter at Fenerbahçe and has also impressed with some very strong performances in the Champions League. Under contract until 2028, a move… pic.twitter.com/NKQljznnRd — Florian Plettenberg (@Plettigoal) November 25, 2026 Man United must seize Archie Brown transfer opportunity United reportedly have a £50 million winter budget, with a striker also viewed as a crucial signing for Mauricio Pochettino. If Ineos are wise and want a successful winter transfer window, they must pounce on Brown. He is athletic, bombs forward down the left flank and thrives in high-tempo football without needing time to adapt to physical duels – ideal for Pochettino’s style. He offers progressive carries, crosses and goals while contributing clearances, interceptions and tackles, making him one of the most complete left-backs available. Securing a player of Brown’s quality for £19 million would be daylight robbery. It would strengthen a major weakness while still leaving room to address other areas, like the attack, as Pochettino fights to keep United in the Premier League. 26e0bda7dcd92190.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
26e0bda7dcd92190.text: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. 26e0bda7dcd92190.content:
“I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.”
It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil. Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United, whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club.
I prepare for a possible meltdown because rare archive footage, which opens the documentary, captures a televised standoff between Cantona and a few French journalists. He objects to the fact that L’Équipe had described his kung fu kick against a Crystal Palace supporter in 1995 as “unforgivable”. After asking who is truly “unforgivable”, and highlighting the historical sins of the Catholic church, Cantona sneers: “I piss on the pope’s arse. Just as I piss on the arse of certain journalists … including you and you,” he says, pointing to two outraged writers.
Now, 30 years later, Cantona emerges in his home city of Marseille, wearing a natty trilby. Within minutes I can tell that the flower of evil is elsewhere because Cantona is in a generous mood. As he recalls that bitterly sensational clash with the French reporters he smiles: “I’m a good client for the journalists – and they are a good client for me to express myself. We play a bit like the cat and the mouse. Sometimes we have good relationships, sometimes a bad relationship. But it’s always interesting and exciting.”
This might be Cantona at his most angelic, stretching the truth about the supposed thrill of his journalistic encounters, but it’s fitting that the film starts with the 60-year-old quoting Charles Baudelaire, the 19th-century French poet who, in his Flowers of Evil collection, wrote: “I am the wound and the knife/I am the blow and the cheek/ … The victim and the executioner …”
Cantona’s brilliance and spite defined his troubled time at six French clubs between 1983 and 1992. He could have “disappeared” from football because, despite being France’s most gifted player, he had fallen out with the national manager. The young Cantona said: “I hope people realise Henri Michel is one of the most incompetent coaches in world football.”
Michel Platini, who replaced Michel, persuaded Cantona to end his fleeting retirement in 1992 by moving to England. As Cantona says: “I knew it will be my last chance … and it’s really in England where I regain this passion for football … it’s a rebirth.”
The documentary provides a compelling account of his turbulent love affair with English football – but ignores a strange prelude at Sheffield Wednesday. Cantona tells me this forgotten strand of his story with amused incredulity. “I arrived at Sheffield Wednesday and we played a friendly. We won 4-3 and I scored three goals. And then I waited to sign the contract. At the end of the week they said: ‘You have to spend one more week on trial.’ I said: ‘No. I leave.’”
Who managed Wednesday then? “Trevor Francis – who was a great player,” Cantona replies. “Howard Wilkinson heard about that and asked me to come to Leeds. I arrived in Leeds and then we became champions and it was a great time.”
That deceptively simple last sentence fails to capture the seismic impact Cantona had on English football and especially on Leeds, who won the league title for the first time in 18 years in 1992. “It was old-fashioned football,” Cantona says. “It was interesting. There was also, for me, the feeling of adding something different.”
Was it disheartening playing antiquated football? “No, because I played with wonderful players. We had a great midfield with Gary Speed, David Batty, Gary McAllister and Gordon Strachan. And quickly [the following season] I arrive at Manchester United with Alex Ferguson. The club had the Busby Babes. That was wonderful football. Manchester United has always been a club where winning in a good way is important.”
This should be the moment to ask Cantona about the contrast with the current moribund state of United but, rather than falling out over his refusal to discuss the club now, it’s enough to hear him in full flow. “This club always loved people with different personalities. They loved George Best, Brian McClair, [Norman] Whiteside, [Roy] Keane …”
Cantona was adored at Old Trafford, as he had been at Leeds before his shock departure to United for a mere £1m in November 1992. He also led United to their first Premier League title, in 1993, after a 26-year drought.
There are great clubs in Italy, Spain and Germany so could he have resurrected his career in one of these countries? Cantona shakes his head: “I love Italian football. I love Spanish football. I love Barcelona. But nothing can compare to English football and the fans, the way they sing and express themselves. It’s so powerful.”
Cantona remembers that, when he arrived in England, “in the street, nobody knew me. I felt free for the first time in my life. I could go have a drink somewhere, listen to some music and it was always peaceful.”
Ferguson recalls that he asked Guy Roux, the wise old manager who nurtured Cantona at his first club, Auxerre, how to harness his volatile talent. Roux offered two words: “Love him.”
Cantona nods: “I’m instinctive. If I feel bad I go. If I feel good, I try to create a relationship. And when I arrive in Manchester I see the ghosts of the past. I felt this very strong energy and I thought: ‘Maybe this is the place where I will have the opportunity to express myself.

0184e41f50b9337a.title: Sky Sports: Everton could rival Man United for 'amazing' striker
0184e41f50b9337a.text: Everton could reignite their interest in Manchester United target Folarin Balogun in January, according to sky sports. Everton came close to signing Balogun last summer, but the deal fell through. The Toffees could make another attempt to sign the United States international as they seek to provide competition for Thierno Barry. Man United have been […] Article written by Henry Thornton .
0184e41f50b9337a.content: Everton could reignite their interest in Manchester United target Folarin Balogun in January, according to sky sports . Everton came close to signing Balogun last summer, but the deal fell through. The Toffees could make another attempt to sign the United States international as they seek to provide competition for Thierno Barry. Man United have been linked with Balogun since Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival as the club’s head coach. The striker is reportedly keen on reuniting with Pochettino, having worked under him with the USMNT. Man United could beat Everton to Balogun’s signing Balogun, described by Marseille right-back Timothy Weah as ‘ amazing ‘, rejected a move to Everton last summer due to the way the club handled his medical. The Toffees claimed they discovered an injury in his medical, but the striker and Monaco denied it. They then attempted to renegotiate the deal on cheaper terms in case the injury left him unable to play. Balogun was also reportedly angered by Everton’s attempt to sign United striker Joshua Zirkzee. David Moyes’ side are still interested in Zirkzee. Given what transpired in the last transfer window, the Monaco star may be reluctant to join Everton, potentially handing United an advantage in the race for his signature. The Mancunian giants are seeking to sign a striker in January to strengthen their attack, given Benjamin Sesko’s fitness struggles. Balogun’s previous relationship with Pochettino makes him a potential serious target, but his asking price could be a stumbling block. The 25-year-old could be available for around £40m, the fee Everton almost paid to sign him. United would have less than £50m budget in January, suggesting that Balogun could be out of reach. The Mancunian giants may also prioritise a more proven striker than the former Arsenal academy graduate, although finding an affordable option in January could prove difficult. Article written by Henry Thornton .

8e13e720a9457e39.title: Man United team up with Liverpool to prepare lucrative legal claim against Man City
8e13e720a9457e39.text: Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham have enlisted London-based media, entertainment and technology specialists, Wiggin
8e13e720a9457e39.content:
Man United team up with Liverpool to prepare lucrative legal claim against Man City
Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham have enlisted London-based media, entertainment and technology specialists, Wiggin
Manchester United and Liverpool are using the same law firm to prepare legal action against scandal-ridden Manchester City.
An independent commission found City guilty of violating the Premier League's financial regulations, revealing that the club had artificially inflated its revenue by £900million between 2009 and 2018 through 'scam' commercial dealings.
City have lodged an appeal against the verdict and continue to protest their innocence. Meanwhile, their rivals are gearing up to pursue individual claims that could run into hundreds of millions of pounds.
The Guardian reports that United, Liverpool and Tottenham have enlisted London-based media, entertainment and technology specialists, Wiggin. Arsenal, meanwhile, are utilising their retained solicitors, HFS Kramer, to pursue their claim.
It is further understood that there has been some collaboration among the clubs working with Wiggin, who have also appointed the same analysts to evaluate the scale of their potential losses arising from City's financial misconduct. The claims, however, would be pursued independently by each club.
"The cases are similar but different," a source commented. "The ultimate causation may be the same, but the damages will be different, so they will be separate claims."
The report further reveals that Spurs initially engaged Wiggin while Daniel Levy was chairman, making them the first club to pursue legal action against City before Liverpool and United followed suit.
Together with Arsenal, the three clubs filed legal notices in November 2024 to safeguard their right to pursue compensation against City.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
Each of the clubs suffered losses to City throughout the nine-year period. United and Liverpool finished as runners-up behind them in 2012 and 2014 respectively, while Tottenham were denied Champions League qualification by City on four occasions.
In 2017, Arsenal fell short of Champions League qualification by finishing fifth, two positions behind City. It would be a further six years before Arsenal secured a place in the competition again.
Furthermore, the Gunners sold five of their finest players to City between 2009 and 2018. Arsenal could therefore pursue additional losses on the basis that those transfers were artificially bankrolled.
Beyond those four clubs, several others have legitimate grievances. Chelsea, Everton and Newcastle were among the sides denied Champions League football during the period under scrutiny.
Stoke, meanwhile, were beaten by City in the 2011 FA Cup final. Victory would have secured the Potters a place in the Europa League. Former Stoke boss Tony Pulis declared following City's guilty verdict that they ought to be awarded the trophy.

Manchester United bekerja sama dengan Liverpool dan Tottenham untuk menyiapkan klaim hukum terhadap Manchester City.

Klub-klub tersebut menunjuk firma hukum Wiggin untuk menuntut ganti rugi atas pelanggaran finansial Manchester City.

The post Nico Paz: Real Madrid’s transfer stance emerges amid Man United’s interest in Argentine genius appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
f60330c65cb6baaa.content: Manchester United’s on-field struggles aside, INEOS are also concerned with the contract situations of several key stars. None more so than Manchester United club captain Bruno Fernandes , who once again dragged the Red Devils back into the contest against Sporting CP on Wednesday. The Portuguese superstar has not had the impact fans have come to associate with him, yet the club captain remains the top scorer this season. However, with the 20-time English league champions languishing second-from-bottom in the Premier League table, the 32-year-old could be finally fed up with the situation. INEOS’ lack of help in the transfer market and the loss of another manager, Michael Carrick, have sowed the seeds of doubt in the Portugal international. Nico Paz on United’s radar As a result, he has ended up rejecting both of United’s contract extension offers , and there is a chance he leaves as early as January . Naturally, the Old Trafford side are keeping their eyes on long-term successors, and Nico Paz of Como has caught their fancy , and for good reason. The Argentine has six goals and eight assists already this season, including a brace against United in the Champions League. N. Paz 26/27 stats Stat Serie A, UEFA Champions League Apps 16 Minutes 1265 Goals 6 Assists 8 However, Real Madrid held all the aces as they had a buyback clause inserted into his deal with Como. Spanish outlet AS have some good news for United fans. Real Madrid’s stance will be music to United’s ears Los Blancos are not sure about bringing back the Argentina international as he will demand regular minutes, something Jose Mourinho cannot guarantee considering the riches at his disposal. Also, the 22-year-old will cost €80 million to bring back to the Bernabéu, and such an outlay on the attack is not planned for next summer. “Inside Valdebebas, however, nothing has changed regarding the club’s assessment of the Tenerife-born playmaker. In fact, doubts remain about a possible return.” “Real Madrid know firsthand that Paz wants regular minutes and a prominent role, and right now any move back to the Spanish capital would mean competing primarily with players such as Bellingham and Arda Güler, while Brahim Díaz and Rodrygo Goes also wait for their opportunities.” January approach unlikely “Any return would also involve a significant financial commitment. A deal could cost as much as €80 million ($88 million), dwarfing the €60 million ($66 million) Como paid to acquire Paz’s registration rights.” Whether United jump for Nico Paz remains to be seen, but he would certainly add a different dimension to United’s attack. A January approach, as previously reported, is certainly off the cards due to INEOS’ meagre transfer budget for the winter window. ed572e47dfe985e2.text: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. ed572e47dfe985e2.content:
Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. Simon Burnton
Nottingham Forest v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times GMT)
When Leeds recruited Dominic Calvert-Lewin on a free transfer during the summer of 2025 it is fair to say many of their fans were underwhelmed. Now though the news that the England centre-forward has penned a contract extension at Elland Road is a cause for celebration in West Yorkshire. Calvert-Lewin had proved somewhat injury-prone at his former club, Everton, yet Daniel Farke evidently knew what he was doing. The newly robust 29-year-old has scored 18 goals in 46 Premier League appearances for Leeds, 17 arriving in the last 36 games. With Calvert-Lewin now having signed a new, improved deal extending until 2029, attention is turning to Farke’s own contract. The German’s current agreement expires next summer but renewal talks have been under way for some time and, for the moment at least, the normally open Leeds manager has turned coy. “I’ve fallen in love with the club,” said Farke ahead of his upwardly mobile team’s home meeting with Coventry. “But I’m not willing to speak about my future.” Louise Taylor
Mauricio Pochettino will send out his first Manchester United XI at Old Trafford on Saturday hoping Senne Lammens’ errors for the season are over. The fumble of a simple aerial ball late on at Sporting that allowed Luis Suárez to salvage a point on Wednesday was dismal from the goalkeeper despite his head coach’s protestations that the backline as a collective was at fault for allowing the opening. Karl Darlow, United’s second choice, has Premier League experience after a stint as Leeds’ first choice towards the end of last season but has played only 30 games in all divisions in the past three years. That means, probably, that Pochettino will retain Lammens but if more mistakes follow then the Wales international Darlow may be handed his chance. Jamie Jackson
Manchester United v Brentford, Saturday 3pm
Being forced from the field with “stud marks all the way down the back of his calf” after a clash with Tottenham’s Mohammed Kudus towards the end of last weekend’s match led to Leif Davis missing his first Premier League minutes of the season. It left Ipswich’s central defensive pairing of Issa Diop and Dara O’Shea as their only players to have been on the pitch for the entirety of the league campaign so far. O’Shea said this week of playing with Diop that “the more games we play with each other, obviously the better we’ll become as a pair”. They’re being given the best possible chance, even if Ipswich are yet to keep a clean sheet and have already conceded 22 goals, from an opposition xG of 21.82. Only the league’s bottom two have conceded a higher xG. More surprising is that Aston Villa have the next highest tally, with 18.56. Tuesday, when Villa lost 1-0 at Galatasaray, marked out a month since their last win. They have drawn three and scored in only two of their six outings. Ipswich may be just two points and two places outside the bottom three, but a win would put these teams level. SB
Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm
“We are having a great week,” Virgil van Dijk said after Liverpool followed up their 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United with a 3-0 win at Club Brugge that reinforced the strides being made by Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Andoni Iraola’s team overall. Liverpool’s week contrasts starkly with their local rivals. Everton suffered the heaviest defeat and produced arguably the worst performance of David Moyes’s second spell in charge on Monday when going down 4-0 at Brentford. James Tarkowski’s red card made no difference, so superior were Keith Andrews’s side from the start, but the absence of the Everton captain could be keenly felt on Sunday. Liverpool won the first Merseyside derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium last season from a 100th-minute corner, capitalising on disruption to Everton’s central defence when Jarrad Branthwaite went off injured. Without Tarkowski the hosts may be vulnerable again. Jake O’Brien could get his long-awaited chance to stake a claim as Branthwaite’s partner in the most demanding circumstances. Andy Hunter
Everton v Liverpool, Sunday noon
Georginio Rutter offered an insight into the Fabian Hürzeler effect at Brighton this week. “He has changed the mentality of some of the players: he wants us to run and give 100% – we did that last season but not as hard as he wanted,” said the Frenchman. “Some new players have come in and given us a new vibe.” While the likes of Luka Vuskovic – who surpassed Rutter as Brighton’s record signing in the summer – and Chema Andrés have quickly established themselves as first choices, the 24-year-old forward who joined from Leeds in 2024 has fallen behind Greek teenager Charalampos Kostoulas since recovering from a foot injury. Rutter started in the defeat by Hull last week but missed the opportunity

a8e44ffa6240e462.title: 'He's not a predictable character' - Working with Manchester United icon Eric Cantona
a8e44ffa6240e462.text: Cantona: Flower of Evil, an intimate portrait of the legendary former Man Utd striker, is set to be released in two weeks.
a8e44ffa6240e462.content:
Eric Cantona has turned down plenty of offers from documentary makers to make a film on his life over the last 15 years, but over a dinner in Lisbon with two British directors, he gave the green light to their vision.
"When Eric says no, he means no," David Tryhorn, co-director of Cantona: Flower of Evil, said. "I think we came at it from an angle where we said we wanted to make something a bit more artistic.
Flower of Evil is released in cinemas in two weeks. It's not an ordinary sports documentary, but the end product will leave Manchester United fans immersed in the big screen as Cantona's years at Old Trafford are beautifully retold.
The documentary premiered at the Cannes Film Festival earlier this year, and Tryhorn sat beside Cantona as he watched the final cut for the first time. "It was very nerve-racking," Tryhorn recalled during an interview with the Manchester Evening News.
"As mild-mannered as he is, he's not a predictable character. And so you're watching something like the kung fu kick, and you're sat right next to the guy thinking this is already quite a surreal experience seeing this on the big screen.
"But then he gave me a fist bump at the end of the film. And he's said since that he's very, very proud of the film and he's really, really happy with it, and that it's better than he imagined it would be."
Cantona had no final editorial say in the film, which is rare in the era of sports documentaries masquerading as carefully crafted PR pieces, but "Eric relishes the fact that he is a flawed human being," according to Tryhorn.
The Frenchman's involvement in the film was limited once Tryhorn and his co-director, Ben Nicholas, had completed around 20 hours of interviews with him, the large majority of which had to be left on the edit room floor.
"He loves the fact he is flawed, like you or I," said Tryhorn. "We can be liars, we can be hypocrites, but that's who we want to be. That's what living is all about. That's quite refreshing from a filmmaker's point of view to get to make a film on someone who doesn't really care about their image."

Controversy followed Cantona for much of his career, and the film opens with old footage of him saying he wants to "p*** on" journalists from French newspaper L'Équipe.
Naturally, Cantona's infamous kung fu kick at Selhurst Park features heavily in the film. "I should have kicked him harder," says Cantona about the incident. Tryhorn laughed: "I'm sure he's said it with his tongue slightly in his cheek. He has got quite a mischievous sense of humour."
It took six months of negotiations with the Premier League to persuade them to license the footage for the film. "They had never licensed the clip before, but you can't make a Cantona documentary without that", said Tryhorn.
"We needed to make Selhurst feel as big as it was because it was huge. You know, I remember listening to the game on the radio next to my dad and realising straight away, this is giant, this is huge, this is an incredible moment. Oh my God, nothing like this has ever happened in English football before."
The fallout from the kung fu kick dominated news bulletins. Cantona was fined £20,000 and banned from playing football. He was also sentenced to two weeks in prison, which was later reduced to 120 hours of community service.
Cantona decided to retire when his ban was nearly served, deciding he'd had enough, but Ferguson jetted to France and got another two seasons out of him.
"I don't think Eric becomes the icon he is without that moment. I genuinely don't," Tryhorn said. "You know, obviously he won the league when he came to Leeds, and he won the league in his first season at United, which was a huge thing, and then again in the second season when he was player of the year.
"He's become the King of Old Trafford by that point. But I think the kick is what makes him an icon, and I think for fans as well, it's almost a f*** you. It's one of those iconic moments that underlines that this guy is not just phenomenal at football, but a rebel and a champion of something greater."
The early edit of Flower of Evil included several interviewees, but the decision was made to limit the voices in the film to amplify Cantona's. "It just wasn't really working," said Tryhorn of the initial edit.
"We boiled it down and thought this is actually like a romance, it's like a love story between him and Alex Ferguson. Because obviously when Eric arrives in Manchester, Eric needs Ferguson to revive his career, and Ferguson needs Eric to win the league.
"They have their meet-cute, they come together, and they grow happy together. And then obviously Selhurst Park happens, Eric transgresses and the relationship kind of falls apart from a dramatic perspective.
"I know in reality Ferguson stands by him very tightly. But then the sort of coming-together season is Eric repaying the faith that Ferguson has shown in him. And so we kind of viewed it as almost a love story between the two."
Tryhorn continued: "There was even one stage where we cut everyone out apart from just the two of them. Most of the film plays as a two-hander. But then we sort of set rules for the other people who come in, needing to justify their stature within the film."
Ferguson's team receive an immense number of requests for his time. When he does agree to speak in something, a pre-arranged slot is typically agreed, but the legendary former manager waived that rule for Cantona.
"He usually does quite a limited amount of time," said Tryhorn. "For Eric, he was far more flexible. I think they still have a very close relationship. They still text, they're still in touch, and they'll still meet if Eric's over in Manchester. I think that comes across in the film. He loves Eric."

51432709cd74169b.title: Three familiar demons Man Utd must finally overcome at Old Trafford vs Brentford
51432709cd74169b.text: Manchester United will be desperate to return to winning ways when they welcome Brentford to Old Trafford in a crucial Premier League encounter. The Red Devils currently sit 19th in the Premier League table and desperately need positive results to climb away from the relegation zone. Manager Mauricio Pochettino will know that his players must […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
51432709cd74169b.content: Manchester United will be desperate to return to winning ways when they welcome Brentford to Old Trafford in a crucial Premier League encounter. The Red Devils currently sit 19th in the Premier League table and desperately need positive results to climb away from the relegation zone. Manager Mauricio Pochettino will know that his players must get three things right if they are to give themselves a genuine chance of securing all three points on Saturday. Stop conceding early goals One of United’s biggest problems this season has been their inability to start each half on the front foot. The Red Devils found themselves 2-0 down against Liverpool, Aston Villa and Roma within the opening 20 minutes, repeatedly leaving themselves with an uphill battle. They have often managed to respond after those disastrous starts, only to undo their progress by conceding shortly after the interval. Aston Villa and Como both scored twice within 10 minutes of the restart. Pochettino must ensure his players remain switched on throughout the contest rather than allowing Brentford to seize control through another sluggish start. Eliminate individual mistakes United must also accept that they have played a significant part in their own downfall this season. The players have made far too many mistakes, which have had a ripple effect on the entire squad. Senne Lammens made two costly mistakes during the recent outing against Sporting, with the Portuguese side capitalising on both opportunities. Leny Yoro was harshly shown a red card against Liverpool, but the young defender could have avoided the controversy by resisting the temptation to make a clumsy challenge on Alexander Isak. Lisandro Martinez, Youri Tielemans, Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt and Ayden Heaven have also been guilty of costly errors at the back. United must cut out these individual mistakes and stop giving their opponents easy opportunities. Officials must do their job Refereeing decisions have become another major talking point surrounding United’s recent performances. Pochettino has every reason to feel frustrated with how the last two games have been officiated. The Red Devils were forced to play with 10 men for 80 minutes in the hostile environment of Anfield after the unfortunate sending-off of Yoro. Against Sporting, United also had two goals ruled out for fouls, decisions that ultimately contributed to them dropping two valuable points. United cannot allow refereeing controversies to become an excuse for their own shortcomings, but they have every right to expect consistency from the officials. Fair and consistent officiating should be the bare minimum at this level of football. Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .

a786210ad2c395f8.title: The inside story of Mauricio Pochettino's first week at Man United - Message to players, 12-hour days and staff demands
a786210ad2c395f8.text: Mauricio Pochettino has been in charge of Manchester United for just over a week and he has crammed plenty in during that time.
a786210ad2c395f8.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's message to the Manchester United squad in the first team meeting he held at Carrington was simple: 'I trust you completely,' he told a group of players devoid of confidence. 'Until you break it'.
It summed up the 54-year-old's first week or so in charge of United. He is warm and engaging with players and staff, but he can also be intense and demanding. He expects things to be done the way he wants and to be done well.
The players left that meeting buoyed by Pochettino's approach but under no illusions that if they did break the trust, the road back would likely lead to a dead end. So far, the trust has flowed both ways. He has wrapped a protective blanket around them and made it clear he absolutely has their back.
Pochettino has made every effort to talk this group up. Even after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in his first game, he spoke of the "very positive" way the team approached the test following Leny Yoro's red card. "They like to fight" and "we made an unbelievable effort" reinforced the messaging to a squad who could have been forgiven for thinking 'here we go again'.
He took a similar path in Lisbon on Tuesday, using a question about whether United could be seen as fragile to talk instead about how strong they were. That came just after he had taken aim at ProRef for the decision to send Yoro off at Anfield.
It was part diversionary tactic, part attempt to foster a siege mentality. It felt like it was straight out of the Sir Alex Ferguson playbook. Pochettino went into that press conference at the Estadio Jose Alvalade with a desire to talk about the incidents at Anfield and how they had cost his team, and United made sure he was given the opportunity to do so.
He spoke about the need to defend his club and it was refreshing to see him doing so. It also felt like he was using the controversy surrounding Yoro's dismissal to fuel the sense that the world is against them at the moment. Pochettino certainly likes to foster a closeness within the dressing room and this is a useful tool for doing so.
His smile around Carrington has been almost constant, and he regularly envelops his players in hugs or puts an arm around their shoulders. Even as he walked out at Anfield after a disastrous first game in charge, he punched a journalist who is an old acquaintance on the arm and looked and sounded upbeat and positive.

He has maintained that mood despite a chronic lack of sleep. 12-hour days at Carrington aren't uncommon and on Monday morning he arrived at 6.40am on the back of that defeat to Liverpool. There is a lot to do and Pochettino and his staff are using every minute possible to make an impact. He is still staying in a hotel in Cheshire that the club are putting him up in, but he isn't spending much time there.
He is arriving early to plan sessions, hold meetings with his early-bird staff and make sure no stone is left unturned in the desire to turn the club around. He has already become something of a unifying figure.
Long days on the training pitch have become a fairly regular feature, although sessions have shortened a little this week, with the sense that his methods are now beginning to get across to the players, as seen in the performance in Lisbon.
It was after that game that Pochettino asked long-time No.2, Jesus Perez, how many training sessions they had had until that point. Perez accompanies Pochettino to almost every press conference and is across everything going on around his boss. They have an implicit trust in each other.
Pochettino wasn't sure if it was five or six sessions. 'Six', said Perez. It's actually five. They can be forgiven for losing count amid the maelstrom of their first week in charge.
Away from the grass, Pochettino and Perez have made sure they are across everything that is going on at the club. The Argentine has already shown his relaxed nature, allowing the club's social media team to post the starting XI graphic in positional order and letting United post a squad list on their website for a European away game, an approach Michael Carrick had stopped this season because he felt it could hand an advantage to the opposition.
Pochettino has made an effort to get to know every member of staff in the first-team building at Carrington. He wants to know and understand them, and has given people the impression that he is interested in them and genuinely cares.
But there has been some surprise, in a positive way, at just how intense and demanding Pochettino and Perez can be. They are determined to ensure everything is done to the highest possible standard and have made it clear that every member of staff has a role to play in that.
It feels like roadblocks are being placed in his path at United. Refereeing decisions have gone against his side in both his games in charge so far. Individual errors have been costly in Liverpool and Lisbon. In the Portuguese capital, United were unable to fly back after the game due to airspace restrictions, with the airport located in the city centre so late-night flights aren't possible.
There was nothing they could do about it, but rather than seeing it as another impediment, Pochettino was relaxed. He didn't need to rush media duties after the game, and stood idly next to the stage as Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca finished his own press conference.
United had the option to use a training pitch in Lisbon on Thursday, but it was a recovery day, and Pochettino told the players they could use the hotel gym and pool for that.
He has been present for a few of the gym sessions, and it was noticeable that United's players were using weights in a post-match session on the side of the pitch on Wednesday. 9f76602dbf156f52.content: Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo provided Manchester United with a stark reminder of what they are missing during the midweek 2-2 draw against Sporting in the Champions League. The Uruguayan was a constant threat all night, giving the Red Devils’ backline a headache while also providing ample support to his own defence. New manager Mauricio Pochettino would like such a character in his team, a marauding left-back who is solid at the back and can cause the opposition all sorts of problems while going forward. The English giants are expected to upgrade their left-back position at the turn of the year, with Luke Shaw struggling to stay fit and Patrick Dorgu hardly an improvement in the position. Araujo is already linked with a move, but United have several others on their wish list, including Club Brugge speedster Joaquin Seys . United wanted Seys in the summer United explored the possibility of strengthening their left-back position before the start of the season and they had their eyes on Seys as well. The Belgian was coming off an impressive campaign, where he registered five goals and eight assists in 55 appearances across all competitions. However, the Red Devils failed to get a deal across the line, a decision they now live to regret. United are 19th in the league table after 11 games, already 20 points behind leaders Arsenal. The Red Devils are going through another managerial upheaval, with Pochettino taking over from Michael Carrick last week. 989ed37b4e063523.content: Manchester United have discussed the possibility of signing Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde ahead of the winter transfer window. The Red Devils were linked with multiple left-backs last summer, and Balde was one of the top names on the wishlist. A deal did not materialise. The Spaniard decided to stay put with the La Liga champions amid the transfer speculation. The decision has not proved worthwhile for him, and Sport recently claimed that he has privately opened the door for a mid-season departure. Speaking to The United Stand , journalist Ben Jacobs revealed that Balde is a ‘growing’ name discussed at United, given he could be available this winter. Jacobs said: “It seems to be a name [on Balde] that is growing in terms of the noise I am hearing within Carrington, probably because he might actually be available in the month of January.” Left-back pursuit may depend on Luke Shaw’s fitness Luke Shaw stayed unscathed throughout the previous campaign. The England international started every league game and was one of the season’s standout performers. There were still concerns about how his workload could be hampered by United’s return to European football due to his injury record. Shaw has yet to play in the Champions League this term, but has already missed several games. He has been absent for 10 matches due to injuries alone. Shaw returned to the squad in midweek, and his fitness over the next few weeks could determine whether the Red Devils spend on a new left-back. Manager Mauricio Pochettino has recently experimented with Lisandro Martinez in the role, considering Patrick Dorgu has looked vulnerable when asked to operate in a defensive capacity for United. If United can’t sort out the position between Shaw and Martinez, they could revive their pursuit of Balde. The Spaniard could be available for £33 million, as per Sport , but United are more likely to explore a loan deal for the La Masia graduate with an option to buy at the end of the campaign. Balde is a quality ball-playing left-back but has had injury problems of his own. The Red Devils may want to assess whether he can suit the league before considering a permanent deal. 9c4d28172d2b38bd.title: "Everybody needs to be": Former Man United star Paul Pogba gives Man United blueprint to follow to get back to the top
9c4d28172d2b38bd.text: Paul Pogba urges Manchester United to give Mauricio Pochettino time and cites Arsenal's patient rebuild as a potential model. The post “Everybody needs to be”: Former Man United star Paul Pogba gives Man United blueprint to follow to get back to the top appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
9c4d28172d2b38bd.content: Manchester United have gone back to the drawing board once again after sacking Michael Carrick. United’s current situation Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has become the eighth manager to be given the permanent role after the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013. The Red Devils are in quite a pickle as they are out of the League Cup and sit 19th in the Premier League. The Champions League is going slightly better with seven points from five matches, but they are still at risk of not making it into the knockout phase with three league matches remaining. Pochettino has so far lost 0–4 at Anfield to Liverpool and drawn 2–2 with Sporting CP. Tomorrow will mark the Argentine’s first home game as manager against Brentford. Paul Pogba’s thoughts Speaking to talkSPORT , the former United man Paul Pogba gave his thoughts on the current situation at the club. Pogba threw his weight behind the new manager when he claimed, “I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he’s a great manager. And I’m sad also for Michael Carrick because I don’t think he had enough time to show and prove himself.” He continued, “but I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there’s a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win, and we all think that they should change manager.” Pogba also drew on his own struggles at the club and stated, “all I think about this team – I’ve been there – is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside. Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things.” The 2018 World Cup winner also explained that the Red Devils could do worse than to follow the Arsenal model. He added, “the players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere – like Arsenal. Arsenal had a great time with Thierry Henry. They had a great [era], they went to Champions League final, they won the Premier League. And they had a [long] time [before] winning again.” Pogba explained that Arsenal made their own way back to the top and he continued, “that’s all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about them like they are the team that it was back then. You need to respect, you need to let them grow again and get back to the top.” Paul Pogba Man United career stats Apps Goals 235 39 Source: Wikipedia and API-Football Featured image Ed Sykes via Getty Images online polls The post “Everybody needs to be”: Former Man United star Paul Pogba gives Man United blueprint to follow to get back to the top appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .

206a71db44474dac.title: Uruguay international open to leaving Sporting CP for Man Utd in January as Mauricio Pochettino eyes Luke Shaw replacement
206a71db44474dac.text: Uruguay international open to leaving Sporting CP for Man Utd in January as Mauricio Pochettino eyes Luke Shaw replacement
206a71db44474dac.content:
United convinced by Lisbon display
According to Sport Witness, United used Wednesday's trip to Lisbon to assess Araujo up close and left convinced by the 26-year-old. Making his 14th start in 15 appearances this season, the Uruguay international played the full 90 minutes and assisted Luis Suarez's 33rd-minute opener. Mutual appreciation now exists between both parties, with the defender's camp very open to a winter switch to Old Trafford.
Red Devils renew summer interest
United's admiration for Araujo dates back to April, when they were among several Premier League clubs monitoring his progress. Despite finishing the summer without strengthening that position, reports last month linked both United and Arsenal with renewed plans to pursue him. At that stage, a source informed the outlet that there had been "nothing new" since their initial enquiries earlier in the year.
In August, Araujo had quietened transfer speculation by extending his Sporting contract until 2030, securing a top salary alongside an €80 million release clause. However, his commanding display against United has reignited their pursuit, with Pochettino also familiar with his qualities from facing him while in charge of the United States.
Injury issues force defensive rethink
The Red Devils' urgent need for reinforcements stems from persistent fitness problems on the left side of defence. Shaw and Harry Amass are the club's only two recognised left-backs, and both have contracts expiring in 2027. Shaw has struggled with numerous injuries throughout his spell in Manchester and has missed the last eight matches with a muscle problem.
In his absence, former manager Michael Carrick mainly deployed Diogo Dalot out of position, while Pochettino opted to start Lisandro Martinez there. The report states that United are expected to enter the winter market for a natural left-back, making the South American an ideal fit for Pochettino's side.
Price tag complicates January deal
Despite Araujo's €80 million release clause, a fee of €50-60 million would reportedly be enough to prise him away from Sporting in January. However, the same source believes United are unlikely to invest that much on a full-back midway through the season. Whether Pochettino can persuade the Old Trafford hierarchy to sanction the outlay remains to be seen.

744c0d36a270a909.title: Man Utd news: Toni Jimenez the key to Senne Lammens bouncing back
744c0d36a270a909.text: Man Utd news: Toni Jimenez the key to Senne Lammens bouncing back
744c0d36a270a909.content:
- Published
After a first season at Manchester United that drew little but praise, goalkeeper Senne Lammens is under the microscope like never before.
A bad mistake that gifted Sporting their second goal on Wednesday, having earlier conceded a clumsy penalty, followed several other errors so far this season.
The 24-year-old Belgium international also made an error at the World Cup in the summer, spilling a shot that led to Spain's winning goal in the 88th minute of their quarter-final.
"I don't know [at what point Manchester United drop him]," legendary Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel told CBS Sports on Wednesday.
"Mauricio Pochettino has come in and brought his own staff. That means he's got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.
Toni Jimenez is Pochettino's long-time goalkeeping coach.
His arrival triggered the exit of Craig Mawson, who had been with United since 2019. Connor King is Jimenez's assistant but a relative newcomer himself, having joined from Burnley in 2026.
By its nature, goalkeeping at the highest level can be a mental challenge as well as a technical one. As Andre Onana discovered, flaws can quickly become major issues - and once the spotlight is shining, the attention is fierce.
Lammens has given the impression privately of being strong. He has seemed remarkably unaffected by his World Cup torment â his mistake against Spain came after he was introduced as a 71st-minute replacement for injured veteran Thibaut Courtois with the quarter-final delicately poised at 1-1. But only he knows the full picture.
Jimenez will be Pochettino's guide over what to do about the situation, although for now, Lammens' head coach is behind him.

0c5c0a1d4739e3fd.text: Scott McTominay has reportedly told Napoli he does not want to leave in January, stalling Manchester United's hopes of a reunion. The post Scott McTominay: Ex-Man United ace makes major decision on January Napoli exit appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
0c5c0a1d4739e3fd.content: Manchester United’s plans to immediately bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford appear to have hit a standstill. The midfield was at the centre of INEOS’ squad rebuild this summer, but their investment has yet to bear fruit. The Red Devils spent over €150 million on Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans, but the trio have hardly improved the team. Tielemans has been heavily involved, while Santos has been in and out of the starting XI. Baleba , meanwhile, remains sidelined with a hamstring injury after already missing the beginning of the campaign with an ankle issue. With United languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games, new manager Mauricio Pochettino could seek further reinforcements in midfield in 2027. Recent reports suggest that the Red Devils have been offered the chance to re-sign their former academy graduate McTominay next year. McTominay has been a hit in Serie A United made the surprise decision to allow McTominay to leave Old Trafford in the summer of 2024, and it has since been proven to be a poor move. The Scottish midfielder has hit a higher gear since moving to Napoli, helping them win Serie A in his debut campaign. McTominay has continued his upward trajectory with the Italian club and has already scored 33 goals and registered 10 assists in 93 appearances across competitions. For the record, the 29-year-old, who rose through the ranks at Old Trafford, has 29 goals and eight assists in 255 appearances for the Red Devils in his career. However, with the player’s contract set to expire in 2028 and a renewal yet to materialise, he has been linked with an exit from the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that the player would prefer to return to Old Trafford rather than join Chelsea, who are also in the race. It was suggested that McTominay’s camp held a meeting with Napoli sporting director Giovanni Manna to discuss his future. However, an update on the saga has now emerged that could complicate matters for United. caa107c9efbdebd0.text: Would any USMNT players really make Man United better if they followed Poch?
caa107c9efbdebd0.content:
If you follow the U.S. men's national team, here's a good sanity check: Imagine going back in time -- say, 15 years -- and telling your past self about the current situation.
"Yeah, so there's this guy who came up through the FC Dallas academy, moved to Schalke when he was a kid, started for them as an 18-year-old when they finished second in the Bundesliga behind Bayern Munich, and then moved to Juventus. He has played more Serie A matches for Juve than anyone else in the seven seasons since he joined the team."
"And he just did this news conference where he said, 'Guys from here being talked about going to Manchester United' was 'inevitable.' Oh, and this is important: he was saying that because Manchester United just poached the USMNT manager in the middle of the Premier League season."
Think about all the assumptions your 15-years-younger self would be making, whenever they had regained consciousness after suffering the double-whammy of learning that time travel exists and that the USMNT was one step below Manchester United in the global pecking order.
... Schalke are one of the best development clubs in the world, and Juventus are one of the best clubs in the world, so one of the best soccer players in the world plays for the USMNT now? And then, well, the USMNT coach is now coaching Manchester United, which might be the best club in the world. If my math is right, then there was a World Cup a couple of months ago -- in summer 2026 -- so ... wait ... did the U.S. just win the World Cup?
At this point, you'd disappear back to the present, allowing yourself to dream of a more hopeful future -- rather than explaining what happened to the Italian economy in the aughts, or what went down at Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson left, or what the USMNT's score against Belgium was.
But even with the relative changes in station over the past decade-plus, it's still a surreal thing to say today: Manchester United just hired away the USMNT manager. And, as Weston McKennie suggested, this always happens: Transfer rumors connect the manager of a new club with a smattering of players from the manager's old team.
All of which brings us here: Would any of Mauricio Pochettino's former players actually make Manchester United better? And even if they would, should United sign any of them?
What do Manchester United need?
There are three clear, interrelated issues with the way United's team plays and the way United's team was built.
The first: They're old. In fact, they're as old as Arsenal.
Now, you might be saying, "But Arsenal are the best team in the league!" But, well, Arsenal are the best team in the league, in part, because they're old. After multiple seasons of signing exclusively young players, they've spent the past two years adding established players who are late in their prime to the roster. They are trying to win as much as possible right now, and so their average age, weighted by minutes played, is 27.2 -- tied for third oldest in the league.
Although they finished third last season, United were clearly not a title contender coming into the Premier League season -- and, well, they're currently in 19th place. After Sunday's embarrassing loss to Liverpool, prediction markets now give them a 19% chance of being relegated. Once again, this team should be building for future title contention -- not contention to win right now.
Perhaps connected to that is the team's inability or unwillingness to press. The stats app Futi measures team's tendencies across a variety of stylistic markers. One of which is: "Stay compact to deny space or press to win the ball during the opponent's buildup?" Here's where United landed on that spectrum before Pochettino took over:
It's even worse when you look at what they do soon after possession is turned over: "Press aggressively to win back lost balls or fall back to recover defensive structure?"
While the league has moved toward a much more aggressive stance in these situations, United have gone in the opposite direction:
And it hasn't helped the defense in any way.
Only one team has conceded more expected goals than United this season:
We know that Pochettino wants his teams to press, and we know that pressing tends to favor younger, more energetic, and more mobile players. We also know that Pochettino's USMNT ticked both of these boxes at the World Cup: They were one of the more aggressive pressing teams in the tournament, and -- despite the presence of 39-year-old Tim Ream -- the ninth-youngest team in the field, weighted by minutes played.
Would any USMNT players make Man United better?
Given everything we've just gone over -- or, you know, what you might've watched Sunday -- the obvious place to start is in the back.
Man United goalkeeper Senne Lammens is young and roughly a league-average Premier League starter, and goalkeeper might be the weakest position in the USMNT pool. No Americans would be an upgrade here.
At the back, United's four most-used players this season are Diogo Dalot at right back, Luke Shaw at left back, and Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martínez at center back. Shaw is 31, Maguire 33, Martinez 28 -- and they're all out of contract at the end of this season. Plus, a large chunk of the defensive issues can probably be directed here.
These players are all on the older side, and none of them are above-average or even average ground-covering athletes. It's really hard for a team to press without rangy defenders covering behind the press, but none of these defenders have excelled in the more passive defensive structure. Otherwise, well, United wouldn't give up so many great chances.
Pochettino seemed aware of this, as he benched Maguire for the Liverpool match and played a back three with the theoretically more mobile Leny Yoro and Matthijs De Ligt alongside Martinez. We just needed eight minutes of game time at Anfield to see that this probably isn't the solution.

b22062e4908e5540.title: 'Man Utd being relegated would be the biggest shock in history... but it won't happen'
b22062e4908e5540.text: In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson previews a big weekend for Manchester United, before Arsenal take on Manchester City in a huge game live this Sunday.
b22062e4908e5540.content:
Man Utd being relegated would be the biggest shock in history, but it won't happen, says Paul Merson
Manchester United take on Brentford on Saturday with Mauricio Pochettino looking for his first win to take them out of the relegation zone; Arsenal then take on Man City, live on Sky Sports this Sunday, the reigning champions are aiming to go nine points clear of Enzo Maresca's side
Friday 27 November 2026 09:20, UK
In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson previews a big weekend for Manchester United, before Arsenal take on Manchester City in a huge game live this Sunday.
Mauricio Pochettino is looking for his first win as United boss as he bids to take them out of the relegation zone. However, Brentford visit Old Trafford on the back of their recent win over Everton, which took them into the top six.
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Then on Sunday, Arsenal host title rivals Man City. Enzo Maresca's side are already six points behind the reigning champions and have won just two out of their last seven matches in all competitions.
Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts ahead of a huge weekend in the Premier League...
'Brentford game is massive for Man Utd'
Manchester United are in trouble. 100 per cent. Of course they are. But I don't see them getting relegated, absolutely not.
I would be shocked and amazed, it would be the biggest shock in the history of anything. People will go: Mike Tyson got beat by Buster Douglas. But that was one punch. This is over 38 games.
Brentford is a massive football match for them. If they lost that game, I don't see them beating Newcastle if Matthias Jaissle's side get anywhere near the level they played against Arsenal in the second half.
Then by the time you're playing Coventry, you're more than a win away from getting out of trouble. As soon as that starts happening, that's when it starts getting worrying - when you need two weeks to get out of the bottom three, or four or five points away.
The next three weeks are massive for United. If they beat Brentford this week, that will settle them down.
But I look at the teams down there right now. Crystal Palace won't go to Old Trafford and win. Sunderland and Nottingham Forest won't. Fulham and Coventry won't. Hull won't. So that means to me that Man Utd are better than them.
That's why I don't see them getting relegated. When you look at it like that, there are a lot of worse teams than them.
Man Utd have bought too many 'four or nines' - that's what I call them. They're either 4/10 or 9/10. They're not in between. You can't do that at Man Utd. You have to be between a seven or an eight on a consistent basis. You can't be four one week and nine the next, it doesn't work.
The pace of the game is controlled by the other team, it's never controlled by Manchester United.
They have got no defenders. They've gone it horribly wrong, trying to build from front to back. But it's more than that, it's spine of the team.
They need a centre forward. They don't have a dictating midfield player who comes short and controls the game. The only way United can do that is if they sacrifice Fernandes going forward and playing him deeper, like a quarterback - and then hope you've got enough going forwards elsewhere.
I don't see anyone else in that United team who is capable of coming deep and playing the ball forward. Playing that pass on a consistent basis, making the right decisions.
'Man City have lost their fear factor'
Man City have got to go out and play for the fans, they're the ones who are paying their money. They're getting paid £300,000-a-week, the fans are the ones paying to watch them.
Man City are getting a little bit found out. I have always said, even when they were playing at their best, they give you chances. And you have to make those chances count.
It used to be: go to the Etihad, get your stomach's tickled, get out with a 3-0 defeat that you're more than happy with that, and go back on the coach - because they could win games by six or seven.
Then all of a sudden, they started winning games but they were also open at the same time. And now, teams don't fear them.
Teams know they will get chances if they have a go at them - and enough chances to win football matches, not just one or two chances.
If you are brave enough - like Fulham were by getting players in the opposition box - you can beat Man City.
This is the problem for them: they're too open and there's not that fear factor anymore. And I also don't think Erling Haaland gets the service he deserves.
You would like to think that City's players aren't being affected by the charges hanging over them, because no one knows what is going to happen. So you have to play until you know what's going to happen.
It's like life: no one's going to tell you what's going to happen tomorrow, so live today.
'If Arsenal beat Man City, the league could be over soon'
If Arsenal win this game, the league is finished. That would be nine points clear and this league could be over very, very quickly.
Arsenal were dominant in the first half against Newcastle and if it was a boxing match, then Newcastle would have thrown the towel in.
They came out the second half a bit lackadaisical and Newcastle were outstanding by playing on the front foot. But then Arsenal switched and decided they weren't going to lose.
And then they scored one of the best goals of the season. If the finish from Noni Madueke was good, it would be the goal of the season. But when you see the finish, it's not great and the goalkeeper should save it. If he whips it into the far corner, it's goal of the season.
I think we saw enough with Brighton last weekend against Hull. That's one of those games where you go: if you can't win it, don't lose it.
You feel sorry for Brighton, because Konstantinos Tzolakis was unreal. He should be playing for the New York Rangers this weekend. He was like an ice hockey goalkeep

Paul Merson menilai Manchester United tidak akan terdegradasi meski sedang menghadapi masa sulit.

Paul Merson menyampaikan pendapatnya dalam kolom terbaru Sky Sports menjelang akhir pekan pertandingan Liga Inggris.

Paul Merson: “Degradasi Man Utd akan menjadi kejutan terbesar dalam sejarah, tetapi itu tidak akan terjadi”, ujarnya kepada @SkySportsNews.
b22062e4908e5540.label: SPEKULASI
b22062e4908e5540.body_en:
Paul Merson believes Manchester United will not be relegated despite their ongoing struggles.

Paul Merson shared his thoughts in his latest Sky Sports column ahead of the Premier League weekend.

Paul Merson: “Man Utd being relegated would be the biggest shock in history, but it won't happen”, told @SkySportsNews.

38123b7dc70ce516.title: Music to Man United's ears as Nico Paz's stance on Old Trafford switch is confirmed - David Ornstein
38123b7dc70ce516.text: Man United have been handed a stunning boost in their bid to land Nico Paz as his stance on an Old Trafford switch emerges. The post Music to Man United’s ears as Nico Paz’s stance on Old Trafford switch is confirmed appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
38123b7dc70ce516.content: Nico Paz, Como attacking midfielder, stance on a potential transfer to Manchester United has come to light, as interest in the midfielder mounts. United interest Paz has emerged as one of the best attacking midfielders in Europe this season, amid his electric performances for Como both in Serie A and the Champions League. He has notched three goals and as many assists in 11 top-flight appearances this term. He boasts eight contributions in Europe, the joint-most alongside Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappé. United have been named as admirers of Paz alongside Chelsea, Arsenal, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Inter Milan. Madrid are also said to be keen on a reunion, although it recently emerged that Los Blancos have little appetite in triggering his €80m buy-back clause. Paz provided United with a first-hand demonstration of his capabilities, dismantling the Red Devils at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. He scored two goals as United suffered a 4-0 defeat. Paz latest According to Ornstein, Paz has been identified by United as a potential replacement for Bruno Fernandes . The Portuguese playmaker’s terms expire at the end of the campaign and an agreement has yet to be struck. Fernandes has already rejected two offers from the club. United retain the option of extending his stay by an additional 12 months. Ornstein reports: “Sources privy to the matter, talking anonymously to protect relationships, suggest Paz does not currently favour rejoining Madrid. 3d728524d0303de7.text: Manchester United retain an interest in Tottenham defender Micky van de Ven as they weigh defensive reinforcements under Mauricio Pochettino. The post Micky van de Ven: Man United retain interest in Tottenham Hotspur defender appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
3d728524d0303de7.content: It is clear as daylight that Manchester United are in urgent need of defensive reinforcements. The Red Devils conceded 58 goals in the Premier League in the 2023/24 season, prompting INEOS to invest heavily in the backline. In came Matthijs de Ligt , Noussair Mazraoui and Leny Yoro in the summer of 2024, while Ayden Heaven joined the squad six months later. The English giants ended the season in 15th place, conceding 54 times in the league. Senne Lammens was signed to upgrade the goalkeeping department last summer. United went on to secure third place in the league, thanks to a resurgent run under Michael Carrick, but conceded 50 times in the league. This season, the Red Devils have already let in 23 goals in 11 Premier League games, managing just one win, and now sit 19th in the table. Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Carrick in the dugout as the English giants look to immediately climb up the table. However, the backline remains a concern for the Argentine as well, given that the team has conceded six goals in the two games since his arrival. United need a new defender in January United already have three senior centre-backs in their squad – Harry Maguire , Lisandro Martinez and De Ligt – but none of them inspire much confidence. Maguire and Martinez are out of contract next summer, while De Ligt has struggled with fitness issues. Heaven, meanwhile, had a positive start to his Old Trafford spell, but has looked off colour this season. Yoro has shown promise but has lacked consistency and perhaps could do better with an experienced head alongside him. This is where targeting a Premier League-proven central defender in January makes sense. United were linked with Micky van de Ven in recent times but a previous report suggests that the Dutchman has no desire to leave Tottenham Hotspur in January . b5665eb8b872230d.content: Former Manchester United forward Alejandro Garnacho has plunged to a new all-time low, with Aston Villa making a major decision on his future ahead of the January transfer window. Since his £40m move from United to Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he has endured a torrid time, having departed after falling out with then-manager Ruben Amorim. He struggled both for form and consistency at Chelsea, managing just one Premier League goal all term. Chelsea decided they had seen enough and approved a move to Villa , initially on loan, with the deal set to become an obligation depending on appearances. But Garnacho has so far failed to impress Emery, both during games and on the training pitch. The Argentine has been omitted from the previous two Premier League squads and has accumulated only 34 minutes of top-flight football. He has made just seven appearances from the bench. According to The Athletic , Villa are actively working to offload the Carrington academy graduate in January. e08b692e17f5ba73.text: Manchester United need to establish a succession plan for Bruno Fernandes, with his contract set to expire next summer. The Portuguese magnifico will be free to negotiate with foreign clubs from January onwards, with […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
e08b692e17f5ba73.content: Manchester United need to establish a succession plan for Bruno Fernandes, with his contract set to expire next summer. According to The Athletic , United have Nico Paz on their list of potential options in case Bruno Fernandes leaves Old Trafford. The Portuguese magnifico will be free to negotiate with foreign clubs from January onwards, with his current contract set to expire in June 2027. Fernandes recently confirmed that discussions over a new deal have been put on hold, insisting that his priority is to help United return to winning ways. The Red Devils do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, but it remains to be seen whether both parties can agree on a longer-term arrangement. With Fernandes set to turn 33 next year, some believe this could be the right time for United to consider a succession plan and identify a long-term replacement. Nico Paz came through the academy ranks at Real Madrid but has taken his career to another level since joining Como, where he has flourished under Cesc Fabregas. He has bagged 25 goals and 23 assists in 91 games for the Italian outfit. The 22-year-old also has six goals to his name in 16 international games for Argentina. He made eight senior appearances for Real Madrid during the 2023-24 campaign, helping the Spanish giants win both La Liga and the UEFA Champions League titles. Although he is predominantly an attacking midfielder, the 22-year-old can also operate on the right flank. Widely regarded as one of the most exciting young prospects in world football, Paz has even been tipped to become a potential heir to Lionel Messi’s throne in Argentina. The Red Devils have failed to compete for the biggest honours over the last decade, but they still have the charm and global stature to remain one of the biggest clubs in football history.
