3203ffdbeb85328d.title: “Wouldn’t be here now”: Man United academy graduate opens up on traumatic addiction during playing career
3203ffdbeb85328d.text: Former Manchester United midfielder Darron Gibson details his sleeping pill addiction and how it nearly cost him his life. The post “Wouldn’t be here now”: Man United academy graduate Darron Gibson opens up on traumatic addiction during playing career appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
3203ffdbeb85328d.content: Former Manchester United player Darron Gibson has opened up on his terrible battle with drug addiction. Man United career Gibson came through the Man United academy and made his first-team debut during the 2005-2006 season. It wouldn’t be until the 2008-2009 season that he really started to feature regularly in the senior team. He played a total of 60 matches for the Red Devils, scoring 10 goals in all competitions. Gibson would leave United in 2012 and spent six seasons at Everton before finishing his career at Sunderland, Wigan Athletic and Salford City. The midfielder represented the Republic of Ireland 27 times, scoring one goal in total. Drug addiction The latter years of Gibson’s time at Everton were blighted by his sleeping pill addiction and he opened up on the topic to RTÉ Sport . Speaking on a podcast run by the Irish television station, Gibson told a story of how, after recovering from a knee injury in 2013, he became addicted to the drugs. He even claimed that he would take up to 14 a night. Gibson revealed just how close he was to death when his wife found him one day. His wife, who was also on the podcast, explained, “when the ambulance staff came in, he had blue lips, I thought he had gone. I was being treated for shock. I just thought: ‘At least he’s not struggling anymore.’ Next minute (sharp intake of breath), he’s back.” Gibson added, “ultimately, if that hadn’t have happened, I wouldn’t be here now. Probably. No, not easy. If that hadn’t of happened, I wouldn’t be here now. It was a difficult time. I went to hospital and done all the tests and everything came back clear. I woke up, and the two paramedics were standing there, and I was like ‘Why are you here?’ and walked past them into the kitchen and got a drink, came back in and sat down. I’d no idea what happened.” Reflecting on that dark time in his life, he stated, “looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn’t go to sleep? It’s ridiculous. But it’s where I was. It’s what I was doing.” Gibson also opened up on his then-club Everton’s treatment of the situation and he explained, “I think Everton thought they were looking after me by not punishing me, which I really appreciated at the time. And I don’t blame them for any of this, but I think if they’d punished me, maybe I would have changed. But I didn’t and kept going.” Darron Gibson Career stats Club Season Apps Minutes Goals Assists Yellow cards Red cards Salford City 2020/21 7 446 0 0 0 0 Salford City 2019/20 4 315 0 2 2 0 Wigan Athletic 2018/19 18 1020 0 0 1 1 Sunderland AFC 2017/18 18 1285 0 0 1 0 Sunderland AFC 2016/17 12 641 0 0 4 0 Everton FC 2016/17 1 24 0 0 0 0 Everton FC U21 2016/17 1 120 0 0 0 0 Everton FC 2015/16 11 554 0 1 3 0 Everton FC U21 2015/16 1 75 0 0 0 0 Everton FC 2014/15 14 712 0 1 0 0 Everton FC 2013/14 2 97 0 0 1 0 Everton FC 2012/13 26 2010 1 3 5 1 Everton FC U21 2012/13 1 63 0 0 0 0 Everton FC 2011/12 15 1282 1 1 5 0 Manchester United 2011/12 2 180 0 1 1 0 Page 1 of 2 1 2 Club Season Apps Minutes Goals Assists Yellow cards Red cards Manchester United U21 2011/12 3 225 0 0 0 0 Manchester United 2010/11 20 1322 2 4 5 0 Manchester United 2009/10 23 1125 5 2 4 0 Manchester United U21 2009/10 1 57 0 0 1 0 Manchester United 2008/09 14 907 3 1 1 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2007/08 24 1410 1 0 5 0 Manchester United 2007/08 0 0 0 0 0 0 Royal Antwerp FC 2006/07 33 2751 1 0 9 0 Manchester United 2005/06 1 15 0 0 0 0 Page 2 of 2 1 2 Source: Transfermarkt Featured image by Nathan Stirk via Getty Images online polls The post “Wouldn’t be here now”: Man United academy graduate Darron Gibson opens up on traumatic addiction during playing career appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .

cb6a045e04177bb1.title: Bruno Fernandes Doubtful for Man Utd vs Brentford After Missing Training
cb6a045e04177bb1.text: Bruno Fernandes Doubtful for Man Utd vs Brentford After Missing Training
cb6a045e04177bb1.content:
Why Bruno Fernandes is missing from Manchester United training before Brentford
Man Utd trained on Friday morning ahead of their game against Brentford at Old Trafford in the Premier League.
Bruno Fernandes missed Manchester United's training session at Carrington on Friday morning as a precaution because he felt under the weather.
Mauricio Pochettino agreed for the midfielder to be rested to protect him ahead of the game against Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.
The United captain has only missed six games since he signed for the club in January 2020. He is almost always available and is expected to be ready to start in United's important game against Brentford.
United streamed footage from their pre-Brentford training session online on Friday morning. United have a contractual open training deal with the Premier League, but club media are also allowed to film when Sky Sports are present.
Pochettino is due to speak at Carrington this afternoon and will confirm the latest team news.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
United drew 2-2 with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League in midweek, meaning Pochettino is looking for the first win since his appointment as head coach against Brentford on Saturday.
Pochettino wanted to talk about the positives when he spoke after the Sporting draw. “I'm so proud of the players. It was a tough game. I liked the team we played for 90 minutes, the personality, the character," he said.
“It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions. Today we showed how we want to play after just one week of working together."

596d88b036c94c00.content: Bruno Fernandes is currently a doubt to make the squad for Manchester United’s clash with Brentford tomorrow. According to ESPN’s Rob Dawson, the Red Devils skipper missed today’s training session through illness. United sweating on Bruno Fernandes’ availability (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) As a result, United will have to make a late decision over whether he can feature in any capacity. Fernandes looked to be somewhat back to his best last time out against his former club Sporting CP after scoring twice in the second half. He was named the Man of the Match at full-time, so he will be desperate to get back out on the pitch and continue doing his bit to try and turn things around. Should he be ruled out, he would join Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba on the sidelines. Luke Shaw has yet to make his return from injury, but did make the bench on Wednesday night. How the sides fare ahead of Saturday (Photo via ManUtd) Brentford, meanwhile, enter the gameweek placed sixth in the Premier League table. They are on the back of a 4-0 thrashing against Everton at home, while they’ve also already overturned Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur this term. United slumped to a 4-0 defeat at Anfield last Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge. However, plenty would argue that the result might have differed had Leny Yoro not been shown a straight red card in the opening eight minutes, which went on to dictate the match. The decision has since been overturned by the league, so Yoro will be able to play tomorrow, although them U-turning days later will mean very little to Pochettino, who was infuriated at the officiating post-match – and rightfully so. d1a778cbbda7d077.content: Manchester United are sweating over the fitness of Bruno Fernandes ahead of their Premier League clash tomorrow. The Red Devils are preparing to welcome Brentford to Old Trafford, but their preparations have been disrupted by a potential injury concern involving their influential skipper. The 32-year-old won the Man of the Match award after bagging a brace against Sporting CP on Wednesday evening. United head coach Mauricio Pochettino be desperate to have his captain available, particularly with United facing an important fixture in their battle to climb the table. Fernandes has netted four goals and two assists in 10 league games this season. The Red Devils currently sit 19th in the table and desperately need positive results to escape the relegation zone. Losing Fernandes would be a significant setback, as his creativity, vision and ability to influence games are difficult qualities to replace. Mason Mount and Youri Tielemans are among the natural alternatives, but neither offers quite the same creative influence as the Portuguese midfielder. The Portuguese magnifico has been remarkably reliable since arriving at Old Trafford in January 2020, rarely missing games for the Red Devils. Supporters will now be hoping their captain recovers in time to lead the side against the Bees. Fernandes has already turned down two contract proposals from the club, leaving uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at Old Trafford. His current deal expires in June 2027, meaning he will be free to negotiate with clubs outside England from January ahead of a potential summer move. ESPN claim that the influential Red Devils captain missed Friday morning's training session at Carrington as a precaution due to feeling unwell and will need to be assessed ahead of Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge at Old Trafford on Saturday.
A late decision is expected to be made on his availability for that game, with the report adding that Harry Maguire is expected to be in contention to face Brentford after reporting an unspecified injury in the aftermath of Wednesday night's chaotic 2-2 draw against Sporting in the Champions League.
Pochettino will be expected to give an update on both players when he addresses the media at Carrington in his pre-Brentford press conference at 1:30pm GMT on Friday afternoon.

0fb39e22006b8ea6.title: Man United make decisive call on January swoop for Folarin Balogun - report
0fb39e22006b8ea6.text: Manchester United will not pursue Monaco striker Folarin Balogun in January as INEOS consider alternatives to support Benjamin Šeško. The post Man United make decisive call on January swoop for Folarin Balogun appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
0fb39e22006b8ea6.content: A striker signing is at the top of Manchester United’s agenda in January. In fact, an interesting claim emerged this week that Mauricio Pochettino favoured a striker over a left-back. However, while INEOS are expected to land an out-and-out striker to cover Benjamin Šeško , who they will go for remains a mystery. Hard-to-pin-down options Several options have been mooted, but none looks like a straightforward deal. Take Ivan Toney: there is a worry that United will not be able to afford his wages, let alone pull off a deal to bring him back to the Premier League. Meanwhile, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is reportedly set to sign a new deal with Leeds. Beyond those two, Folarin Balogun has also been touted. However, the ex-Arsenal man is unlikely to join United in January, as per The Athletic. Folarin Balogun: INEOS make their transfer decision Past reports suggested the Monaco star would jump at the chance to reunite with his former national team boss, Pochettino, at Old Trafford. Yet INEOS are not going to make that reunion happen. The Athletic explain: “Folarin Balogun is available from Monaco during the winter window, but United are not expected to be in for him. “Pochettino had an excellent experience of Balogun while in charge of the U.S. — he was a pivotal focal point of his team at the World Cup — and sources in France say Monaco are open to doing a deal, which would alert teams across Europe. United, however, are looking elsewhere for now.” Balogun, who never really got the chance to prove his worth in the Premier League at Arsenal, making only two appearances, must be itching to return and prove himself. Yet it seems he will not do so at United. As a result, the USMNT star’s hopes of a winter Premier League return may rest on Everton renewing their interest. Which striker will Manchester United go for? That said, if it is not Calvert-Lewin, Balogun or Toney, who United turn to remains a mystery. Crucially, though, they would not go wrong by pursuing Championship top scorer Will Lankshear . The 21-year-old, who has scored 14 goals in 15 Championship games this season, is said to be on the Red Devils’ transfer wishlist. bedadf7596ad12eb.title: Manchester United suffer Bruno Fernandes injury scare ahead of Brentford clash
bedadf7596ad12eb.text: Manchester United suffer Bruno Fernandes injury scare ahead of Brentford clash
bedadf7596ad12eb.content:
United have confirmed that their influential captain missed Friday morning’s training session at Carrington as a precaution due to feeling unwell and will need to be assessed ahead of Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge at Old Trafford on Saturday.
A late decision is expected to be made on his availability for that game, with ESPN reporting that Harry Maguire is expected to be in contention to face Brentford after reporting an unspecified injury in the aftermath of Wednesday night’s chaotic 2-2 draw against Sporting in the Champions League.
Pochettino will be expected to give an update on both players when he addresses the media at Carrington in his pre-Brentford press conference at 1:30pm GMT on Friday afternoon.
“Manchester United have trained in front of the cameras in the Carrington rain on Friday morning,” United said via their official media channels.
“Mauricio Pochettino's side are preparing for Saturday's 15:00 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford, our head coach's first home game in charge.
“Bruno Fernandes was absent from the session, after scoring both goals in the 2-2 draw against his former club Sporting in the UEFA Champions League in midweek.
“The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”
The absence of Fernandes would be a significant blow for Pochettino as he seeks to achieve his first win as United boss at the third attempt, having overseen a 4-0 drubbing by arch-rivals Liverpool in his opening match at the helm at Anfield last weekend.
Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes to set the tone for that one-sided contest on Merseyside, but has since seen his red card for a last-man challenge on Alexander Isak overturned by a Football Association (FA) regulatory commission following a successful appeal in a ruling that has caused plenty of controversy.

6c5996ef70a419be.title: Rhys Bennett helps launch Man Utd suicide prevention and mental health initiative
6c5996ef70a419be.text: Rhys Bennett helps launch Man Utd suicide prevention and mental health initiative
6c5996ef70a419be.content:
- Published
Content warning: This article contains discussion around suicide and mental health.
Fleetwood and former Manchester United defender Rhys Bennett has spoken about his father's suicide at a support session at Salford Lads Club to help launch an initiative the Old Trafford club are starting at Saturday's game against Brentford.
United are working with the Premier League and Salford-based support group Talk About It Mate to launch The Check-In, a new matchday mental health and suicide prevention initiative.
The pop-up centre, close to the 3G pitches in front of the Sir Alex Ferguson Stand, will be in operation at 10 home league matches this season. United say it will offer "a safe and welcoming space where supporters can chat with trained counsellors and volunteers and find out more about further support".
Bennett's dad, David, took his own life in October 2025. The defender spoke movingly about the personal impact to the BBC among others last December.
However, he found speaking within a two-hour Talk About It Mate session to be "one of the most powerful things I've ever done".
"I play football for a living and it can be hard performing every day in a high-pressure environment, but I was a bit nervous coming here for the first time," he added.
"Within five minutes, you realise there's no judgement and you can talk about how you're really feeling.
"I'm coming up to a year since my dad's passing. The more I talk about it and let my emotions out, it makes me feel stronger in day-to-day life.
"The best thing was how open everyone was and how open I could be myself. There wasn't any point where I felt I couldn't share something I was feeling. Everything came from the heart. It was authentic and powerful.
"I think it would have helped dad massively - people sharing the same experiences. People sitting in a circle all going through different things in a judgement-free zone. For him, that would have been really important."
6c5996ef70a419be.body:
Manchester United meluncurkan inisiatif kesehatan mental dan pencegahan bunuh diri bersama Rhys Bennett.

Klub bekerja sama dengan Premier League dan Talk About It Mate untuk menghadirkan pusat layanan The Check-In di Old Trafford.

bfca1a514fb4e4c9.title: 'No chance!' - Alvaro Arbeloa sends defiant transfer message to Man Utd over Fulham captain Calvin Bassey
bfca1a514fb4e4c9.text: 'No chance!' - Alvaro Arbeloa sends defiant transfer message to Man Utd over Fulham captain Calvin Bassey
bfca1a514fb4e4c9.content:
Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has firmly shut down speculation linking defender Calvin Bassey with a January move to Manchester United. Speaking ahead of his side's meeting with Bournemouth, the coach delivered a blunt verdict on the Nigeria international's future and revealed crucial behind-the-scenes plans at the club.
Arbeloa rejects January transfer talk
Arbeloa has moved swiftly to protect one of his most important players as the winter transfer window approaches. Growing rumours have linked 26-year-old Bassey with a mid-season departure from Fulham.
United are reportedly among a number of clubs monitoring the Nigeria star ahead of January. Their interest reflects the defender's impressive form this campaign. However, Fulham have no intention of letting a key figure leave midway through the season. Arbeloa addressed the mounting speculation directly during his press conference before facing Bournemouth.
Bassey is not for sale
Arbeloa left zero room for doubt when pressed on whether the Red Devils or any other suitors could prise Bassey away this winter. The Fulham boss stressed the defender's vital leadership role within the squad.
"I'm so happy with Calvin," Arbeloa told reporters at his pre-Bournemouth press conference. "Obviously, he's not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. I think he's happy here, he's one of our captains, he's one of our leaders."
New contract talks already underway
Rather than viewing the widespread transfer interest as a distraction, Arbeloa sees it as clear proof of Bassey's high level of performance. The coach believes the attention is a natural consequence of the defender's strong displays on the pitch. To ward off rival clubs permanently, Fulham are already taking proactive steps behind the scenes to tie the 26-year-old down to fresh terms.
"You can see how he's playing and, for me, it's normal that so many clubs are interested in him," Arbeloa explained. "It is good for him, good for us because that means he is performing really, really well, but it's very important for me as a coach and a club and we are working on a new contract and I hope he can sign as soon as possible."
Focus shifts to Bournemouth and renewal
Fulham's immediate priority now returns to the pitch, with Arbeloa preparing his squad for their upcoming fixture against Bournemouth. Bassey remains central to the manager's plans as one of the team's established leaders.
Away from matchday preparations, club officials will continue working to finalise the defender's new deal as swiftly as possible. Securing his signature would provide a major boost for Arbeloa and effectively end the uncertainty surrounding his future.

The post Marcus Rashford: Man United ace’s future in doubt following major Fenerbahce decision appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
0bccdeae9b9d36b5.content: Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford will be hoping that new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival helps turn his career around at Old Trafford. However, all signs indicate that his time at the Theatre of Dreams may be coming to an end. The Argentine took charge of the Red Devils last week in a bid to get the faltering giants back to their heyday. Pochettino’s immediate assignment, however, will be getting his team out of troubled waters. United’s position in the Premier League after 11 games is a clear indication of their woeful form this season. The Red Devils are 19th in the table, with just one win and have scored just 14 goals so far. On paper, the presence of a potent goalscorer like Rashford – who scored 14 goals and registered 15 assists on loan to Barcelona last season – should have been a godsend for the English giants. Unfortunately, the reality has been entirely different. Rashford fails to get going this season Marcus Rashford was heavily linked with an exit from Old Trafford this summer after returning from his loan spell with the Catalans. A permanent return to Camp Nou was also mooted but the player ended up staying. With United also looking for a new left-forward this summer, it was believed to be a win-win situation for all parties involved. Michael Carrick, who was in charge at the Theatre of Dreams during that time, was expected to get the 29-year-old back to his best having previously worked together during former manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s reign. Unfortunately, things failed to click, with Rashford struggling to replicate his previous form. The Englishman started the season as the preferred choice for the left forward role but has yet to register a goal or an assist. He is currently sidelined with a hip injury, and a recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that INEOS are already planning to let him go in January. A fresh update has now arrived that will work to United’s benefit. f43d5c6b3c19f877.title: Pochettino’s Fernandes injury update as four Man Utd players are ruled out
f43d5c6b3c19f877.text: Mauricio Pochettino has provided an injury update on Bruno Fernandes ahead of Manchester United’s Premier League clash with Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. Manchester ...
f43d5c6b3c19f877.content:
Manchester United will be looking to claim their first win under Mauricio Pochettino when they host Brentford at Old Trafford in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.
The 54-year-old head coach will take charge of his first home game this weekend, on the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool last weekend and a 2-2 draw with Sporting CP in the Champions League in midweek.
But there were signs of life for the team during that game in Lisbon, with the team feeling hugely aggrieved by refereeing decisions, and the hope is now that they can finally kick on in front of their own fans.
The team have been boosted by the return of Leny Yoro and Matheus Cunha to the side, with Yoro's red card against Liverpool overturned on appeal, while the Brazilian missed the midweek draw after being sent off against Roma earlier this month. Youri Tielemans will be available to play despite his red card against Sporting, with the ban only valid for Champions League games.
Now Pochettino has shared an injury update ahead of the game during his pre-match press conference, where he has revealed that he will be without a number of first-team stars.
Bruno Fernandes
The Reds captain played a starring role in midweek with two goals against his former club, but GIVEMESPORT sources reported earlier on Friday that he missed training on Friday as a precaution due to feeling unwell.
The club is hopeful that he will be well enough to start in the game, with Pochettino sharing an update on his condition:
"We don't know. He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game, and today he couldn't be apart of the training session. We'll see today and tomorrow when he wakes up if he will be available, but we won't take any risks.
"We'll monitor the situation, but no decision has been made yet."
AVAILABLE
Harry Maguire
Maguire was left out of the starting lineup against Liverpool but came in after Leny Yoro's red card, while he then completed 90 minutes against Sporting.
But GIVEMESPORT sources understand that he suffered a knock in that game and is considered a doubt for the game, although the club remains confident he will be available.
AVAILABLE
Luke Shaw
Left-back Shaw has not featured for Man Utd since going off in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham back in October due to a hamstring injury, but he was on the bench for the first time against Sporting.
Although he was an unused substitute in the game, he is closing in on a return, and will be hopeful of taking his place in the starting lineup back under former manager Pochettino.
AVAILABLE
Marcus Rashford
Rashford, who Man Utd are reportedly ready to sell for the 'right price', has been dealing with a hip and groin issue since the World Cup, and hasn't featured for the club since the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in October.
The England international is still not back in training as he looks to make a return, and with Pochettino desperate to work with the electric forward, this game will still come too soon for him.
"Marcus is back on the grass and starting to feel much better.
"I'm looking forward to working with all the players, the ones that are injured I hope they can recover as soon as possible."
RULED OUT
Carlos Baleba
The £70m summer signing from Brighton looked sharp in his first games in the red shirt following his recovery from an ankle problem, but a fresh hamstring injury has seen him ruled out for several weeks.
The Cameroon international is unlikely to return any time soon, although the club are looking at the festive period for a potential comeback.
"Baleba was hurt against Roma, and the medical staff have said 10-12 weeks."
RULED OUT
Longer Term Injuries
Benjamin Sesko remains sidelined until the new year with a shin issue which has persisted since last season, and United are understood to be looking at potential striker options for January as a result.
Midfielder Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee injury during the World Cup in the summer, and is not expected to return until right at the end of the campaign, if at all, following surgery.

6bdc70563cbf032c.title: David Ornstein discloses what Man Utd can do to significantly boost their chances of signing Nico Paz in 2027

Ornstein confirms United’s Paz interest As if Mauricio Pochettino needed any more motivation to get the club as […] The post David Ornstein discloses what Man Utd can do to significantly boost their chances of signing Nico Paz in 2027 appeared first on utdreport .
6bdc70563cbf032c.content: David Ornstein has verified that Manchester United are among Nico Paz’s suitors heading into 2027. However, there is a chance that United might not be his first-choice suitor, and Champions League qualification is likely to be essential. Ornstein confirms United’s Paz interest (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) As if Mauricio Pochettino needed any more motivation to get the club as far up the table as possible and in contention for the UCL spots, Paz’s availability will now add to it . The 22-year-old starlet is said to be uninterested in returning to Real Madrid, as they hold a £67 million buy-back clause from Como. Game time would be incredibly hard to come by at the Santiago Bernabeu given Los Blancos’ stacked attacking depth, so you can understand Paz favouring a move where he is going to be one of the main men and a nailed-on starter. He could well become that at Old Trafford, though United’s prospective pursuit may hinge on whether Bruno Fernandes leaves. Could Paz be Fernandes’ long-term successor in M16? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Fernandes is out of contract in June 2027 , but the board has the option of triggering a 12-month extension. From fans’ perspective, INEOS should be pushing to bring in Paz irrespective of whether the skipper stays or leaves. The Argentine international shares the same representatives as Pochettino, which could work in United’s favour somehow, while the idea of joining the 20-time champions of England does hold some appeal to him. Paz is overseeing an absolutely outstanding campaign with the Italian outfit, having returned six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions. In Europe alone, he has scored three times and assisted five goals in just five matches and 408 minutes of action. Three of those contributions came against United on October 21, when he claimed the Man of the Match award.

Man Utd suffer major blow as Mauricio Pochettino gives Bruno Fernandes update for Brentford
Manchester United host Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon at Old Trafford - and they might be without captain Bruno Fernandes due to illness
Manchester United could be without Bruno Fernandes against Brentford on Saturday after Mauricio Pochettino confirmed why he missed training on Friday.
Fernandes was missing from United's final training session on Friday morning at Carrington. The United captain scored both of their goals in the chaotic 2-2 draw against Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday but is now a major doubt to face Brentford.
"We don't know, he been affected by a virus from Portugal," Pochettino said in his pre-match press conference when asked if Fernandes was available. "He finished the game with a little bit of a problem and today he cannot be a part of the training session.
"We'll see. We're going to assess during the day and tomorrow. He'll wake up and see. We're not going to take any risks because we know that when these types of situations happen you don't feel your best. We're going to pay attention but still we haven't decided."

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to shoot on goal and appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch.
Baleba has not featured since with Michael Carrick explaining in the days that followed: ‘We don’t know exactly, but it’ll be a number of weeks.
‘It’s definitely not this week and it won’t be any time over the international break. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.’

Speaking at his press conference on Friday, Pochettino said: "We don't know [if he'll be available tomorrow], he's affected from Portugal.
"He finished the game with a little problem. He wasn't part of training today."
The doubts over Fernandes's fitness come as the club decide to trigger the option to extend his contract by one year.
The Athletic report that the captain's contract will now run until 2028, but there remains a possibility of a summer exit at the end of the current season.
Man Utd will definitely be without Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba, who continue to recover from injuries, though Luke Shaw returned to the squad against Sporting after a month-and-a-half absence.
Providing an update on the injured pair, Pochettino said: "Baleba was injured against Roma, medical people were talking about 10-12 weeks. Marcus is on the field, starting to feel much better.

Pochettino is eager to have his full squad available, adding: "I am looking forward to working with all the players, the players that are injured. I hope that they can recover as soon as possible.
"I think to have the full squad fit and available to be selected, that is the most important thing for every single coaching staff."
Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte remain longer-term absentees, with Sesko expected to be out until at least the end of January and Ugarte continuing his recovery from a serious knee injury.
Leny Yoro is available after United successfully appealed his red card against Liverpool, overturning the suspension. Youri Tielemans' second yellow card against Sporting does not affect his availability for Premier League matches.

Manchester United have triggered their option to extend captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract for another year to keep him at Old Trafford to 2028.
The 32-year-old was in the last year of his deal, but United had built in the chance to add a further 12 months, which they have now done.
United chief executive Omar Berrada said last week that the club was holding talks to give Fernandes a new deal but the midfielder promptly said he had put them on hold to concentrate on getting results.
“The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said then.
Fernandes has attracted interest in the past from Saudi Pro-League clubs and from Galatasaray but has chosen to stay at United.
If United had not taken up the option, Fernandes could have discussed a summer move to a foreign club from 1 January.
A 2020 signing from Sporting CP, he has scored 115 goals in 343 games for United, including the first two goals of new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s reign in a 2-2 draw with his former club on Wednesday.
However, he missed training on Friday due to a virus and is a doubt for Saturday’s match against Brentford.
United have three other senior players out of contract next summer, in Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez, though they also have an option to extend the Argentinian’s deal for a further year.

0678af1ef511d484.title: Man United make 'major' decision on Bruno Fernandes' future at Old Trafford amid exit talk
0678af1ef511d484.text: Man United make 'major' decision on Bruno Fernandes' future at Old Trafford amid exit talk
0678af1ef511d484.content:
Manchester United have exercised the option in Bruno Fernandes' contract, Fabrizio Romano reported on Friday. The Portuguese midfielder is now under contract at Old Trafford until mid-2028. United have ensured their 32-year-old captain cannot leave on a free transfer, but his longer-term future remains far from certain.
Fernandes' contract ran until the summer of 2027 and included an option for another season. Manchester United had until the end of December to exercise it and have now done so.
According to Romano, financial considerations drove the decision. United want to prevent Fernandes from leaving on a free transfer next summer if they cannot agree a new contract.
Manchester United have offered the Portuguese midfielder a longer-term deal. Talks have been on hold since October, however, according to the Italian transfer journalist.
"Manchester United have offered him a new contract. This isn't about exercising the option, but about a completely new contract at the club," Romano said on his YouTube channel. "Bruno Fernandes' response was: 'Let's wait.' There is no agreement yet."
Related Topics
Exercising the option does not rule out a summer departure. Fernandes' current contract contains a release clause worth around €65 million that will come into effect next summer, according to Romano.
The coming months will show whether Manchester United can convince Fernandes to stay at Old Trafford for longer. The plans the club's leadership presents to him will play an important role, according to Romano.
"Manchester United have protected themselves with this move today. But this is mainly about the new contract, not extending his current deal," the Italian transfer journalist stressed.
Fernandes' departure could also have major consequences for Manchester United's transfer plans. United are closely monitoring developments surrounding Como star Nico Paz. The Argentine midfielder is represented by the same management agency as Man United manager Mauricio Pochettino.
"If Bruno leaves, that could open the door for new players, such as Nico Paz or other creative players, because Manchester United will need someone in that position," Romano said. For now, there has been little activity surrounding Fernandes ahead of the winter transfer window.

Fabrizio Romano menyampaikan informasi ini melalui saluran YouTube miliknya terkait masa depan Bruno Fernandes.

Fabrizio Romano: “Manchester United telah menawarinya kontrak baru. Ini bukan soal mengaktifkan opsi, melainkan tentang kontrak yang sepenuhnya baru di klub”. “Respons Bruno Fernandes adalah: 'Mari kita tunggu.' Belum ada kesepakatan”, ujarnya kepada YouTube. “Manchester United telah melindungi diri mereka dengan langkah hari ini. Namun, ini terutama mengenai kontrak baru, bukan memperpanjang kontrak saat ini”. “Jika Bruno pergi, itu bisa membuka pintu bagi pemain baru, seperti Nico Paz atau pemain kreatif lainnya, karena Manchester United akan membutuhkan seseorang di posisi tersebut”.

4d3adf44bf228568.title: Man Utd trigger one-year extension for Bruno Fernandes days after captain admitted contract talks had stalled
4d3adf44bf228568.text: Man Utd trigger one-year extension for Bruno Fernandes days after captain admitted contract talks had stalled
4d3adf44bf228568.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have triggered their one-year option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.
The Old Trafford skipper, 32, was into his final year but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.
Triggering the club option is logical from United’s perspective, as clubs could have approached Fernandes over a pre-contract agreement after January 1.
Fernandes last signed terms in 2024 and is now tied down until June 2028, but the parties are expected to resume new contract talks in the months ahead.
While it does not prevent a 2027 departure, it guarantees United can demand a transfer fee for their best player.
It follows the Portugal international confirming talks over fresh terms had paused, as both parties chose to focus on improving on-field results.
United sit 19th in the Prem table after five league defeats from 11 and Fernandes missed training on Friday with a virus ahead of Brentford’s visit on Saturday.
Fernandes remains the subject of interest from Europe and Saudi Arabia, while United have a list of potential recruits should he go.
SunSport revealed that United were interested in Como attacking midfielder Nico Paz, who scored twice against the Red Devils in the Serie A side’s 4-1 win last month.
After Casemiro left, Marcus Rashford became United’s highest paid player, earning around £325,000-per-week.
But Fernandes has insisted that money is not the reason he turned down a new deal, even as United look to cut their wage bill.
The reigning Prem player of the year also made clear he would not stand in the club’s way if they decided his future lay elsewhere.
United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a £100m deal.
Fernandes insisted his ambitions at United have not changed, despite the club’s struggles, and remains determined to bring major honours back to Old Trafford.
He dismissed suggestions of a breakdown in his relationship with former United boss Michael Carrick after his comments questioning the tactics after Como.
Fernandes’ future has been shrouded in uncertainty since he was an unused sub in the 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth.
He was reinstated before Carrick’s sacking and has retained the armband under successor Mauricio Pochettino.
Fernandes scored twice in Wednesday’s 2-2 draw away to Sporting CP as he pushes to regain his form.
Last season he broke the Prem’s assists record with 21 and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after a brilliant campaign as United finished third.
Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.

fbdcf5783c1f316e.title: 'I'm not nice' - Mauricio Pochettino warns his Manchester United players
fbdcf5783c1f316e.text: Mauricio Pochettino sent a warning to his Man Utd players during his press conference on Friday.
fbdcf5783c1f316e.content:
'I'm not nice' - Mauricio Pochettino warns his Manchester United players
Mauricio Pochettino sent a warning to his Man Utd players during his press conference on Friday.
Mauricio Pochettino said he had seen positives in his first two games in charge of Manchester United, but he also warned his players that he is "not nice."
Pochettino lost his first game against Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, and that result was followed by a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night.
The 54-year-old has had one day at Carrington to prepare for Brentford, as the team flew back to Manchester on Thursday evening after doing a recovery session in Portugal, and it was put to Pochettino during his press conference that he's overseen a hectic first eight days at United.
In response to that question, Pochettino said he had seen positives from his players but warned that he is "not nice."
The response from Pochettino could potentially be interpreted as a response to Jamie Redknapp, who said he thought the United boss had "gone too nice" in an episode of The Overlap Daily earlier this week.
Pochettino began his rant by saying: "Always happens. I think the problem is that we forgot that things happened in the past, no? We always live in the present and the future, no? But we are always in the future because the present is only a moment that always disappears quickly.
"Yes, it always happens. When this type of situation happens, the circumstance always feels like, oh, things always happen against us, and it's like, no, but it's not true. That is not true.
"That is a little bit the rhetoric of always. No, this type of thing happens. We had a big mistake from the referee against Liverpool, something happened. Not only did it happen now with us, it can happen in the future, it happen in the past. And the mistake also in Wednesday was the same."
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
He continued: "But we need to accept that. What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Being strong, believe, keep going. I think too many positive things in the two games.
"Maybe we didn't win, okay, we didn't win, but for sure I think we are building, you know, our journey and for sure in the way that now that we are, only we can talk from the last seven, eight days, we found a group of players, a group of staff, and everyone that want to help and want to be there, you know, to help the team to perform and win games.
"That is why I cannot change my vision, I cannot say something that is not true. I cannot judge the past because who I am to judge the past? Only when I was in Cincinnati or I was in Atlanta, I say, no, we should change that or we should do this or do that. Because I was outside.
"I need to shut my mouth and say nothing and start from now when I accept the invitation to come to Manchester United and start to work in this circumstance, shut my mouth and work 12 hours every day, you know, and try to recover the feelings, the emotions, and build our mentality again and really believe in what we are going to do and this group of players deserve that and pushing. And not misunderstand my words.
"Because sometime we are so confusing two words that means sometime everyone says, oh, maybe it's a similitude or similar, you know. Nice and good. I am not nice. I am not nice.
"We have to be good. There is a difference. I am not nice. I am trying to be good. Then be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something, you know, to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything."
Pochettino was asked about his man management strategy and the importance of 'not being nice'.
"I don't know. It's maybe a lot of expertise that have, you know, different things," he said.
"We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put in track again that team, that club, and those players. And we really believe. We are, we really believe that we can do it. It's only a matter of time."

Mauricio Pochettino reveals whether he has spoken to Manchester United legend Sir Alex Ferguson
Mauricio Pochettino first dined with legendary former Man United manager Sir Alex Ferguson over 10 years ago.
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino hasn't had the opportunity to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson since his appointment earlier this month.
Pochettino oversaw his final two games with the United States' national team after accepting the United job, meaning he only had three-and-a-half days at Carrington to prepare for his first game against Liverpool.
Three days later, United played Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, and they have another game against Brentford on Saturday, meaning Pochettino's full attention has been on working with his new players.
Pochettino met Ferguson for dinner in 2016 and the two have kept in contact, but Pochettino hasn't spoken to him since taking the United job.
"No, I didn't have the opportunity," he said when asked if he'd spoken to Ferguson.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
"I send all my admiration and love to him and I promise I will send a text. Look, it's not to say nothing. You ask me... It's 12 hours, 13, 14 hours spent here in the training ground.
"And I didn't have time. I need to talk with a lot of good friends that I have in Manchester, but I prefer that situation to say sorry because I cannot answer the message; I cannot send the message.
"You know, we are so fully focused on trying to provide everything, you know, to start to improve our performance and be close to winning."
Ferguson remains a frequent attendee at United fixtures and has given his backing to every Reds manager since stepping down in 2013.

beca14a57aa96047.title: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
beca14a57aa96047.text: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
beca14a57aa96047.content:
Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’s contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.
Fernandes’s deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers.
Immediate focus is on improving results, with United second-bottom of the Premier League with one win and also 19th in the Champions League standings. Fernandes is a doubt for Pochettino’s first home game in charge of United, against Brentford on Saturday, after missing training on Friday because of a virus.
Pochettino lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first league game and followed that with a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League. He is confident of transforming the club and made clear he would not take a softly-softly approach.
“I am not nice,” he said. “I am trying to be good. But be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put the team, the club, the players on track again. And we really believe, we really believe that we can do it. It’s only a matter of time.”
If United beat Brentford it would be a first domestic win in 90 days. The performance against Sporting gave a vision of Pochettino’s plan to be aggressive and press high. The team have endured misfortune at the start of Pochettino’s tenure, having Leny Yoro wrongly sent off at Liverpool, according to a Football Association commission which rescinded the defender’s suspension, and two goals disallowed in Portugal.
“We need to accept that,” Pochettino said. “What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Be strong, believe, keep going. I can think of many positive things in the two games. Maybe we didn’t win but for sure I think we are building our journey and for sure in the last seven, eight days we found a group of players, a group of staff, that want to help and want to be there, to help the team to perform and win games.”
Pochettino will be without the midfielder Carlos Baleba until late January but Marcus Rashford returned to individual training on Friday.

270790f889cdda1b.content: Manchester United have taken a major decision regarding the future of captain Bruno Fernandes. According to renowned journalist David Ornstein , Man United have activated an option to extend the contract of captain Bruno Fernandes. The 32-year-old was in the final year of current contract at Old Trafford, with his deal set to expire at the end of June 2027. He would have been free to talk to foreign clubs January onwards for a potential summer move next year. The Red Devils have triggered the one-year extension clause, giving themselves the chance to offer him a new deal later this season. They also now have the power to demand a transfer fee if any club shows interest in signing him next summer. United have already presented Fernandes with two contract proposals over the past six months, but the midfielder has yet to put pen to paper. The midfielder confirmed recently that the no negotiations are currently place between the two parties as they want to bring the stability to Old Trafford first. Saudi Arabia outfits offered outrageous wages to Fernandes over the last 24 months but he chose to stay at United. Much will depend on the club’s progress under manager Mauricio Pochettino and their ability to demonstrate genuine ambition. United have already added Como star Nico Paz to their transfer shortlist as a potential replacement for Fernandes. a11b2166f8c62a82.title: Man United handed unexpected route to finally land Jarrad Branthwaite in 2027
a11b2166f8c62a82.text: Manchester United remain keen on Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, whose contract reportedly includes a summer exit clause. The post Man United handed unexpected route to finally land Jarrad Branthwaite in 2027 appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
a11b2166f8c62a82.content: A defensive rebuild is at the top of Manchester United’s agenda come 2027. United’s defensive frailties have been their major undoing this season. Wednesday’s draw with Sporting CP was a case in point, as defensive mistakes denied them the win. While Mauricio Pochettino will look to improve the Red Devils’ defensive play through his coaching, he could also use better defensive options. Meanwhile, INEOS are already looking at reinforcements, and The Athletic have now reported a clear opportunity to sign long-term defensive target Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite . Branthwaite: a dream Manchester United defensive target Back in 2024, the Red Devils were keen on adding the Everton star to their ranks, but the Toffees stood firm and knocked back two United bids. Seeing that the Merseyside outfit did not want to do business, INEOS therefore opted to pursue alternatives, signing Matthijs de Ligt from Bayern Munich. Two years on, however, United still hold an interest in Branthwaite, whose stock has continued to rise over the past two seasons. INEOS would jump at the chance to sign him and have him spearhead their defensive rebuild, and an opportunity seems to have presented itself to land the Everton star. Branthwaite has an exit clause The Athletic are reporting: “Manchester United are still keen on Jarrad Branthwaite, sources say, and people with knowledge of the situation say his contract does contain a timed exit clause at a significant fee, but it is not active in January. It can only be activated in summer but expires at a certain date. “If a club does make an approach, Everton are believed to want the terms met in full and up front, whereas United, in any deal, are likely to try to agree payments in instalments.” Ultimately, then, if United want Branthwaite and wish to avoid back-and-forth negotiations or a bidding war, they would be best advised to find out when his exit clause becomes active. While at it, they should also be ready to break the bank for him and make him their marquee 2027 signing, the face of their defensive rebuild. J. 440399eeaabab8e5.title: Watford, the Pozzos and the hottest managerial seat in the game
440399eeaabab8e5.text: In today’s Football Daily: good luck Edward Iordanescu
440399eeaabab8e5.content: HELLO, GOODBYE A few weeks ago, Alessio Dionisi was forced to deny the “fake news” he had joined Sean Dyche, Gianfranco Zola, Beppe Sannino, Óscar García, Billy McKinlay, Slavisa Jokanovic, Quique Sánchez Flores (twice), Walter Mazzarri, Marco Silva, Javi Gracia (twice), Nigel Pearson, Vladimir Ivic, Xisco Muñoz, Claudio Ranieri, Roy Hodgson, Rob Edwards, Slaven Bilic, Chris Wilder, Valérien Ismael, Tom Cleverley, Paulo Pezzolano and Edward Still in being sacked by the Pozzo family since 2012. There was no denial on Sunday, when the axe inevitably fell on the head coach following a 4-0 shellacking at Sheffield United and the Italian left after only 18 games in charge. While his reign is unlikely to live long in the memory of anyone at Vicarage Road, Dionisi can at least boast on his LinkedIn page that in terms of longevity under the Pozzos, he took charge of 18 more matches than Dyche, 17 more than García and 16 more than McKinlay. Indeed, he even outlasted Rob Edwards, who was assured he would be backed “come hell or high water” upon his 2022 appointment, only to be fired from the ejector seat 11 games later. It’s been quite the white-knuckle ride for Watford since the Pozzos arrived, armed only with a spreadsheet, an army of Udinese cast-offs and knowledge of the loophole that there was no Football League cap on the number of players who could be brought in on loan from clubs outside the UK. And while few fans will be able to recall all 25 of the coaches who have been hired and fired by the Pozzos, they do have fond memories to take to the grave. There was that end-to-end Troy Deeney play-off semi-final goal against Leicester. There were five uninterrupted seasons in the Premier League. There was that time they ended Liverpool’s 44-match unbeaten Premier League run despite being stuck in the relegation zone. And what self-respecting Hornet will ever forget travelling to watch their team play in the 2019 FA Cup final? Of course it hasn’t all been rosy in the Pozzo garden. The eight-day managerial reign of McKinlay was a source of much mirth for fans of rival clubs. A double relegation from the Premier League – the first amid allegations of a dressing-room bust-up linked to an illegal lockdown party – wasn’t great either. Playing I’m Still Standing by Elton John, the club’s honorary life president, over the Vicarage Road PA system to mark their descent into the Championship heaped further embarrassment upon the club. And what self-respecting Hornet will ever forget travelling home after watching their team play in the 2019 FA Cup final? While it would be foolish to predict what will happen next at a club that currently sit two places above the Championship relegation zone, the one stonewall certainty is that the name “Edward Iordanescu” will be the next to be copied and pasted into the over-worked club template announcing a managerial departure. The Romanian was formally introduced this morning and with this being his 14th job in the past 16 years, he can arguably lay claim to being the most ‘Watford’ manager of the Pozzo era. “For me, I want a team that plays very good, organised football with the spirit and attitude, and the strong mentality,” he blathered, as local reporters dabbed their bingo cards. “And then, yes, regarding the organisation of the team, that takes time.” History suggests getting the time he needs is a pipe dream for Iordanescu, whose first game in charge is away at Championship basement-dwellers Derby County. Should Watford go to Pride Park and lose, he could be out of a job by Saturday night. The post Manchester United predicted XI vs Brentford: Senne Lammens keeps his place appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
599055523e134021.content: Manchester United host Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday as head coach Mauricio Pochettino weighs up his team selection following Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting CP. Goalkeeper and Defence Senne Lammens should continue in goal. His errors against Sporting will inevitably create debate over whether a short break would help, but we think Pochettino will probably offer him an immediate opportunity to respond. Former United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has also argued that dropping Lammens may not help him rediscover his confidence . United are expected to return to a back four after their European assignment. Leny Yoro and Harry Maguire could form the central partnership, with Lisandro Martinez moving across to left-back. Using Martinez on that flank would allow Shaw , who returned to training earlier this week after a muscular problem kept him out for nine matches , to be reintroduced gradually from the bench rather than being asked to complete a full Premier League game immediately after his lay-off. Patrick Dorgu is an alternative at left-back. Noussair Mazraoui is the likely choice at right-back after playing reasonably well against Sporting. Diogo Dalot is the other option. Either of those could also switch to the left. Midfield The deeper midfield pairing is expected to remain unchanged. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans should continue together after starting against Sporting. Manuel Ugarte and Carlos Baleba’s continued absence also reduces the scope for rotation in this area, although Andrey Santos is an option. Attack Fernandes should start as the number 10 if he recovers from illness . His two goals on Wednesday underlined his importance to a side desperately needing results, but his condition will have to be assessed before the team is finalised. If he doesn’t make it, either Josh Zirkzee or Mason Mount will likely come in as the number 10. Amad is expected to continue on the right after a positive display against Sporting. Matheus Cunha should return on the left following his suspension for the Champions League fixture. Bryan Mbeumo could lead the line while Sesko remains sidelined. The former Brentford forward would not necessarily stay fixed through the middle, however, with Amad and Cunha also capable of interchanging positions across the front three. ab84653687f79005.content:
Pochettino Reshapes Man United Squad Amid Injury and Transfer Concerns
Mauricio Pochettino is addressing Manchester United's squad problems through academy opportunities and contract management as he begins his tenure at Old Trafford. The Argentine manager has brought French striker Enzo Kana-Biyik into first-team training while the club has activated a contract extension for captain Bruno Fernandes and remains linked with Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala.
United face immediate challenges following defensive difficulties against Liverpool and Sporting CP. Their attacking options are also limited because Benjamin Sesko, the club's only natural number nine, is expected to remain unavailable until at least New Year.
Pochettino previously deployed Bryan Mbeumo as a striker against Liverpool before giving Joshua Zirkee the central attacking role in the Champions League encounter with Sporting CP.
Kana-Biyik has emerged as another option after receiving an opportunity to train with senior players. Manchester United signed the French forward from Le Havre in the summer of 2025 before sending him to Lausanne-Sport on a season-long loan.
The 6ft 2in forward made 26 appearances for the Swiss club, recording one goal and one assist. After returning to England, the Paris-born France U20 international continued his development with United's youth teams, scoring once in four Under-21 appearances this season.
According to Daily Mail journalist Nathan Salt, Kana-Biyik joined senior players during Friday morning's training session.
"Enzo Kana-Biyik among the academy players involved in first team training this morning for United," Salt wrote on X.
Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites and Jaydan Kamason also participated in the session. Kana-Biyik's involvement comes as Pochettino searches for additional attacking solutions during Sesko's absence.
Another important development concerns Fernandes, whose contract was due to expire at the end of the season. Manchester United activated an option extending the Portuguese midfielder's agreement by 12 months, according to a person familiar with the arrangement who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity.
The extension protects United against losing their captain as a free agent next summer. Fernandes signed a three-year agreement in 2024 that included the additional year, while negotiations over a longer-term arrangement are expected to resume.
However, Fernandes' availability for the upcoming Brentford match remained uncertain after he missed Friday's training session. Pochettino explained that the midfielder was dealing with an illness following his two-goal performance in the 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP.
"He has been affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game with a small problem, and today he cannot take part in the training session," Pochettino said.
The manager indicated that United would assess Fernandes' condition before making a decision about his participation.
"We will see during the day and tomorrow how he wakes up, and then we will see. We are not going to take any risks, because you know that when this type of situation happens, you do not feel capable," Pochettino added.
United's opponents have also noticed changes under the new manager. Brentford head coach Keith Andrews assessed Pochettino's early influence after observing his first two matches in charge.
"You can see elements of what he is as a coach, but you have to balance that with where they currently are," Andrews said.
Andrews also acknowledged the quality associated with United's manager and the challenge of playing at Old Trafford.
"You can already start to notice the changes in terms of what he wants, definitely, but we want to play our game. We expect a very good and organized United," Andrews said.
He added that his team expected a demanding contest against the Manchester side.
"It is Old Trafford, it is Manchester United, it is Mauricio Pochettino. He is an incredibly impressive coach because of what he has achieved. So we have to expect Manchester United to be at their best," Andrews said.
Beyond immediate squad concerns, United have also been associated with a potential move for Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala. The 23-year-old's future has attracted attention following comments from Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness concerning the player's health and contractual situation.
Musiala collapsed twice during Bayern's preseason matches and was diagnosed with absence seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction. The condition has been described as treatable, while Bayern have subsequently emphasized their focus on helping him regain full fitness.
Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Bayern should prioritize the player's recovery rather than publicly discussing his contractual future.
"Bayern Munich are in an extremely difficult situation with Jamal Musiala. Whenever a player is suffering with health complications, these sorts of questions get raised about how they will deal with it or whether he will be able to continue playing," Brown said.
Musiala remains under contract with Bayern until 2030, although reports indicate that a release clause could become active at the end of the season. Bayern are reportedly considering their options, with a potential departure attracting attention from several Premier League clubs.
Brown emphasized that decisions concerning the midfielder's playing future should involve the player and Bayern's medical staff.
"At the end of the day, it will be up to the player and the club's doctors to come to a conclusion, and if they think he's okay to continue, then he will continue. It's not up to the club," Brown said.
He also questioned the decision to discuss Musiala's circumstances publicly, particularly given the complicated financial and insurance considerations surrounding professional contracts.

0bc0e8747c333e44.content: Manchester United have combined with Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur to make life even harder for Manchester City as their appeal against the guilty verdict continues. Guilty In September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty of all charges of breaching its financial rules over a nine-year period. Enzo Maresca’s side are said to have boosted their income by a mind-blowing amount of more than £900m. The verdict was reached by an independent commission, which outlined that City entered into “sham contracts” with commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs. City also reported inaccurate accounts in a deliberate attempt to mask their true financial position. United’s cross-town rivals additionally agreed “sham” image-rights deals with players and with the then-manager, Roberto Mancini, artificially inflating their earnings as a result. City have maintained their innocence and lodged an appeal “on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.” The appeal is running in tandem with a sanctions hearing overseen by the independent commission, with the Premier League anxious to wrap matters up as quickly as possible. United constitute one of four Premier League clubs that lodged legal notices in 2024, preserving their entitlement to seek compensation from City so that their potential claims would not be deemed time-barred. Arsenal are using their retained lawyers, HFS Kramer, to prepare their own claim.” “A source with knowledge of the case disclosed there had been a degree of cooperation between the clubs using Wiggin, because they have also engaged the same analysts to assess the size of the potential losses allegedly caused by City’s financial cheating, but that they would bring separate claims for damages.” A source claimed, “The cases are similar but different. a47be73a00faab32.title: Manchester United have new suspension risk after Leny Yoro red card appeal
a47be73a00faab32.text: Manchester United have new suspension risk after Leny Yoro red card appeal
a47be73a00faab32.content:
Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.
Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United's defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach quickly turned into a nightmare.
The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender "for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)".
However, Man Utd appealed the decision and it has proven successful with Yoro cleared to face Brentford on Saturday.
A statement from the FA read: "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.
"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November."
Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal
United have had to deal with their fair share of suspensions already this season. Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matheus Cunha and, more recently, Youri Tielemans, have all been sent-off at some point to raise concerns over a disciplinary issue within the squad.
A further suspension concern is in the form of central defender Harry Maguire, who is currently on four Premier League yellow cards.
As per the rules, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.
Man United's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the away game against Brighton on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.
Maguire's Premier League yellow cards this season have come against Everton, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea.
As such, if the central defender is booked against Brentford, he will have to serve a one-match ban against Newcastle at St James' Park on December 2.
Even if Maguire avoids a yellow card, he will still be walking the disciplinary tightrope in upcoming games against Newcastle, Coventry, Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Brighton.
The other Man United players in danger of a Premier League ban are Bruno Fernandes, Diogo Dalot, Ayden Heaven, Bryan Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Luke Shaw, all on two yellow cards.

The Red Devils are set to host Brentford at Old Trafford in the Premier League tomorrow. Speaking at the pre-match press conference , Pochettino was quizzed about the injury status of Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford. The 54-year-old said: “Baleba, the moment was Roma, [when he got] injured, and the medical staff were talking about 10, 12 weeks. “Marcus, today I think, started being in the session on the field. “I think he is starting to feel much better, we will see day by day, working with the feeling that he is going to provide us [with something] after every single training session, increasing the progression of the recovery.” Injuries continue to cause problems Baleba suffered a hamstring injury shortly after half-time during United’s 3-2 victory over AS Roma earlier this month. The initial recovery estimate of 10 to 12 weeks suggests the midfielder may not return until January. Baleba is a dynamic midfielder but has struggled with injuries since his £65 million transfer to United earlier this summer. The 22-year-old missed the start of the season with an ankle injury before gradually working his way back into contention. However, just as he appeared ready to establish himself as a regular starter, another injury struck against Roma. Pochettino prefers young and energetic midfielders. There is no doubt that the United head coach would have relished having the midfielder available for his high-intensity style of football. Rashford was managing a hip problem during the early stages of the campaign. Despite continuing to feature regularly, the issue worsened and eventually forced the forward onto the sidelines, where he has spent the past six weeks. His return to on-field training is an encouraging development, although he may need several more sessions to rebuild his fitness before being considered for first-team action. The post Amad explains how former Man United boss Ruben Amorim helped improve major skill appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
28f572fdf70757e6.content: Manchester United speedster Amad may have had a goal disallowed in the 2-2 draw against Sporting CP, but he certainly did not look out of place in new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s tactics. The Argentine manager is working to implement his intense attacking football at Old Trafford, and facets of his game were evident at the Estadio José Alvalade in midweek. According to Opta, the Red Devils registered 12 high turnovers against the Portuguese club, the most they have managed in a single game this season. Amad was central to the team’s performance, continuously harrying the opposition and keeping them on their toes. This is one of the Ivorian ’s trademarks, and he has now opened up about honing his work ethic under a former manager. Learning from Ruben Amorim Speaking to United Review , Amad acknowledged that he developed his off-the-ball pressing under former head coach Ruben Amorim. He said: “I mean I tried to develop that part of my game when Ruben Amorim was here.” “It’s thanks to Ruben that he made me step up on this, on this thing, and, yeah, I’m pretty good at taking the ball off opponents. But I think the most important for me is to help the team in every aspect that they need me.” “Sometimes, you can have a bad game, sometimes you can have a good game, the most important thing is always to be focused and try to do your best you can.” Amad enjoyed some of the best football of his career under the Portuguese while operating mostly as a right-sided wing-back, registering 10 goals and 11 assists in 43 appearances. Dealing with the physicality of the Premier League Amad arrived at Old Trafford in 2021 from Atalanta as one of the most exciting young forwards on the continent and needed time to cope with the physicality of the Premier League. Reflecting on the matter, the Ivorian said: “I think the first thing that I realised when I came here, it was my muscles, that I need to develop my muscles.” “I need to build my muscle. I know, in the Premier League, that is going to help me a lot when I don’t have the ball or when I have contact with some other guy that’s maybe bigger than me. So, it was in this couple of years, that I was trying to build that part of my body.” “Yeah, the things that I want to improve now is to score goals and give assists. b5e27d758b86c794.title: Nottingham Forest v Chelsea: Premier League – live
b5e27d758b86c794.text: Minute-by-minute report: Oliver Glasner’s men are starting to get results to go along with performances. Scott Murray has updates on the Friday night action
b5e27d758b86c794.content: Here’s how the Premier League table looks as we all barrel towards one-third-of-the-season territory. Chelsea can go fifth with a win tonight, and would be guaranteed to stay there for at least 19 hours, by which point we’ll know the fate of Brentford at Manchester United, and the outcome of the Leeds-Coventry 1987 FA Cup semi-final rematch). Nottingham Forest can rise as high as 14th with victory, but their rubber-stamped 19-hour stay will only extend if Leeds beat Coventry, in which case they’re guaranteed another two-and-a-half hours, after which all would be dependent on Ipswich’s result against Aston Villa. I’ll level with you, I’m killing time until kick-off. Jamie Carragher and Toby Alderweireld eviscerated Chelsea’s defence earlier this week on Monday Night Football. Xabi Alonso seems to have taken that criticism seriously, because by the looks of it, he’s dropped Levi Colwill and replaced him in the centre of defence by Moisés Caicedo, with Jordan Henderson deputising for the Ecuadorian in midfield. That’s a ballsy call, given that Chelsea’s midfield crumbled to a premium grade of dust when Caicedo was injured against Leeds. At least he’ll still be on the pitch this time. Chelsea make three changes to their starting team, in the wake of that 1-4 home skelping by Leeds. Jordan Henderson, Danny Welbeck and Pedro Neto are in; Levi Colwill, Emmanuel Emegha and Estêvão drop to the bench. Forest make two changes to their starting XI following their 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth last weekend. Igor Jesus and Xaver Schlager replace Dan Ndoye and captain Ryan Yates, who both drop to the bench. Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams, Igor Jesus, Gibbs-White, Delap. Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Ndoye, Kalimuendo, Yates, Netz. Chelsea: Martinez, Acheampong, Fofana, Lavia, Chavarria, Henderson, Caicedo, Pedro Neto, Palmer, Rogers, Welbeck. Subs: Penders, Palestra, Barco, Colwill, Emegha, Quenda, Gusto, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao. Referee: Andrew Madley VAR: Lewis Smith Since returning to the Premier League in 2022, Nottingham Forest have yet to win this particular fixture. They’ve lost it three out of four times, though, the most recent defeat a 3-0 shellacking last October that got Ange Postecoglou the sack 15 minutes after the final whistle. Nobody’s expecting Oliver Glasner to get the old heave-ho should Forest extend their miserable record tonight, but with the Tricky Trees currently above the relegation places only thanks to goal difference, the Austrian could do with three precious points and a little time and space. But it’s his opposite number Xabi Alonso who is under the real pressure tonight. Chelsea are eighth in the table and could go fifth tonight, a scenario that usually doesn’t merit the sounding of the crisis klaxon. But they were hammered 4-1 at home by big rivals Leeds last weekend, their second Premier League defeat in a row and their third in four matches. The defence is in tatters, the midfield falls apart when Moisés Caicedo isn’t there, the style of play is yet to be determined, and the boss used to play for Liverpool. Another defeat would set the cat, if not among the pigeons, then a couple of paces behind them, quietly waiting for the most effective moment to pounce. The good news for Chelsea: that aforementioned record at the City Ground. The good news for Forest: they’ve already beaten Manchester City at home, and won at Stamford Bridge back in May. So good luck confidently predicting this. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT. It’s on!

860b2ada5fb3fdbe.content: Manchester United are set to tap into the transfer market for a new centre defender after a nightmare start to the 2026-27 campaign. According to The Athletic , “talks are taking place to understand the conditions of a potential transfer for Fulham defender Calvin Bassey in January.” Fulham have no interest in selling their captain in January, as he has developed into a solid defender under new manager Alvaro Arbeloa. The left-footed centre-back is known for his quick bursts of acceleration and ability to drive the ball forward. United unlikely to sign Bassey in January The 26-year-old has been at Fulham for the past three years and has made 114 appearances. He has helped his side keep three clean sheets this season. He has reached a top speed of 34.4 km/h and covers 10.6 km per 90 minutes. These are impressive numbers, and his athleticism is likely to appeal to United head coach Mauricio Pochettino. Considering he is a left-footed defender, INEOS could see him as a replacement for Lisandro Martinez. The Argentina international could walk out of Old Trafford as a free agent after contract expires at the end of June 2027. Arbeloa revealed earlier today that Fulham want to offer Bassey a new contract following his impressive performances. We believe Bassey will end up signing a new deal, as United will not commit to paying a premium fee to the Cottagers in January. Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton) and Nathan Collins (Brentford) are other names on United’s transfer shortlist. Stats from Fotmob.com Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
