United were likewise unfortunate […] Article written by Sri Aswin .
7fb96e5118e7f77e.content: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could hand midfielder Andrey Santos a start during Saturday’s Premier League encounter against Brentford at Old Trafford. The Red Devils could not return to winning ways against Sporting CP in the Champions League in midweek. They were unlucky after some big refereeing decisions went against them. United were likewise unfortunate against Liverpool last weekend with Leny Yoro’s red card, and Pochettino will be determined to end the club’s winless run against the Bees. Ahead of the game, there could be a big change in midfield with captain Bruno Fernandes doubtful with a virus picked up in Portugal. He was not part of training for the same reason . With the short turnaround time to tomorrow’s kick-off, the Portuguese faces a race against time to be fit. If Fernandes is sidelined, we believe Youri Tielemans could move into the number 10 position, having done so on a few occasions this campaign. This could hand Santos a start alongside Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield. United will come up against a stubborn Brentford side known for quick transitions from defence to attack, and the club need more mobility in the centre of the park against them. We would pick Santos over Tielemans regardless of Fernandes’ condition, but the captain’s sickness means that both could be in the starting XI to face the Bees on Saturday. Santos, signed for £48 million from Chelsea last summer, had a solid pre-season, but he has been out of contention for a starting role lately despite Carlos Baleba’s hamstring injury. Pochettino recently handed Joshua Zirkzee his first start of the season against Sporting CP. The Dutchman did not score but certainly left a good impression on the Argentine, as shown on the sidelines. Zirkzee provided a focal point in attack and fared decently with his link-up play. 0f9cc123bf6a6d80.title: Forgotten Man United star called up to first-team training by Mauricio Pochettino
0f9cc123bf6a6d80.text: Mauricio Pochettino will make his home debut from the Old Trafford dugout when Manchester United play Brentford this weekend
0f9cc123bf6a6d80.content:
Forgotten Man United star called up to first-team training by Mauricio Pochettino
Mauricio Pochettino will make his home debut from the Old Trafford dugout when Manchester United play Brentford this weekend
Mauricio Pochettino invited forgotten striker Enzo Kana-Biyik to train with the Manchester United first team ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford.
The highly-rated French forward was joined by Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites and Jaydan Kamason as Pochettino got a good look at the youngsters in his squad as he prepares to make his Old Trafford debut.
Kana-Biyik joined United on a free transfer from Le Havre in the summer of 2025 but was immediately sent out on loan to Lausanne-Sport in Switzerland to aid his development.
The 19-year-old striker netted just once in 26 appearances before returning to Manchester, where he has played four times for the U21s so far this season. He now has his eye on a first-team call-up.
Pochettino could be without Bruno Fernandes for the clash with the Bees, with the club captain suffering from a virus. Should he fail a late fitness test, the midfielder will miss the fixture alongside Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte.
"Yes, we don't know," Pochettino said of Fernandes in his pre-match press conference on Friday. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and today, he cannot be part of the training session.
"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."
United go into the game in the relegation zone, with Pochettino yet to taste victory in his opening two fixtures in all competitions. Brentford, by contrast, are defying odds once again, and battered Everton 4-0 last time out.
But Bees boss Keith Andrews isn't getting carried away ahead of a trip to the Theatre of Dreams. "It's Old Trafford, it's Manchester United, it's Mauricio Pochettino," he said. "He's an incredibly impressive manager with what he's achieved.
"So, we have to expect Manchester United to be at their absolute best. If we compete to our levels, we're confident with what we can do. I expect a really tough game."

8564f0c311e0aa60.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
8564f0c311e0aa60.text: Mikel Arteta would not be drawn on City’s financial charges but said of the points target: ‘It’s only been done once and that’s what we want’
8564f0c311e0aa60.content: Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season. Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches. Arsenal drew against Newcastle last week and have only dropped points in one other game so far: a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in September. But Arteta said that his team will have to be exceptional if they are to match City’s record of only two defeats and four draws across the whole season. “We haven’t hit the level yet that they did and I was there when we did 100 points,” he said. “That’s the level that is unprecedented and every record was beaten. That’s what we have to aim for because that’s what I expect that all the clubs and all the squads with the capacity they have in this league are going to aim for this season or the next few seasons.” Asked if that City side was his benchmark as a manager, Arteta added: “You want to be the best version that you can. That’s something that’s been done only once in the league and that’s what we want to do. It’s going to be extremely difficult but we want to be as close as that because that’s what is going to increase the probability of winning the Championship again.” City finished their record-breaking season in 2017-18 with a +79 goal difference and wrapped up the title with five games to spare. It also falls inside the nine-season period when they have been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations. City have yet to learn their fate but Arteta denied that the uncertainty over what punishment they will receive could overshadow the game on Sunday. “I hope that it doesn’t because this is a process that is still open and not resolved and I wouldn’t know what is going to happen,” he said. “I think when we have two teams at the level that they’re both in right now with the quality of play that they have on that pitch it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy.” Arteta also said retaining Arsenal’s title on the pitch is “the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on”. Arsenal supporters are being urged to arrive early on Sunday for a pre-match display. But Arteta bizarrely refused to comment on whether emotions will be running high among fans when City come to north London for the first time since being found guilty. “I don’t know. That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there,” he said. David Raya could play against City despite fears that the Spain goalkeeper could be out for a substantial period after injuring a shoulder against Newcastle last week. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Borussia Dortmund in midweek and Arteta said he has full faith in the former Chelsea goalkeeper despite his error in the Carabao Cup final against City this year. “The experience that Kepa has is already incredible. In the teams that he’s been involved [in], the squads that he’s been involved [in], the trophies that he’s won. There’s none of that [doubts],” he said.

4de619240d9d148d.content: Manchester United host Brentford in today’s Premier League game at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have had a dreadful league season so far, picking up only eight points from 11 matches. They desperately need to return to winning ways and have the chance to do so against the Bees. Ahead of the game, manager Mauricio Pochettino could make at least three changes from the 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP in midweek. Formation: 4-2-3-1 Predicted Line-up: Senne Lammens had a forgettable night in Lisbon. The Belgian saved a penalty conceded by Lisandro Martinez, but went on to concede his own, which was converted. He was also poor with his handling, which contributed to Sporting CP’s equaliser (2-2). Despite this, he should be an assured starter between the sticks ahead of Karl Darlow again. The backline could witness one change from midweek. Noussair Mazraoui replaced Diogo Dalot in the XI and had a tough outing after an early knock. The Moroccan has not quite replicated his international displays at club level and could make way for Dalot at right-back. The rest of the backline should stay unchanged. Yoro, whose red card against Liverpool was rescinded by the FA on appeal, should partner Harry Maguire in the heart of the defence. Lisandro Martinez has been refreshing to watch as a left-back, and the Argentine should continue in the same role. In midfield, United are yearning for more mobility and a higher work rate. Brentford like to play in quick transitions, and Youri Tielemans should be benched in our view. The £35 million signing could be a potential weak link. It appears an ideal game for Andrey Santos to partner Kobbie Mainoo. Santos offers more with his mobility and defensive contributions. The Brazilian looks best suited to operate as a number six. Mainoo should get more licence to press forward. Pochettino said in his presser that Bruno Fernandes is doubtful after missing training due to a virus picked up in Portugal, but the club captain has hinted that he could be fit for the encounter. He should continue as the attacking midfielder. Matheus Cunha is available again after serving a one-game suspension in Europe. The Brazilian could start on the left wing today, with Bryan Mbeumo switching to the opposite flank. Amad Diallo looks likely to drop to the bench with Mbeumo’s role change and Cunha’s return. Pochettino was delighted on the sidelines for Joshua Zirkzee after his substitution in midweek. Based on the Argentine’s reaction, we believe the Dutchman could continue to lead the line. The former Bologna man was a good focal point in midweek and could make his first league start this season. Stats from Transfermarkt.com Article written by Sri Aswin .

26e0c546b764d279.title: Manchester United line-up vs Brentford predicted as Bruno Fernandes call made and one star returns
26e0c546b764d279.text: Man United are looking for their first Premier League win since August today as they face Brentford at Old Trafford.
26e0c546b764d279.content:
Manchester United line-up vs Brentford predicted as Bruno Fernandes call made and one star returns
Man United are looking for their first Premier League win since August today as they face Brentford at Old Trafford.
Will it be third time lucky for Mauricio Pochettino? The new Manchester United head coach should have bagged his first win against Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night but a couple of refereeing howlers meant his side came away with a 2-2 draw.
Next up is Brentford in what will be Pochettino's Old Trafford debut as United boss. The Bees are enjoying another solid season and have lost just two league games this campaign, so United will need to be at their best if they are to secure the win they need to haul themselves out of the relegation zone.
Senne Lammens had a night to forget on Wednesday as his two mistakes led to Sporting goals, but he will almost certainly start in goal today. United need some consistency right now and so Pochettino could opt to stick with Noussair Mazraoui at right-back, though Luke Shaw has to come into the side on the left if fit.
Leny Yoro performed well against Sporting and he should keep his place in the heart of the backline. Harry Maguire can partner him.
Kobbie Mainoo is one of the first names on the team sheet, while Youri Tielemans starts alongside him with Carlos Baleba still out.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
Amad wrongly had a goal disallowed against Sporting and he looked bright. Pochettino should give him a run on the right as he looks to regain some confidence, while Bryan Mbeumo can start on the opposite side.
Bruno Fernandes missed training on Friday as a precaution and Pochettino has confirmed he is a doubt for the game, but if he is even close to being available you can guarantee he will want to play.
And finally, Joshua Zirkzee could be given another chance to lead the line. The Dutchman's long-term future clearly lies away from Old Trafford but it's needs must right now and he has given a decent account of himself in recent weeks.
United predicted XI: Lammens, Mazraoui, Yoro, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Amad, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Zirkzee
26e0c546b764d279.body:
Mauricio Pochettino menyiapkan susunan pemain Manchester United untuk menghadapi Brentford dengan satu keraguan pada kapten tim.

Manchester United mengincar kemenangan pertama di bawah Mauricio Pochettino saat menjamu Brentford di Old Trafford. Pelatih asal Argentina tersebut diprediksi tetap menurunkan Senne Lammens di bawah mistar gawang meski melakukan kesalahan melawan Sporting Lisbon. Bruno Fernandes diragukan tampil setelah absen dalam sesi latihan akibat tindakan pencegahan. Sementara itu, Luke Shaw berpeluang besar kembali mengisi posisi bek kiri jika dinyatakan bugar.

6d3b6bc0371f82a0.text: Manchester United are reportedly willing to let Ayden Heaven leave in January, at least on a temporary basis. The 20-year-old joined the Red Devils in January 2025 and made a swift impact under Ruben Amorim before suffering an injury. The defender was scarcely used last season, but he featured prominently in the first three months […] The post Man Utd tell Carrick favourite he can leave in January after losing his place under Pochettino appeared first on utdreport .
6d3b6bc0371f82a0.content: Manchester United are reportedly willing to let Ayden Heaven leave in January, at least on a temporary basis. The 20-year-old joined the Red Devils in January 2025 and made a swift impact under Ruben Amorim before suffering an injury. The defender was scarcely used last season, but he featured prominently in the first three months of the current campaign when Michael Carrick was still in charge. Man Utd open to loaning out Ayden Heaven (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) In addition to playing in his original role at centre-back, the former Arsenal man was also one of the makeshift left-back solutions Carrick used in Luke Shaw’s absence. However, Heaven’s status at the club instantly diminished following the managerial change, as Mauricio Pochettino kept him on the bench in his first two games as Man Utd head coach. Heaven’s Man Utd Stats per Coach Appearances Goals Assists Ruben Amorim 16 0 1 Darren Fletcher 1 0 0 Michael Carrick 15 0 0 Mauricio Pochettino 0 0 0 Total 32 0 1 The Argentine tactician has seemingly placed the young Englishman at the bottom of his centre-back pecking order, with Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, and Matthijs de Ligt all ahead of him, at least based on the early evidence. According to Football Insider transfer correspondent Pete O’Rourke, Man Utd are ready to listen to loan offers for Heaven in January. However, the club isn’t willing to sell the promising defender just yet. The plan is to send the London native elsewhere so he can gain experience while earning consistent opportunities before rejoining United’s ranks in the summer. Should Man Utd sanction Heaven’s loan move? (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Between now and January, Pochettino’s pecking order could easily shift as the manager and his staff learn more about the players at their disposal. If Heaven still finds himself at the bottom when the dust settles, he would naturally consider a loan move to maximise his chances. But with De Ligt still far from his optimal physical shape and Yoro occasionally moved to right-back, losing Heaven could leave Man Utd with limited options at the back. So unless INEOS bring in a new defender in January, parting ways with any of their current players would be ill-advised. MUFC have been linked with the likes of Nathan Collins , Calvin Bassey, and Jarran Branthwaite, but it remains to be seen if the management will be able to deliver one of them in the middle of the campaign. c0300579bce866e9.title: “Completely blocked”: Fabrizio Romano drops update on Bruno Fernandes’ contract situation at United
c0300579bce866e9.text: Manchester United have extended Bruno Fernandes' contract to 2028, but Fabrizio Romano claims talks over a long-term deal are blocked. The post Fabrizio Romano drops update on Bruno Fernandes’ contract situation at Man United appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
c0300579bce866e9.content: Manchester United find themselves in a predicament as they sweat over the future of Bruno Fernandes. Fernandes has inarguably been United’s most consistent performer over the past half a decade, proving to be a talisman under different managers. However, his future and role under Mauricio Pochettino remains unclear. The United captain has yet to commit to the club’s new project. Manchester United trigger extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract As far as Manchester United’s official stance is concerned, Bruno Fernandes is in the final year of his contract at Old Trafford. However, on Friday, The Athletic reported that United have activated an option to extend Fernandes’ contract. The deal, which was initially due to expire in the summer of 2027, included the option of a further 12 months. The Red Devils have reportedly exercised the option, ensuring the Portuguese superstar will not be able to talk to foreign clubs from January to discuss a free transfer next summer. Still, The Athletic underlined that the extension does not rule out a sale next year and all it does is put United in a position to demand a fee for Fernandes. Talks over long-term deal going nowhere Now, Fabrizio Romano has shed more light on the situation and relationship between the two parties. Speaking on his YouTube channel , Romano claimed that talks between United and Fernandes over a new long-term contract are “completely blocked”. It is understood the 32-year-old wants to see a United project capable of competing for the Premier League and Champions League. “I told you in the previous video that Manchester United activated the option to extend Bruno’s contract for one more season, until 2028. But let me clarify: the new contract talks between Bruno and Manchester United are completely blocked,” Romano said. “So the fact that United activated the option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract is a protection, but it doesn’t mean Bruno is 100% staying for the 2027/28 season at all.” Romano continued: “Bruno wants to understand which direction United are going. Bruno wants to understand how the feeling will be with Mauricio Pochettino. Bruno wants to understand if Manchester United will really build a team able to compete to win the Premier League and compete for the Champions League. Bruno wants to win.” Bruno Fernandes, 2026/27 Stat Premier League UEFA Champions League League Cup All competitions Competition Premier League UEFA Champions League League Cup All competitions Apps 10 5 1 16 Goals 4 4 0 8 Assists 2 0 0 2 Goals + assists 6 4 0 10 Avg rating 7.13 7.13 6.30 7.08 Accordingly, the United hierarchy will have the winter transfer window to show their captain, and more importantly Mauricio Pochettino, that they mean business. It has been reported elsewhere that INEOS intend to strengthen the club’s backline in January. d76754bbf307f5d9.text: Napoli have opened talks with Manchester United and Joshua Zirkzee's entourage over a potential January move for the Dutch striker. The post Joshua Zirkzee: Napoli set Man United ace’s January exit in motion with major move appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
d76754bbf307f5d9.content: Manchester United’s decision to invest in Joshua Zirkzee in the summer of 2024 has yet to yield dividends. The Red Devils were looking to add more firepower to their attack and competition for Rasmus Hojlund when they turned to the Dutch striker. Fresh from lighting up Serie A with Bologna, Zirkzee was expected to work in tandem with the Dane and usher in the glory days at Old Trafford. Unfortunately, the Dutchman ‘s first season ended in a whimper, as he picked up an injury and was sidelined for the final weeks. Meanwhile, Hojlund was replaced with Benjamin Sesko in the summer of 2025, and Zirkzee has struggled for game time ever since. The Slovenian finished last campaign as the preferred focal point in attack, with the Dutchman playing second fiddle. Sesko, meanwhile, has missed much of the current season due to a shin injury, offering Zirkzee the perfect opportunity to cement his place in the starting XI. Unfortunately, things have not worked out for him so far. Zirkzee a peripheral figure at United Zirkzee failed to convince former manager Michael Carrick, who deployed Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha in the No. 9 role in the absence of Sesko this season. With the team dropping to the relegation zone, the Englishman was relieved of his duties earlier this month. Mauricio Pochettino took charge last week as Carrick’s replacement, generating hope that Zirkzee could be afforded a lifeline. The Dutchman started last weekend’s disastrous 4-0 defeat to Liverpool from the bench, but was selected to lead the line in midweek against Sporting CP in the Champions League. Unfortunately, Zirkzee failed to make an impact, with United having to rely on their mercurial skipper Bruno Fernandes to secure a 2-2 draw at the Estadio José Alvalade. The Dutch striker’s performance did not help his cause and he now remains linked with an exit in January. A previous report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that Napoli are among the clubs keeping a close watch on the 25-year-old. An update on the saga has now emerged. 15fe4559ae8b6912.text: Manchester United are in desperate need of improvement and chiefs think Mauricio Pochettino could hold the key to revolutionary upcoming transfer windows
15fe4559ae8b6912.content:
Mauricio Pochettino can help pull off second stunning Man United transfer with 'chiefs hopeful'
Manchester United are in desperate need of improvement and chiefs think Mauricio Pochettino could hold the key to revolutionary upcoming transfer windows
Manchester United chiefs had believed Mauricio Pochettino could help the club pull off an ambitious move for Julian Alvarez. Now, the hierarchy thinks young superstar Nico Paz could be tempted to Old Trafford by their new boss.
Pochettino has not enjoyed the greatest of starts as United manager, and when the January window arrives, there will no doubt be a need to snap up some reinforcements.
It is understood that the club are eyeing up a striker, centre-back and left-back. And reports that arose before Pochettino arrived at Carrington hinted that the chance to work with a fellow countryman could coax the in-demand Atletico Madrid star Alvarez to the club.
Now, Paz, a young playmaker cutting his teeth for Como, is another who has been touted to join forces with his fellow Argentine in the summer - with half of Europe seemingly interested in the attacker.
Prior to Pochettino taking up his role as head coach, TNT Sports claimed that United's hierarchy believed they had a chance at landing 26-year-old Alvarez because of Pochettino.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
Alvarez was at the centre of a long and drawn-out transfer saga with Atleti this summer after naming Barcelona as his ideal destination.
Whilst Barca were also keen on securing the forward, a volatile relationship with his club made negotiations impossible. In the end, the Madrid-based club vowed never to sell Alvarez to Barcelona, and he remained with the club for this season.
Arsenal also flirted with the idea of signing the Argentine star over the summer but never made a concrete move. Atleti set a staggering £128million price tag for their talisman.
Now, a second ambitious move for Paz has been rumoured. The Athletic reports that Paz, who joined Como from Real Madrid in 2024 and is the subject of a £67m buy-back clause, is keen on playing under the new United manager. The club's top brass are hopeful.
Paz has been linked with a return to Real Madrid, but it is claimed he is drawn to the prospect of playing under Pochettino and could be viewed as a long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes.
The club captain's one-year contract extension option was triggered by United this week, but his deal still expires in 2028 and fresh terms are not close.
It has also been reported that Paz and Pochettino share the same agent, which could aid the proceedings. Speculation suggests that United could only have £50m to work with in the upcoming window, but that does not mean they couldn't push the boat out in the summer.

603e2b679c186818.content: Manchester United have secured one of their top young talents to a new deal. Youth focus With crippling debt and owners who are clearly unwilling to spend huge amounts of money, the Red Devils will likely need to turn to their academy more and more in coming months. Playing and promoting youth is a keen tradition at the club and was one of the main attractions of appointing Manchester United main coach Mauricio Pochettino as he has always given young players the opportunity to shine in his previous jobs. This can be seen in numerous young players like Jaydan Kamason and Karim Cassim taking part in first-team training already. The Red Devils have numerous young talents in their squad right now as both the under-18s and under-21s are doing quite well in their domestic leagues. The latest player to secure his future at the club is defender Yuel Helafu . New deal The club’s official website reports: “talented youngster Yuel Helafu has committed his future to Manchester United. The 18-year-old defender has signed a long-term professional contract.” Helafu has been a regular in Darren Fletcher’s under-18 side and he also played a key role in the youth side reaching the FA Youth Cup final last season, which they ultimately narrowly lost to Manchester City. Hard work = rewarded Talented youngster Yuel Helafu has signed a long-term professional contract with the club — congratulations, Yuel! — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 27, 2026 The young full-back has also played for the under-21s, showing his experience and quality for his age. The site also adds: “on the international front, the youngster has been called up by England’s Under-18s and Under-19s.” Finally, the club concluded in its statement: “everyone at Manchester United is delighted that Yuel has signed a new deal and looks forward to seeing him progress.” He has played 14 matches this season in all competitions, scoring a goal and providing three assists. c62cb7d2fdc7c6b5.title: 'A good example': Mikael Silvestre surprisingly criticises 27yo Man Utd star ahead of Brentford game
c62cb7d2fdc7c6b5.text: Former Manchester United defender Mikael Silvestre has surprisingly criticised Matheus Cunha ahead of the Premier League game against Brentford at Old Trafford. Cunha signed for the Red Devils from Wolverhampton Wanderers in the summer of 2025, and he has since been a good performer with several key goal involvements. He has not been firing on […] Article written by Sri Aswin .
c62cb7d2fdc7c6b5.content: Former Manchester United defender Mikael Silvestre has surprisingly criticised Matheus Cunha ahead of the Premier League game against Brentford at Old Trafford. Cunha signed for the Red Devils from Wolverhampton Wanderers in the summer of 2025, and he has since been a good performer with several key goal involvements. He has not been firing on all cylinders this campaign but has still scored four goals and provided two assists for United, including a memorable display against Roma. In a recent interview with BestBettingBonuses, Silvestre said Roy Keane and Gary Neville are right to criticise United players, given the club’s current league fortunes. He also highlighted a lack of effort from United players and gave Cunha as a ‘good example’. While Silvestre rates him ‘very highly’, he added that the Brazilian’s performance against Roma was a one-off and believes the attacker should be more consistent. Silvestre said: “I think the former players like Roy and Gary are right to express their opinion. “They’re hurting watching United like this and, in my opinion, can say whatever they like because they know what it takes to compete for and win the biggest prizes in the game. “A good example is Matheus Cunha, who I will use as an example because he is a player I rate very highly. I see that performance against Roma in the Champions League. “In that game, he played like a man possessed, but where are those performances week in week out? That level of performance must be the standard every time you put on the shirt. It can’t be a one-off.” Silvestre is completely wrong with Cunha criticism Cunha has been one of the Premier League’s best wingers over the past few seasons. His scoring rate may not be exceptional with United, but his effort can’t be questioned, in our view. The Brazilian works hard with and without possession. This season, the 27-year-old has won almost four duels per game, alongside 2.5 recoveries and 1.5 tackles per league appearance. He has made 14 key passes in the English top-flight with four big chances created. In addition to his six goal contributions in all competitions, Cunha has also won three penalties for the club. Of course, his performance against Roma was world-class with two goals and a penalty won, but you can’t expect him to replicate it every game with different opposition presenting different challenges. We feel Silvestre was justified in criticising the lack of effort in the squad, but Cunha should not be an example. The Frenchman was completely wrong with his criticism of the versatile star. Stats from Sofascore.com Article written by Sri Aswin .

7ffc695d46bf76e3.text: Manchester United's youngsters will begin their FA Youth Cup campaign against Burnley on Thursday 3 December at Leyland's County Ground. The post Burnley vs Man United: Exciting FA Youth Cup fixture locked in appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
7ffc695d46bf76e3.content: Manchester United have a fine tradition of promoting youth and hope to do so even more with Mauricio Pochettino and Eva Olid as the head coaches of the men’s and women’s teams, respectively. Youth Cup The Red Devils also have an excellent history in the FA Youth Cup, as no other team has won the trophy as many times. United have come out on top 11 times in their history. Their most recent success came in 2021/22 when Alejandro Garnacho’s brace helped United defeat Nottingham Forest in the final. Manchester United first-team player Kobbie Mainoo was also part of the winning squad. United were also successful in the 2010/11 season, with Paul Pogba and Jesse Lingard part of the winning group. The Red Devils came agonisingly close last season to lifting the trophy for a 12th time, but they lost the final 2-1 to rivals Manchester City. Third round locked in United’s talented youngsters will start their quest for another title next week. The club’s official website reports, “Manchester United’s FA Youth Cup tie against Burnley has been allocated a date.” The site continues: “the third-round clash with the Clarets is to be held on Thursday 3 December. The game will kick off at 19:00 GMT at The County Ground in Leyland.” Last time out against Burnley, United ended up winning 6-0 in a massive victory. Kai Rooney , son of Manchester United’s all-time goalscorer Wayne Rooney, scored four goals in the match. Nonetheless, Burnley will most likely be a much tougher nut to crack at home in a Youth Cup tie. 89ffde8b76556e61.title: Man United Women's Eva Olid and two players nominated for WSL awards after perfect November
89ffde8b76556e61.text: Eva Olid, Maya Le Tissier and Elisabeth Terland have been nominated for Women's Super League awards after United's perfect November. The post Man United Women’s Eva Olid and two players nominated for WSL awards after perfect November appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
89ffde8b76556e61.content: Manchester United Women are enjoying a very positive season to date. Recovery Things did not look so promising at the start of the season when United struggled in pre-season and lost 1-2 to London City Lionesses and Chelsea 0-5 in the opening two matches of the season. The Red Devils have spectacularly recovered to go 14 matches unbeaten in all competitions, a new record for the women’s team. Eva Olid ‘s side have rocketed up the league into fourth place and are just two points behind third place, the final spot for the Champions League in the Women’s Super League. They are also top of the Players’ Cup league phase with five wins from five. November nominations In the month of November, Man United Women logged four victories from four matches. They defeated Aston Villa 0-1 away from home, beat Crystal Palace 2-0 at home and Birmingham City 1-2 away. They also overcame Everton 2-1 in the Players’ Cup. As a result, manager Eva Olid has been nominated by the Super League as a potential winner of the coach of the month award . West Ham United’s Rita Guarino, Tottenham Hotspur’s Martin Ho and London City Lionesses’ Eder Maestre are the other three coaches gunning for the award. You can vote for Olid by following this link . Unbeaten in 14. Enough said Eva is among the nominees for November’s #WSL Manager of the Month award — support the boss here https://t.co/OGLvhTizp8 https://t.co/Qd0EJbxs2E — Manchester United Women (@ManUtdWomen) November 27, 2026 Players Of course managers are just part of a club’s success and it is the players who ultimately perform on the pitch. Therefore, United have two of their squad members nominated for the award. Captain Maya Le Tissier recently brought up her 150th appearance for the Red Devils and scored a fine goal versus Crystal Palace to mark the occasion. She has also been part of a backline that only conceded one goal in three league matches. Elisabeth Terland has also been nominated after scoring two league goals in three matches against Palace and last time out versus Birmingham. She is now joint third in the club’s all-time goalscoring list with only Ella Toone and Leah Galton having scored more than the Norwegian striker. You can vote for Le Tissier or Terland by following this link . 7167c789e0c755c7.title: The 13 players who could miss Man United vs Brentford as big injury list adds up
7167c789e0c755c7.text: Manchester United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon but there will be a large contingent of absentees
7167c789e0c755c7.content:
The 13 players who could miss Man United vs Brentford as big injury list adds up
Manchester United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon but there will be a large contingent of absentees
Manchester United host in-form Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday, with the two sides enduring vastly contrasting campaigns in the Premier League. United are rooted in the relegation zone, claiming victory in only one of their 11 top-flight outings this term.
Mauricio Pochettino's tenure began disastrously with a chastening 4-0 reverse away to Liverpool. That was succeeded by an exasperating 2-2 stalemate with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League which did precious little to lift spirits.
By contrast, Brentford are comfortably positioned in sixth spot following Monday's 4-0 triumph at home to Everton. Yet one parallel between the clubs are their fitness concerns.
MEN Sport examines who's expected to be absent from Saturday's encounter.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources
Man United
Having taken charge of an already injury-ravaged squad, the last thing that Pochettino required was Bruno Fernandes sustaining an issue in midweek. The United skipper has been unwell and his manager confirmed on Friday that he remains doubtful.
"We don't know (if Fernandes can play)," Pochettino said. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session. We'll see.
"We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."
Meanwhile, Amad appeared to pick up a knock in the second half against Sporting and was spotted in discussion with Pochettino after being withdrawn for Shea Lacey. Four further players are definitely sidelined with longer-term injuries, namely Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba.
Doubts: Bruno Fernandes, Amad.
Ruled out: Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba.
Brentford
As for the visitors, they too will be without at least four players through injury. Nathan Collins, Kaye Furo, Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey all remain on the treatment table, while talismanic striker Igor Thiago is absent through suspension.
However, Keith Andrews could welcome back both Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo. "They're building the fitness level that's needed to come into the first-team space," the Brentford boss said.
"But they're training with us pretty consistently. They'll continue that over the next week or two and then, hopefully, they can gatecrash the first-team squad."
Doubts: Josh Dasilva, Antoni Milambo.
Ruled out: Nathan Collins, Kaye Furo, Rico Henry, Aaron Hickey.
Suspended: Igor Thiago.

Manchester United host Brentford at Old Trafford with a severely depleted squad due to fitness concerns. 7dc3246f1d37c822.title: Man Utd predicted XI vs Brentford: Two Reds dropped but Lammens survive
7dc3246f1d37c822.text: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino could make a couple of changes to his lineup when his team hosts Brentford. The Argentine manager began his MUFC tenure with a heavy 0-4 defeat at Anfield last weekend before being hampered by abysmal refereeing on Wednesday, forcing his side to settle for a 2-2 draw in the […] The post Man Utd predicted XI vs Brentford: Two Reds dropped but Lammens survive appeared first on utdreport .
7dc3246f1d37c822.content: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino could make a couple of changes to his lineup when his team hosts Brentford. The Argentine manager began his MUFC tenure with a heavy 0-4 defeat at Anfield last weekend before being hampered by abysmal refereeing on Wednesday, forcing his side to settle for a 2-2 draw in the away Champions League contest against Sporting Club. On Saturday, the 54-year-old will be making his Old Trafford bow, as the Red Devils entertain six-place Brentford at 15:00 UK time. Senne Lammens to be confirmed despite Lisbon struggles (Photo by Jurij Kodrun/Getty Images) Since the start of the season, Senne Lammens has been in shaky form , and his poor performance in Lisbon confirmed as much. After saving Sporting’s first spot-kick, he gave away another with a challenge on Maxi Araujo, and this time, Luis Suarez had the better of him. In the second half, the Belgian failed to pick up an easy long ball, and his fumble allowed the Sporting striker to complete a brace and deny Man Utd a deserved victory. pic.twitter.com/1XDUdCok7W — Best (@kosiDbest) November 25, 2026 But despite the woeful run, Pochettino is unlikely to drop Lammens this early in his tenure, so we can expect the 24-year-old to keep his place in the lineup. On the other hand, Noussair Mazraoui, who had an underwhelming display in midweek , could be dropped in favour of Diogo Dalot, who will be keen to bounce back after miserable outings against Aston Villa and Liverpool. The Portuguese full-back showed some promising signs during his cameo in Lisbon, so he should join Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire, and Lisandro Martinez, who are all expected to keep their places in the team. Mbeumo & Amad could battle for a spot in Man United lineup vs Brentford (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) In his pre-match press conference, Pochettino confirmed Carlos Baleba will be out for 10-12 weeks, so the unusual partnership of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans will be given more time to flourish, as Andrey Santos has yet to convince the technical staff. Bruno Fernandes is a major doubt after missing training with a physical problem, but the club captain often bounces back on matchday, as he can be too stubborn for his own good. So unless the medical staff deems him unfit to play, the captain should be in the starting lineup. Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes absent from training due to illness I hope he’ll be available for the game against Brentford pic.twitter.com/GWaZJR9Pep — kosi (@itzgod_son) November 27, 2026 While Joshua Zirkzee couldn’t get on the scoresheet, having a striker in the lineup, albeit an unconventional one, helped the rest of the team. Therefore, the Dutchman should be given a run in the absence of Benjamin Sesko . Matheus Cunha is available after serving a suspension in Europe, but instead of leading the line, he could start in a more natural role on the left wing, leaving Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo vying for a spot on the right wing. Although the Ivorian has been in decent form lately, the Cameroonian may have the upper hand in the pecking order, so he should get the nod against his former club. Man Utd predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha; Zirkzee The post Man Utd predicted XI vs Brentford: Two Reds dropped but Lammens survive appeared first on utdreport .

0630b1fb7ae87a80.title: Gary McDermott: Man United sign up key coach from rivals to strengthen their academy
0630b1fb7ae87a80.text: Manchester United have appointed Gary McDermott, formerly of Brentford, as a key coach in their academy to further strengthen their youth development. The post Gary McDermott: Man United sign up key coach from rivals to strengthen their academy appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
0630b1fb7ae87a80.content: Manchester United are always looking at ways to improve their academy. Hope for future With Mauricio Pochettino at the helm, there will be hope in the youth ranks that the head coach will begin to give more young players a chance. Talented full-back Yulu Helafu has just signed a new deal, and the youngsters will be hoping to prove themselves in the upcoming Youth Cup fixture versus Burnley on Thursday of the upcoming week. New role United’s staff has undergone a seismic change in recent weeks, with Pochettino bringing in his own staff and, in particular, experts to work on fitness, such as his son Sebastiano, who is now part of the coaching set-up. Spaniard Silvia Tuya is also waiting for a work permit to join up as a strength and conditioning coach and will be the first woman to have a coaching role on the male side of the club. The Red Devils have also made a change to their youth department according to Brentford’s official site . The website reads, “Gary McDermott has left Brentford to take up a role in Manchester United’s Academy.” It continues, “during his two years with the Bees, McDermott oversaw a fourth-place finish in the Under-18s Professional Development League and victory in the Under-17s PDL Shield, before leading the Under-18s into the U18 Premier League following the Academy’s promotion to Category One status.” McDermott has plenty of experience with different youth levels, having worked his way up as head coach of the Under-13s and Under-14s before being appointed Under-18s head coach in May 2025. Brentford Academy director David Rainford said, “on behalf of Brentford Football Club, I’d like to thank Gary for everything he has given to the Academy. His hard work and commitment, first with the younger age groups and then with the Under-18s, have helped a number of our young players take important steps in their development. He has played his part in laying the foundations for our first season as a Category One Academy.” Finally, he commented, “Gary leaves with our very best wishes for his new role at Manchester United.” McDermott also has experience coaching the Under-18s at Forest Green Rovers and spent a decade at Southampton, working across the Under-9s to Under-16s, having started his coaching career at Bristol City. 36eac533c9da4203.title: Basque to the future: Andoni Iraola fired up for first Merseyside derby
36eac533c9da4203.text: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes
36eac533c9da4203.content: “I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape. “It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a very respectful way. This week there has been a lot [of interaction with Liverpool fans], especially with playing big games against United and Everton. ‘We need to win, we need to win,’ they say.” That has rarely been a problem of late for Liverpool, who have lost one of their past 15 visits to Everton and showed with last season’s 100th-minute winner from Virgil van Dijk that a move to a new stadium does not necessarily mean a fresh start. Iraola has identified parallels with the Basque derby not only through this week’s encounters with an approving public. The Liverpool head coach says of Athletic v Sociedad: “It is a massive game for us and it’s a bit like here – you know a lot of people on the other side. I have a lot of friends who are Real Sociedad and they have a lot of friends who are Athletic. I think it’s quite a natural rivalry. The relationship between them is normally quite good but everyone wants to win that game.” David Moyes, who managed Real Sociedad for 12 months from November 2014, offers a comparison that extends beyond football. “In some ways, the Basques are like scousers,” the Everton manager says. “They compete with each other and they are rivals but they see themselves as being different from the rest of the country. There is a bit of camaraderie between them. But it is a fierce derby and a huge game. “The thing about Real Sociedad, nearly all your players have to be Basque. Bilbao are pure Basque but we had incredible players coming through ourselves. We gave a debut to [Mikel] Oyarzabal. They had an incredible setup. There are very few teams in the Premier League who could do what Sociedad do in terms of bringing kids through the ranks.” Moyes had a habit of frustrating but not beating his local rivals during his time in the Basque country, which has echoes of his record in the Merseyside derby. That reads four wins, nine draws and 16 defeats across two spells with Everton. All three of his games in charge of Real Sociedad versus Athletic ended in draws, with the first two featuring a red card. Iraola played in the second, in April 2015, when La Real had a man sent off but fought back to draw 1-1 at San Mamés in the last of his 12 seasons with his boyhood club. Despite being born only 10km from San Sebastián, and 100km from Bilbao, there was no question which Basque club Iraola was destined to represent. “It was always Athletic for me,” he says. “I went there very young and I never played for the academy of Real Sociedad. I have a lot of friends who went on to play for Real Sociedad but at my club, Antiguoko, in that moment and also now, it was like an Athletic Club team. The connections mean if you are good at Antiguoko you will go through the Athletic Club system. I was lucky enough to arrive there and spend 16 years in Bilbao.” The Merseyside rivals enter the 249th edition of England’s most-played derby on the back of starkly contrasting weeks. Whereas Everton suffered the heaviest defeat of Moyes’s second spell as manager in Monday’s 4-0 hammering at Brentford, where they also produced arguably their worst performance since the Scot’s return, Liverpool have plundered seven goals without reply in commanding victories against Manchester United and Club Brugge. Their away form under Iraola also augurs well for a fourth successive win over Everton for the first time since a run to August 1991. Liverpool have won their past four fixtures on the road and six from eight in all competitions, scoring 21 times. And it is not only their pace, Florian Wirtz’s growing influence and Alexander Isak’s predatory qualities in attack that have made the difference away from Anfield. No team have conceded fewer goals on their travels in the Premier League this season than Liverpool, with four. The additions of Jérémy Jacquet and Ronald Araújo have improved Liverpool’s resilience as well as their defending at set pieces, both of which will be important at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday. “I don’t think there is a big difference in our performances away or at home,” Iraola says. “Normally you will find more spaces when you play away because teams are braver and they press you more. But sometimes they can press you and you will feel more uncomfortable. I prefer to play at home even if we have better numbers away at the moment. Also at home we have had difficult games in terms of having big games, but the way we play doesn’t really change a lot. “Derbies are always different. It doesn’t matter where you are in the standings, it doesn’t matter the run that you are in. Normally, this type of game is different and you can feel it from the beginning. We have to be very competitive, we have to win our duels and be at a good level because everyone wants to win this game.”

70dfdba575e400dc.title: The Renéessance is over but Arsenal’s chaotic cycle will go on without further change | Suzanne Wrack
70dfdba575e400dc.text: Renée Slegers’ exit, 18 months on from European glory, was inevitable but much of the blame lies with those higher up
70dfdba575e400dc.content: The Renéessance is over. Three down, how many more to go? The exit of Arsenal manager, Renée Slegers, 18 months after delivering European glory was somewhat inevitable, her position made untenable after six home draws in six games and just 15 points from 11 games, but will it solve the Gunners’ problems? There were high expectations in north London prior to the season, after difficult starts in back-to-back WSL campaigns put them outside a real title challenge within the opening few games. There was frustration at their early sluggishness in previous seasons, but there were also asterisks next to each campaign; injury crises stifling things, players going far in a major tournament leaving the club with a stunted pre-season and Champions League qualifying campaigns also cutting into that vital pre-season preparation and players’ time off. This year, there were no excuses. Qualification for the Champions League league phase was secured with a second-place finish in the WSL. Other than Élisa de Almeida, who arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, their summer transfer business was done early. No major international tournament in the summer gave them a full pre-season with a close to full squad. That transfer business was applauded, too, although there were eyebrows raised at the decision to let go of Beth Mead and Katie McCabe, two of their strongest performers last season, with a late attempt to reverse on the latter’s exit a complete mess The arrivals lifted spirits. The recruitment of Georgia Stanway, Selina Cerci, Lisa Baum and Géraldine Reuteler from Bayern Munich, TSG Hoffenheim, RB Leipzig and Eintracht Frankfurt, respectively, and Ona Batlle from Barcelona, and goalkeepers Isabella Damm and Misa Rodríguez from Brøndby and Real Madrid, in addition to De Almeida, demonstrated their title-chasing ambition. How, then, does a starting XI packed with so much talent and with a bench as stacked, fall so short? A squad with so much depth that the HB Køge manager, Kristian Mørch, said, after his side faced the 2025 Champions League winners on 22 September: “We laughed when we saw the lineup and started joking that it must be one of the strongest benches ever in the Women’s Champions League.” After Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall, Slegers is the next manager to be shown the door after a period of underperformance. The difference this time is the clamouring for managerial change was far quieter than her predecessors experienced because many believe Arsenal’s problems are far greater than the manager. Slegers also delivered one of the greatest moments in the club’s history, leading them to Champions League glory with a stunning 1-0 defeat of reigning champions Barcelona in May 2025, having taken charge, initially on an interim basis, the preceding October. It was the most exhilarating of moments for Arsenal fans, who had had to wait for the club that had set the standard for so many years to lift a major trophy again. That victory should have been a launchpad for further success, instead Arsenal have gone backwards, failing to overhaul the squad in the season which followed and then, arguably, failing in their attempt to overhaul it this summer. Slegers is not blame free. The minimal minutes handed to players such as Reuteler and Cerci have been hugely frustrating after the fanfare with which they arrived and the lack of use of Reuteler in particular has felt almost cruel at times. In addition, tactical decisions haven’t made an impact and an inability to light a fire under the beleaguered players has been evident. Ultimately though, the blame lies with those higher up. Under Montemurro, Eidevall and Slegers, all talented managers who began with so much promise, when things started to turn, there was talk of internal reviews, investment, a reset and work being done to find solutions. Except despite those reviews and any changes that were made as a result, here we are, on groundhog day. Those higher up need to take a healthy portion of responsibility for Slegers’ position eventually becoming untenable. In letting Slegers go, Arsenal are losing a young manager with lots of developing still to do but also huge potential. They are also losing a manager who gets the club, a manager who spent time in the academy as a player and who wears a silver ring with the 1936-49 Arsenal crest on it on her little finger. Her future is bright. What’s in Arsenal’s future without greater change is unclear. The former London City Lionesses and Brighton manager Melissa Clarke-Reed, who has been part of Arsenal’s coaching staff since 2004, has been named interim manager, with assistant Aaron D’Antino also leaving after eight years at the club. Possible replacements include a vocally available Nick Cushing, who led Manchester City to a first league title in 2016, the former Manchester United manager Marc Skinner, and the former Bayern Munich and Angel City manager Alexander Straus. Though they may choose to wait and try to lure someone already in post elsewhere such as Casey Stoney (Canada), Laura Harvey (Seattle Reign) or Juan Carlos Amorós (Gotham FC). Whoever comes in, if great change doesn’t come with them, then it would be reasonable to expect that after any initial positivity Arsenal’s chaotic cycle will continue.

4e4cb987606ecb39.text: Jason Wilcox's approach has been criticised ahead of a crucial transfer window for Manchester United
4e4cb987606ecb39.content:
Man United chief Jason Wilcox scolded 'Are you kidding?' as frosty phone call leaked
Jason Wilcox's approach has been criticised ahead of a crucial transfer window for Manchester United
Manchester United's potential difficulties in the transfer market have been laid bare by a leaked conversation involving Jason Wilcox. United's director of football will be busy preparing for a crucial January window.
United desperately need reinforcements following a dire start to the season that has seen off another manager, Michael Carrick, and left the team entrenched in the relegation zone. Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with hauling United clear of danger, but he needs help in the form of new signings.
Bolstering the defence is priority number one, while a new attacking option would be welcome too. Defensively, United have been linked with Fulham duo Antonee Robinson and Calvin Bassey, while Barcelona's Alejandro Balde remains on the radar. As for attacking options, Ivan Toney and Folarin Balogun are potential targets.
It will take savvy negotiations from Wilcox for any of those deals to materialise in the notoriously tricky January window. However, concerns over Wilcox's approach to deal-making have been raised by an unnamed agent, who has detailed a private call over a player.
They told The iPaper: "He started a conversation with me insisting that, given it was Manchester United, they wanted to set the price, lead negotiations over the fee.
"I was like, 'Are you kidding?! Man Utd are nothing like the force they used to be!' Talks struggled from there on in." Another recruitment executive said: "He (Wilcox) talks a lot, but actually says very little."
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
One agent said United were no longer the Premier League's go-to club, especially at this stage of the season. They said: "I expect many of their targets are using United to get a new contract.
"They are ideal for that at the moment, because we know how desperate they are. In the summer, it is a different story, but why would a player willingly join a relegation fight in January?"
For now, Pochettino must work with what he's got, with United facing a tough home clash with in-form Brentford on Saturday afternoon. He may have to cope without captain Bruno Fernandes due to illness.
United have triggered the option to extend the club captain's deal until 2028, preventing other clubs from striking a pre-contract agreement in January.
Both parties are understood to agree that it makes sense to return to negotiations further down the line, allowing full focus on turning around United's fortunes.

Seorang agen mengungkapkan bahwa Wilcox bersikeras agar United memimpin negosiasi harga, yang langsung ditolak karena status klub saat ini. Selain itu, agen tersebut menilai para pemain target dikhawatirkan hanya memanfaatkan situasi keputusasaan United untuk kontrak baru atau enggan bergabung dalam pertarungan degradasi. Di sisi lain, klub telah memperpanjang kontrak Bruno Fernandes hingga 2028 untuk menghindari kepindahan gratis.

Manchester United football director Jason Wilcox faces criticism over his transfer negotiation approach.

Manchester United director of football Jason Wilcox has faced criticism from an agent and a recruitment executive regarding the club's transfer negotiation approach ahead of the January window. f969eb699a227237.title: Will Bruno Fernandes play for Manchester United today? Latest update as ‘new hint dropped’
f969eb699a227237.text: Will Bruno Fernandes play for Manchester United today? Latest update as ‘new hint dropped’
f969eb699a227237.content:
Manchester United will be desperately hoping that Bruno Fernandes is able to play against Brentford today.
The Red Devils welcome Keith Andrews’ high-flying Bees to Old Trafford at 3pm GMT in what is new head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge since leaving the United States national team to succeed the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month.
The former Chelsea and Tottenham boss is seeking a first victory in his new role at the third attempt, after a truly chaotic opening week that saw a 4-0 drubbing by arch-rivals Liverpool with 10 men at Anfield quickly followed by an incident-packed and controversial 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting, in which Fernandes scored both goals against his former club.
But the Argentine’s hopes of achieving that have been hit by concerns over the availability of influential captain Fernandes, who has played all but one minute of Pochettino’s first two games at the helm and looked on track to lead the team again from the No10 position against Brentford as usual.
However, reports then emerged on Friday morning that the 32-year-old had not trained at Carrington on the eve of the game as a precautionary measure after feeling unwell.
United swiftly released a statement to confirm that was indeed the case, informing fans: “Bruno Fernandes was absent from the session. The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”
Pochettino then admitted at his pre-match press conference a couple of hours later that he “did not know” if Fernandes would be in contention to face Brentford, following a virus picked up in Portugal.
"He's affected by a virus from Portugal,” Pochettino said. “He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.
"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].
"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."
It also emerged on Friday that United had triggered their option to automatically extend Fernandes’ contract with the club by a further 12 months, until June 2028.
Will Bruno Fernandes play for Manchester United today?
Fans believe that Fernandes may already have dropped a clear hint as to his potential availability to face Brentford on social media on Friday.
On his official Instagram account, the Portuguese - or his team - posted a match graphic to his Stories that featured an image of him and the title “next match”, before featuring the details of Saturday’s game.
It can be unusual for such graphics to still be posted to official players’ accounts if they are not playing, which can often be a valuable clue as to their involvement when it has generally thought to be in question.
Liverpool have been a good example of this on more than one occasion already this season with regards to the availability of reigning Player of the Season Dominik Szoboszlai during his injury struggles.
However, there is of course the possibility that such a post was scheduled before Fernandes was kept out of training on Friday morning and as such it would obviously have no bearing on his potential availability.

0f95ddf641e53200.content: Mauricio Pochettino is delighted to have Marcus Rashford among his ranks at Manchester United, having tried to acquire his services in the past. The Argentine head coach was appointed earlier in the month as a replacement for Michael Carrick, who oversaw the team’s shocking fall into the relegation zone. The 54-year-old began his tenure with a 0-4 defeat at Anfield and a 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting CP in Lisbon, but he was hampered by controversial refereeing on both occasions. Moreover, Pochettino is still operating with limited options upfront, while awaiting the returns of Rashford as well as Benjamin Sesko. Mauricio Pochettino already wanted Marcus Rashford at PSG (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) After spending 18 months on loan between Aston Villa and Barcelona, Rashford returned to Man Utd in the summer. Unlike Ruben Amorim, Carrick was delighted to accommodate his former teammate. But like the majority of MUFC players this season, the versatile attacker didn’t truly thrive under the recently axed coach. Nevertheless, Italian journalist Fabrizio Romano believes Rashford could have an important role to play in the new regime. In the most recently uploaded video to his official YouTube channel, the transfer market expert recalls how Pochettino had ‘pushed like crazy’ to bring Rashford to Paris Saint-Germain during his tenure in the French capital between January 2021 and June 2022. The Argentine tactician missed out on the England international at the time, but he will finally have the chance to coach him after taking over at Carrington. Therefore, Romano believes Rashford will get the opportunity to play ‘for sure’ once he fully recovers. What can Rashford bring to Pochettino’s Man Utd? (Photo by Carl Recine/Carl Recine/Getty Images) The attacker has been unavailable since the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in early October. While it seemed to be a slight knock at first, it later turned out that Rashford’s condition is more serious than initially anticipated . But the good news is that the 29-year-old is nearing a return to the pitch. “Marcus, today I think, started being in the session on the field,” reassured Pochettino during Friday’s press conference (via the official Manchester United website ). “ I think he is starting to feel much better, we will see day by day, working with the feeling that he is going to provide us [with something] after every single training session, increasing the progression of the recovery.” Once Rashford is available, the new MUFC boss will have more room to manoeuvre in attack. The Man Utd academy product is most comfortable playing on the left side, and he offers a different skill set from Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu. Moreover, he can be a solution for the centre-forward role amid Sesko’s continued absence, even though Joshua Zirkzee should be considered the first option.

That remains the team’s only victory in the English top flight this season, and one of three in all competitions. Pochettino arrived at Old Trafford last week as Michael Carrick’s replacement, with the club trusting him to turn things around. Looking forward to United’s home support In his first programme notes as United manager, Pochettino looked forward to being in the home dugout at Old Trafford for the first time in his career. He said: “It is an incredible feeling to be at Old Trafford today for the first time as Manchester United head coach.” “We are really excited to be here and I want to thank everyone who has given us such a special welcome. Myself and my coaches demand a lot from ourselves and a lot from our players but we don’t ask anything from you because we know just how incredible the support always is inside Old Trafford.” “Having the passion of more than 70,000 people pushing us forward is a moment that I have been thinking about since we landed in Manchester.” Man United Premier League Results: 2026/27 Season Date H/A Opponent Score Result 22/11/2026 A Liverpool 0-4 L 08/11/2026 H Aston Villa 4-4 D 31/10/2026 A Chelsea 0-2 L 25/10/2026 H Bournemouth 0-3 L 18/10/2026 A Leeds 1-1 D 10/10/2026 H Tottenham 1-1 D 20/09/2026 A Fulham 1-1 D 13/09/2026 H Manchester City 0-1 L 06/09/2026 A Everton 2-2 D 30/08/2026 H Ipswich 5-2 W 22/08/2026 A Hull City 0-2 L Players giving their all to turn the season around Pochettino went on to reveal that the players are giving their everything to help turn United’s season around. He continued: “We are enjoying working with this group of players and can tell that they really care about United and are giving everything to change the situation.” “We are building together day by day and game by game. We are already starting to make progress. I know the responsibility that comes with leading this club. We have to always be pushing to improve everything as much as possible.” “We understand the size of the challenge ahead to reach our ultimate ambitions but it’s something that inspires us and we are here ready to take it on together. Our first objective is very simple, to be competitive in every single action and show the energy on the pitch that will make you proud of our team.” The Argentine went on to issue his trademark ‘Vamos’, concluding: “Today is a great opportunity to show that we are ready to fight for everything Manchester United represents. e296a236886c89ea.content: The Premier League’s financial regulations have become an increasingly important factor in shaping clubs’ transfer strategies, with Manchester United among those seeking a more sustainable business model. Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Old Trafford could therefore present an interesting challenge, as the Argentine looks to strengthen his squad without compromising the club’s financial position. Until the end of the 2025/26 campaign, Premier League clubs operated under the Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR), which restricted their allowable losses to £105 million over a rolling three-season period. In practice, clubs could lose up to £15m without external funding, while the remaining £90m had to be covered by secure owner funding, usually through equity injections. However, not every expense counted towards the calculation. The regulations allowed clubs to exclude certain investments considered beneficial to football, including spending on infrastructure, youth development, women’s football and community projects, as well as depreciation of tangible fixed assets. Breaching the permitted threshold could have serious sporting consequences. Everton, for instance, were initially handed a 10-point deduction in November 2023 after an independent commission established that their adjusted losses had reached £124.5m, exceeding the permitted limit by £19.5m. The Premier League has since introduced a new financial framework, replacing PSR from the 2026/27 season with two complementary systems: the Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) and Sustainability and Systemic Resilience (SSR). The SCR focuses on clubs’ spending on their playing squads rather than their overall financial losses. It limits expenditure on first-team player and head coach wages, transfer-fee amortisation and agents’ fees to 85% of football-related revenue, including relevant profits from player sales. Certain expenses, such as non-playing staff salaries and investments in youth academies and women’s football, are excluded from the calculation. The new framework also introduces the SSR, which assesses clubs’ financial resilience through three separate tests: the Working Capital Test, Liquidity Test and Positive Equity Test. In other words, clubs must demonstrate that they can meet their short-term financial obligations, withstand potential financial difficulties and maintain a sufficiently healthy balance sheet. Meanwhile, teams participating in European competitions, including Manchester United, must also comply with UEFA’s stricter financial sustainability regulations, which set the squad cost ratio threshold at 70%. The financial implications of losing gambling sponsors While the new regulations encourage clubs to improve their financial discipline, Premier League sides must also find ways to maximise their commercial revenues. This has become particularly relevant following the collective decision to phase out gambling sponsorships from the front of matchday shirts, a measure that came into effect at the beginning of the 2026/27 season. Although gambling brands can still feature on shirt sleeves, training kits and stadium advertising, front-of-shirt partnerships have traditionally been among the most lucrative commercial agreements available to football clubs. Consequently, losing these deals could leave a considerable gap in the budgets of some Premier League sides, particularly those that relied heavily on gambling operators for sponsorship income. Clubs will therefore need to explore alternative commercial partnerships, with technology, artificial intelligence, financial services and international investment emerging as potential sources of replacement revenue. Indeed, several Premier League sides have already moved in this direction, with Crystal Palace partnering with technology company Temporal, Aston Villa signing a deal with Visit Rwanda and Everton agreeing a partnership with CMC Markets. This practice is not entirely unprecedented, as Belgium adopted a Royal Decree on 27 February 2023, which came into effect on 1 July 2023 and restricted gambling sponsorship on sports clothing. The regulations apply across the sector, meaning an online casino such as Madison Casino operates within the same broader Belgian regulatory environment as other gambling businesses. The Belgian measures illustrate how football clubs and gambling operators have had to adapt to changing advertising regulations, with sponsorship opportunities becoming increasingly restricted. As for Manchester United, their financial resources certainly dwarf those of Belgian clubs, but even the Old Trafford outfit must adhere to the Premier League and UEFA regulations. Therefore, Pochettino certainly won’t be handed a blank cheque, but perhaps his January budget could be sufficient to reunite him with some of his American pupils. The 54-year-old kept the door open for such a possibility in a recent press conference. “All the good players always have dreams to reach the last level. But now I think they need to be focusing on today, on [Tuesday’s] game, in their clubs,” said Pochettino during Monday’s press conference (via ESPN ). “I know really well for more than two years, all players with an unbelievable talent. And of course in the future when that happen, of course we are going to pay attention in case to make some decision and to pay attention to the player that we know really well.” With that in mind, let’s take a closer look at three American internationals who might be suited for a role at Old Trafford. f2851754d12cdd87.title: Man United legend makes huge prediction on Erling Haaland's future: 'Will be a Real Madrid within 18 months'
f2851754d12cdd87.text: Man United legend makes huge prediction on Erling Haaland's future: 'Will be a Real Madrid within 18 months'
f2851754d12cdd87.content:
Erling Haaland has been a Real Madrid target for a long time, but the stars never really aligned to bring the Norwegian star home.
Over the years, Los Blancos have maintained a perpetual interest in the Manchester City striker and have even been willing to pay big bucks for his acquisition.
Manchester City's continued success, stable project under Pep Guardiola and the player's renewals, however, kept the deal from materialising.
A lot has changed, however, in the past few months. With Guardiola leaving Manchester City, the project is now restarting far from the level it was in.
Further, the Cityzens have been caught up in numerous allegations, with the club now facing a threat of serious consequences. Amid all the tension, Haaland's departure is no longer seen as an impossible development.
Madrid-bound in the future? (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images)
Real Madrid, needless to say, are alert to the possibility and stand out as a top destination if the player is indeed considering an exit. The competition, needless to say, is very high, with clubs like Barcelona also in the mix.
Manchester United legend's verdict
Speaking on a podcast (h/t MARCA), Manchester United legend and English football pundit Gary Neville gave his honest thoughts on Erling Haaland's future and how he saw Real Madrid as a potential destination.
Beyond just a hunch, the legend went on to make a very committed statement on the same, claiming that Haaland will be a Real Madrid player in the near future.
"I am absolutely certain that Erling Haaland will be a Real Madrid player within a maximum of 18 months, perhaps at the end of the season." he said,
Will one make way for the other? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)
The big question around Haaland's potential arrival, needless to say, revolves around where he will fit into the starting lineup given Real Madrid's solid starting trio. Neville, however, explained the nuance and linked the situation with Vinicius Jr.'s departure.
"I think Vinicius will leave Real Madrid, Mbappe will move to the left wing and Haaland will be Real Madrid's centre-forward," he added.
Finally, Neville explained why signing Haaland makes sense for Real Madrid, especially given Florentino Perez's long-lasting desire to bring the best players in the world to the Santiago Bernabéu,
"If you look at Florentino Perez, he signs the best players in the world," noted Neville.
