50b71e98b192d330.title: Former Red Devil makes United pay as dubious refereeing extends to U18s defeat
50b71e98b192d330.text: Yuel Helafu scored after signing a new contract but Manchester United U18s lost 3-1 to Leeds United, remaining second in the league table. The post Yuel Helafu scores after extending contract as Manchester United U18s fall 3-1 at Leeds appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
50b71e98b192d330.content: Manchester United U18s took on Leeds United U18s away at Thorp Arch on Saturday morning. Darren Fletcher started Karim Cassim after the 17-year-old trained with the first team during the week, and Yuel Helafu who was rewarded with a new contract yesterday. There were familiar faces in the opposition side in Alfie Walker and Edward Ibrovic-Fletcher, who both made the switch from Manchester United earlier in the year . First half Torrential downpours meant the conditions weren’t the most conducive to playing technical football, and both sides took time to find their footing in the match, with little in the way of chance creation through the first half. United’s first opening came down the left wing when Jay McEvoy played a delicate lofted pass to Sam O’Brien in the left channel, but the England youth international was unable to pick out a teammate in the area. Approaching the half-hour mark, it took a wonder goal from Joe Bhaskaran to open the scoring. The Leeds captain picked up the ball after some pinball action in midfield and smashed a rocket into the top-right corner from over 25 yards out. Noah Ajayi had a chance from a wide angle after cutting inside, but his effort whipped past the far post and wide to leave United trailing at the break. Second half Early in the second half, the ball broke from the Leeds area for Cassim to run onto and side-footed narrowly wide of the right post. The poor refereeing decisions which have plagued the first team recently extended to the U18s when Jacob Watson conceded a penalty despite making a clean connection with the ball with his sliding tackle. Logan White scored from the spot, his 14th in the league this season, to extend the home side’s lead to 2-0. Jay McEvoy’s low corner delivery bounced through the area before falling to Kai Rooney, but the forward scooped the ball over the bar as he quickly snatched at it. Substitutes Jaume Camacho and Edson Dejonge-Seiros combined after entering the fray to create two openings in quick succession, but the latter couldn’t find the target. Yuel Helafu pulled one back in the 82nd minute after some nice work down the right wing with Dejonge-Seiros to escape into the area and fire past the keeper inside the near post. But Leeds restored their two-goal lead just a minute later. A clear foul on Noah Ajayi in midfield wasn’t called, and former Red Devil Ibrovic-Fletcher capitalised with a nice finish from 20 yards out to seal the three points. United remain in second place in the table but fall further behind rivals Manchester City. The youngsters now turn their attention to the FA Youth Cup, where they will take on Burnley on Thursday. cd78c810baf71d37.title: Man Utd handed major boost as late Bruno Fernandes decision confirmed
cd78c810baf71d37.text: Man Utd handed major boost as late Bruno Fernandes decision confirmed
cd78c810baf71d37.content:
Despite starting both of Pochettino’s games in charge so far and scoring twice against former club Sporting in Wednesday night’s chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw in Lisbon, Fernandes had emerged a surprise late doubt to face Brentford on Saturday after missing training at Carrington on Friday morning.
Man Utd released a statement to confirm reports that he had been absent due to illness, telling fans: “The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”
"He's affected by a virus from Portugal,” Pochettino said. “He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.
"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].
"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."
Also on Friday, it was reported that United had activated their option to trigger an automatic one-year contract extension for Fernandes, whose deal - which was previously due to expire in the summer amid further speculation over a move elsewhere - now runs until June 2028.
But Fernandes does start against Brentford, donning the skipper’s armband as usual and joining Patrick Dorgu, Joshua Zirkzee and Amad Diallo in a surprising-looking attack, with the latter passed fit after a knock suffered in midweek.
It means Cunha and Mbeumo are both only substitutes in a huge call by Pochettino, who has made three changes to the side who started the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield in his first game at the helm last weekend after Harry Maguire also shrugged off an issue suffered in Portugal.
He replaces Matthijs de Ligt as Leny Yoro also starts after his early red card on Merseyside was controversially overturned, with Mbeumo and Cunha replaced by Amad and Zirkzee.

92a6743466be84d7.content:
Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, and that could have been a huge spanner to throw into the works.
Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.
Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, Pochettino looks to have opted for a back four again.
It has been a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.
Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available and starts after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game and keeps his place despite having reportedly complained of an injury.
Amad Diallo - passed fit after a knock - and Patrick Dorgu join Fernandes in the attacking trio behind lone frontman Joshua Zirkzee, with Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo only on the bench.
Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain injured, as do midfielders Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino revealed on Friday that Baleba would be out for 10 to 12 weeks from when he first sustained his hamstring issue against Roma in early November.
Man Utd XI vs Brentford: Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Fernandes, Dorgu; Zirkzee
Subs: Darlow, De Ligt, Mazraoui, Shaw, Andrey Santos, Mount, Cunha, Lacey, Mbeumo
Injured: Rashford, Baleba, Ugarte, Sesko

Manchester United will host Brentford in a crucial Premier League 2026-27 encounter at Old Trafford on Saturday, November 28. The Matchweek 12 fixture will kick off at 8:30 PM IST, with Mauricio Pochettino searching for his first victory as Manchester United manager. Brentford, meanwhile, will look to continue their impressive campaign and take advantage of United’s defensive struggles.
The Red Devils have endured a difficult start under their new manager, suffering a 4-0 defeat against Liverpool before drawing 2-2 with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League. Brentford arrive in Manchester after an emphatic 4-0 victory against Everton and will be confident of securing another positive result.
Manchester United vs Brentford Match Details

- Competition: English Premier League 2026-27

Manchester United vs Brentford: Team Form
Manchester United are desperate to turn their season around after a disappointing run of results.
Pochettino replaced Michael Carrick as manager but has yet to register a victory in his opening two matches. United lost 4-0 against Liverpool before playing out a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon.
Their defensive problems remain a major concern, with the team struggling to prevent opponents from scoring first.
Brentford, in contrast, have enjoyed a much stronger campaign under Keith Andrews. The Bees sit sixth in the standings with 17 points from 11 matches.
Their 4-0 victory against Everton highlighted their attacking potential, although the absence of suspended striker Igor Thiago remains an important concern.
Manchester United vs Brentford: Injury Updates
Manchester United have several fitness concerns ahead of their home fixture.
Bruno Fernandes is doubtful after missing Friday’s training session because of a virus. The Portuguese midfielder will undergo a late fitness assessment before the match.
Marcus Rashford remains unavailable with a hip injury, while Benjamin Sesko is recovering from a shin problem. Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are also sidelined with hamstring and knee injuries respectively.
Amad Diallo is another concern after picking up a knock against Sporting Lisbon. Luke Shaw has returned to the matchday squad and could be considered for selection.
Leny Yoro is available after the Football Association overturned his red card from the Liverpool match.
Brentford will be without Igor Thiago, who is serving a suspension following his red card. Aaron Hickey, Nathan Collins and Rico Henry remain unavailable with injuries.
Kaye Furo, Antoni Milambo and Josh Dasilva are also expected to miss the encounter.
Manchester United vs Brentford: Predicted Playing XI

Manchester United vs Brentford: Head To Head
Manchester United have historically enjoyed the advantage in this Premier League fixture.
The two clubs have faced each other 10 times in the competition, with United winning six matches. Brentford have secured three victories, while one encounter ended in a draw.
Their most recent meeting at Old Trafford finished 2-1 in favour of Manchester United in April 2026.
However, Brentford have previously caused problems for the Red Devils, including consecutive victories in 2025.
Players To Watch
Matheus Cunha (Manchester United): Cunha returns after serving a suspension in the Champions League. His movement, creativity and ability to carry the ball forward could be important against Brentford’s defensive structure.
Vitaly Janelt (Brentford): The midfielder has been one of Brentford’s most consistent performers. His defensive work and ability to disrupt opposition attacks could prove particularly important against United’s midfield.
Manchester United vs Brentford: Match Prediction
Manchester United will have home advantage, but their recent defensive performances make this a difficult fixture to approach with confidence.
Brentford have demonstrated greater consistency and arrive with momentum after their impressive win against Everton.
The availability of Bruno Fernandes could significantly influence United’s attacking performance. If the Portuguese captain is unavailable, Pochettino’s side could struggle to create opportunities against a well-organised Brentford team.
Prediction: Manchester United 1-1 Brentford.

86aacdf91120552e.title: Just in: Romano confirms dropped Man Utd star will leave in January
86aacdf91120552e.text: Manchester United are reportedly planning to loan out their young defender Ayden Heaven for the second half of the season. On Saturday, Mauricio Pochettino made his Old Trafford bow as the Red Devils host Brentford for a Premier League fixture. 📋 Lining up for the Reds this afternoon… pic.twitter.com/qu6nKtJIlf — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 28, […] The post Just in: Romano confirms dropped Man Utd star will leave in January appeared first on utdreport .
86aacdf91120552e.content: Manchester United are reportedly planning to loan out their young defender Ayden Heaven for the second half of the season. On Saturday, Mauricio Pochettino made his Old Trafford bow as the Red Devils host Brentford for a Premier League fixture. Lining up for the Reds this afternoon… pic.twitter.com/qu6nKtJIlf — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 28, 2026 The Argentine manager started with Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro at the heart of his backline, while Lisandro Martinez has been shifted to left-back since the midweek game against Sporting Club. Matthijs de Ligt is the only centre-back on the bench, as Heaven is nowhere to be seen. Ayden Heaven set to leave Man Utd on loan (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The 20-year-old’s absence from the squad raised many eyebrows. After all, the London native was a regular feature under Michael Carrick this season. While some speculated a physical problem, Fabrizio Romano revealed that Heaven has been dropped because United are planning to send him out on loan in January. Ayden Heaven, left out of Manchester United squad today as he’s expected to leave in January to play more elsewhere. pic.twitter.com/NPsv4TgOGr — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 28, 2026 The Italian journalist has thus confirmed previous reports linking Heaven with the exit door . Pochettino will likely be interrogated on the issue after the contest, but the writing is on the wall for the rising centre-back. Could United regret letting Heaven leave in mid-season? (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images) With every managerial change comes a new pecking order, and it appears Heaven has gotten the short end of the stick on this occasion. The good news for the Arsenal academy product is that Man Utd aren’t willing to cash in on him just yet, but they’re only looking to give him additional playing time on a temporary basis. But unless United plan to sign a new defender in January , letting Heaven leave would leave the club short in personnel at the back, especially if injuries occur. It should be remembered that United have a packed calendar in January and beyond, especially if they can progress in the FA Cup.
86aacdf91120552e.body:
Manchester United menyiapkan kepindahan Ayden Heaven pada bursa transfer musim dingin, dengan satu alasan khusus.

Manchester United berencana meminjamkan bek muda Ayden Heaven pada paruh kedua musim ini agar mendapat tambahan waktu bermain. 5d03c5e1ead569a3.text: Manchester United had another awful time at Old Trafford against Brentford and one decision left former Arsenal forward Paul Merson perplexed
5d03c5e1ead569a3.content:
Man United receive immediate penalty verdict as Paul Merson left utterly baffled
Manchester United had another awful time at Old Trafford against Brentford and one decision left former Arsenal forward Paul Merson perplexed
Paul Merson was left baffled that Brentford were not awarded a penalty against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Leny Yoro was judged to have won the ball from Kevin Schade with United already 2-0 down on Saturday afternoon.
However, the French defender, starting the game after seeing his suspension for a red card against Liverpool overturned, appeared to get nowhere close to the ball as he brought down the Brentford star inside his own area.
Reviewing the challenge on Soccer Saturday, Merson said: Great ball by Damsgaard to put Schade away on the right-hand side. He gets in the box and Yoro comes to close him down.
"I think he might catch him here. He goes to shoot, he comes across and gets nowhere near the ball. They haven’t given a penalty I don’t know why. It looked like a penalty to me, it’s a corner. I’d have been interested to see what Mike thought there because he didn’t get anywhere near the ball."
Mauricio Pochettino's side started positively against the Bees with greater intensity in their pressing. However, old habits die hard and the visitors made sure to capitalise on the opportunities they were provided.
Callum Wilson twice got on the scoresheet in the opening half as United became the first team in the Premier League to concede two goals or more goals in six consecutive halves.
5d03c5e1ead569a3.body:
Paul Merson mempertanyakan keputusan wasit terkait insiden di kotak penalti Manchester United.

Paul Merson bingung mengapa Brentford tidak mendapatkan penalti setelah Leny Yoro melakukan tekel terhadap Kevin Schade di Old Trafford. Yoro tampak tidak menyentuh bola saat menjatuhkan penyerang Brentford tersebut di area terlarang. Sementara itu, Manchester United tertinggal dua gol di babak pertama setelah Callum Wilson mencetak dua gol untuk tim tamu.

5d03c5e1ead569a3.body_en:
Paul Merson questions the referee's decision regarding an incident inside Manchester United's penalty area.

Paul Merson was left baffled as Brentford were not awarded a penalty after Leny Yoro's challenge on Kevin Schade at Old Trafford. Yoro appeared to get nowhere near the ball when bringing down the Brentford forward in the box. 6cd3785119118b19.title: Four things we learned as Pochettino’s Man United collapse under the weight of the same old problems against Brentford
6cd3785119118b19.text: Manchester United's 3-0 home defeat to Brentford exposed goalkeeping and defensive issues, while key attackers were left unused. The post Four things we learned as Pochettino’s Man United collapse under the weight of the same old problems against Brentford appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
6cd3785119118b19.content: Manchester United returned to action today, hosting Brentford at Old Trafford in Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game. After a defeat to Liverpool last Sunday and a midweek draw away to Sporting CP in the Champions League, this clash with Brentford was meant to return United to winning ways. Manchester United v Brentford at Old Trafford Premier League Date Score Result 27/04/2026 2-1 W 19/10/2024 2-1 W 07/10/2023 2-1 W 05/04/2023 1-0 W 02/05/2022 3-0 W Unfortunately, that was not the case. United’s defensive frailties handed the Bees their first Old Trafford win, ending a run of five straight defeats in their last five visits. There was much to take from this game, and here is what we picked up as United lost 4-0 to Brentford: Lammens becoming a liability Pochettino needs to see that Senne Lammens cannot keep costing us games. He cost the team a win over Sporting CP, as both goals in that 2-2 draw were his fault. Then, against Brentford, both of Callum Wilson’s first-half goals were balls played directly to him, yet he failed to save them. It is frustrating that he is not making the simple saves he should. The Belgian international is under so much pressure, and it is reflected in his errors. Therefore, he needs to be taken off the firing line and made to earn his place back in the team. It is time that Karl Darlow played. Judging by his Leeds highlights last season, he cannot be any worse. Defensive frailties demand January action While we can blame Lammens for his poor goalkeeping, United’s poor defending has put him in that situation. The Red Devils’ defence is as easy to slice through as butter, and Wilson was made to look like a star because of it. Indeed, the defensive overhaul might not wait until the summer, as it could be too late. Pochettino needs quality defensive additions in the winter, because United’s Premier League survival may depend on it. Pochettino’s line-up gamble backfires Why Matheus Cunha was overlooked is hard to comprehend. Whenever United have been behind, he has been the player who forced things and dragged them back into games, as he did against AS Roma and Aston Villa. A full week’s rest should have had Cunha itching to play. Pochettino needs to rely on him; in Carrick’s last few games, he showed he can make something of the mediocre performances we have been dropping. That said, leaving Bryan Mbeumo on the bench is also concerning. With Benjamin Šeško leading the line, your best bet for scoring is having Mbeumo and Cunha on the pitch. That cannot be any clearer. Simplify the attacking play Before Brentford broke the deadlock, United had three great chances to score but failed to take them. In contrast, Brentford scored with their first shot on target, and not long after, they added another with their second. Earlier in the first half and throughout the second, United dominated possession. Still, they failed to capitalise, overcomplicating things in the final third and not knowing when to shoot or when to pass. Patrick Dorgu also had chances he could have converted but did not. United need to show hunger in front of goal, but unfortunately, they did not. Had they done so, it could have been a different story. It is unfortunate that wins keep eluding Manchester United. Yet there are positive signs, signs that if they finally get it right, we could be on for one famous resurgent run that silences the critics who had relegation and Manchester United in one sentence. Up next for United is a clash with Newcastle United at St James’ Park. Featured image by Michael Regan via Getty Images online polls The post Four things we learned as Pochettino’s Man United collapse under the weight of the same old problems against Brentford appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .

He began well by delivering two good crosses in the early stages, but his contribution dwindled somewhat as Brentford assumed control. Leny Yoro 4 – He was too soft on Wilson for Brentford’s second goal and fell asleep, affording the England international a free run at goal. He got away with what could have been a penalty. Harry Maguire 5 – A set-piece threat for United but he was twisted and turned by Wilson for the visitors’ opener. Lisandro Martinez 3 – Just not at it and struggled against Sango Ouattara. Hooked at half-time. Kobbie Mainoo 4 – One of his poorer games this season. Slow to the ball, not strong enough in his duels and dominated, especially by Mikkel Damsgaard. Youri Tielemans 4 – Although a fine effort of his struck the woodwork, his overall performance in the pivot was just as laboured as Mainoo’s. He was caught flat-footed for the third goal, which sealed the game for Brentford. Bruno Fernandes 5 – He endeavoured to make things happen, but very little was coming off for him. Amad 5 – A bright start, but he eventually drifted out of the game and was dispossessed in the lead-up to Brentford’s first goal. Patrick Dorgu 4 – He was presented with multiple opportunities to score but was unable to hit the target. One can only speculate what might have been had he converted at least one. Joshua Zirkzee 4 – While there were some nice touches and effective hold-up play, overall he was not nearly threatening enough in the striker’s role. Substitutes Luke Shaw 5 – Decent on his return from injury. Bryan Mbeumo 4 – Didn’t really make a difference, and certainly no improvement on Amad. Matheus Cunha 4 – Waste of a substitution. Shea Lacey 5 – Tested the goalkeeper with a powerful effort and looked to take his man on. Mason Mount 4 – Game was already lost by the time he came on. 7fcdfdb82fe98ac5.title: 0 saves, 0 punches: Senne Lammens’ disastrous form continues in Man United’s 4-0 Brentford defeat
7fcdfdb82fe98ac5.text: Manchester United lost 3-0 to Brentford at Old Trafford as Callum Wilson scored twice and Senne Lammens endured another difficult outing. The post 0 saves, 0 punches: Senne Lammens’ disastrous form continues in Man United’s 4-0 Brentford defeat appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
7fcdfdb82fe98ac5.content: Manchester United suffered a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Brentford on Saturday, 28 November, at Old Trafford in the Premier League. A Callum Wilson brace, coupled with goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade helped the Bees secure all three points and kept Mauricio Pochettino waiting for his first win. The Argentine made two changes to the team that came away from the Estádio José Alvalade with a 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP in midweek. Diogo Dalot replaced Noussair Mazraoui at the back, while Bryan Mbeumo made way for Patrick Dorgu. That meant that Senne Lammens had Dalot, Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez ahead of him. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans continued in the middle of the park, having now started every game under the Argentine manager. In attack, Dorgu and Amad were stationed either side of Joshua Zirkzee, who started at Old Trafford for the first time since December 2025. Bruno Fernandes, who scored a brace in midweek, recovered from an illness scare to continue in his preferred No. 10 role. United suffer another defeat United started the game well and had multiple chances to go ahead but failed to get the ball in the back of the net. They were subsequently punished in the 19th minute when Callum Wilson put the visitors ahead against the run of play. The goal pumped confidence into the Bees, who began to threaten the Red Devils’ backline. Things then went from bad to worse for Pochettino’s team when Wilson scored his second of the game in the 32nd minute. United tried to get back into the game but ended the break trailing by two goals. The Red Devils stepped up the pressure after the break, but Brentford refused to budge and even scored through Ajer in the 82nd minute. Schade added a fourth in second-half injury time to compound United’s woes and inflict their second 4-0 defeat in the last three game. While the attack’s inability to score will frustrate fans, there will also be questions asked of Lammens, who had an outing to forget. Senne Lammens Stats: 2026/27 Season Stat Premier League UEFA Champions League All competitions Competition Premier League UEFA Champions League All competitions Apps 12 5 17 Minutes 1079 450 1529 Starts 12 5 17 Avg rating 6.68 6.55 6.64 Saves 40 11 51 Goals conceded 12 4 16 Save % 76.9% 73.3% 76.1% Clean sheets 0 1 1 Penalties saved 0 0 0 Page 1 of 2 1 2 Stat Premier League UEFA Champions League All competitions xG conceded (PL) 22.22 – 22.22 Goals prevented (PL) 10.22 – 10.22 Passes 305 141 446 Accurate passes 193 93 286 Pass accuracy % 63.3% 66.0% 64.1% Yellow cards 0 1 1 Red cards 0 0 0 Page 2 of 2 1 2 Lammens has another outing to forget Lammens arrived at the game under scrutiny following his poor performance against Sporting CP in midweek. The Belgian was out to redeem himself against the Bees, but had another outing to forget. The 24-year-old registered 29 touches of the ball and made 28 passes with a mere 61% accuracy. He did not register any key passes and attempted 19 long balls, only eight of which found a teammate. Surprisingly, Lammens did not make a single save in the game and could not register a punch either. He did, however, make one high claim and perhaps should have done better for both goals. With an upcoming trip to Newcastle United next week, Pochettino could have a decision to make regarding his No. 1 spot. With Lammens now conceding 26 goals in 12 games, perhaps it is now time to give Karl Darlow a chance in midweek. cf85d0e90e42ed14.title: Manchester United player ratings vs Brentford as two get 3/10 but Shea Lacey good

cf85d0e90e42ed14.content:
Manchester United player ratings vs Brentford as two get 3/10 but Shea Lacey good
Man Utd were beaten 4-0 by Brentford in the Premier League as a desperately bad season hit a new low.
Manchester United could be bottom of the Premier League table on Sunday evening after they made it 10 games without a win in the competition by losing to Brentford.
United had started the game well but went behind when Senne Lammens let a Callum Wilson effort go through his hands into the centre of the goal. 13 minutes later they got hit on the break, with Wilson applying the finishing touch after good work from Dango Ouattara.
Mauricio Pochettino's first home game in charge ended in familiar fashion and a wretched United never looked like getting back into the game. Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade scored late on to round off a miserable afternoon.
Here's how the United players rated:
Senne Lammens: Made a world-class save but derived no confidence from it all. Had to save Wilson's opener and might have been a different game if he had done. 4
Diogo Dalot: Played a different role as he inverted into midfield and actually did well. Short passing range is fine for that role and put in a couple of dangerous crosses, but lost confidence in second half and poor for third goal. 5
Leny Yoro: One really strong run out of his own half that got United on the front foot, but needed to be stronger against Wilson in the build-up to the second goal. 4
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
Harry Maguire: A set-piece threat in the opposition box, heading against the crossbar from one corner. Should probably have been firmer when he tried to shut Ouattara down for the second goal. 4
Lisandro Martinez: Played well in midfield but looked so far off it here. Casual with his defending, outpaced by Ouattara and then sold himself so easily. No surprise he was taken off at half-time. 3
Kobbie Mainoo: Not as good as recent weeks and found it a bit tougher against a strong Brentford midfield. Been playing well, but needs to get back to his best form. 5
Youri Tielemans: Some good moments, turning away from danger smartly and got Zirkzee into a good position early on. Tactical shift enabled him to play higher up the pitch and hit the bar. 6
Amad: Closing in on a year since he last scored for United. Should have got an assist with a cross for Dorgu but drifted out of the game and offered little threat in the latter stages of the first half. 5
Bruno Fernandes: Probably not feeling 100% and drained by another dismal day in his United career. Toiled away but didn't have a big influence. 5
Patrick Dorgu: Put a header wide when he should have scored and had another excellent chance which he sent straight at Kelleher. A strong runner, but not a polished attacker. 4
Joshua Zirkzee: Has deserved his chance this week but the fact he is starting says it all. Just isn't good enough and doesn't have the quality or belief to make a difference. 3
Substitutes
Luke Shaw: Good clearing header under pressure and defended pretty well when he came on. 6
Bryan Mbeumo: Mocked by the away end after ditching them for United last summer. Free-kick into the wall. 5
Matheus Cunha: Came on at centre-forward but had little impact. 5
Shea Lacey: Fierce shot brought out a brilliant save from Kelleher. Has to start on Wednesday. 7
Mason Mount: A late sub. 5
Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, De Ligt, Santos

99de61a7121d04ce.title: Poll: Should Mauricio Pochettino drop Senne Lammens for Man United?
99de61a7121d04ce.text: Senne Lammens is struggling for form after a solid first year at Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino could look to take his goalkeeper out of the firing line.
99de61a7121d04ce.content:
Poll: Should Mauricio Pochettino drop Senne Lammens for Man United?
Senne Lammens is struggling for form after a solid first year at Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino could look to take his goalkeeper out of the firing line.
Senne Lammens enjoyed an encouraging first season at Manchester United but it's been downhill since then.
The Belgium goalkeeper had a tough summer as his error cost his national side their place at the World Cup, and those struggles look to have had a knock-on effect on his domestic form.
Lammens made two big mistakes in United's draw with Sporting Lisbon in midweek and he was at fault again on Saturday as he was far too easily beaten for Callum Wilson's opener.
Karl Darlow watched on from the bench as Lammens struggled at Old Trafford. The former Newcastle shot-stopper arrived at United on a free transfer in the summer and he is yet to make his Reds league debut.
But do you think he should be handed his chance soon?
Would you take Lammens out of the side because of his recent patchy form and give Darlow his chance? Or do you think Lammens still has plenty of credit in the bank from his solid first season at United and Mauricio Pochettino should show faith in him and keep him in the team?
Let us know your thoughts by voting in the poll below:

Mauricio Pochettino menghadapi dilema pemilihan penjaga gawang Manchester United setelah penurunan performa Senne Lammens.

Penjaga gawang asal Belgia ini sebelumnya tampil solid pada musim pertamanya, tetapi kini posisinya mulai mendapat tekanan. Karl Darlow, yang bergabung secara gratis pada musim panas lalu, masih menunggu debutnya di liga dari bangku cadangan.

262f084d483bb305.text: Callum Wilson scored twice as Brentford secured their first victory at Old Trafford since 1937 and kept Manchester United in relegation trouble - how they rated
262f084d483bb305.content:
- Published
Manchester United
Man Utd XI
Senne Lammens: All the pressure on him but brilliant reaction save to deny Anthony. Could he have done better with the first goal? 5
Diogo Dalot: Picked out Bruno Fernandes with an excellent cross but Portugal team-mate couldn't convert. Did OK in a poor overall performance. 6
Leny Yoro: Wilson drifted off him for the opener. Didn't respond quickly enough to the danger for the second. 4
Harry Maguire: Early effort against the bar, then on-target header saved and another off the line. It's at the other end where the problems are. 5
Lisandro Martinez (off 46, Shaw): Played as left-back but didn't really work. Not strong enough defensively now either. Feels like end of his Man Utd career is looming. 4
Youri Tielemans (off 83, Mount): Did a lot of midfield scheming to try and create opportunities and hit the bar but midfield so easily bypassed by opposition. 6
Kobbie Mainoo: So much being asked of him in an under-performing side. Little wonder he is a long way off his best. 6
Amad Diallo (off 46, Mbeumo): A big threat on the right but home side couldn't make most of it. Surprise when taken off at half-time but Pochettino had to do something. 6
Bruno Fernandes: Recovered from virus to play. Usual invention and never stopped trying but you wonder how long he has left here. 6
Patrick Dorgu: Excellent opportunity at far post but headed wide. Passing not quick or clinical enough. Wasted another chance in second half. 5
Joshua Zirkzee (off 62, Cunha): Successive starts for the first time since December and brought early save out of Kelleher. Did a lot of running, but is he good enough? 6
Subs:
Bryan Mbeumo (on 46, Amad): Free-kick into the wall but more expected against his old club. 5
Luke Shaw (on 46, Martinez): Return after seven-week absence and definitely improved home side's defending. 6
Matheus Cunha (on 62, Zirkzee): Didn't really get on the ball enough to make an impact. Had a late shot. 5
Shea Lacey (on 70, Dorgu): Crowd was willing him to do well and he forced Kelleher into a good save. 7
Mason Mount (on Tielemans, 83): 6
Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, De Ligt, Mount, Andrey Santos.
Brentford
Caoimhin Kelleher: Wasn't worked hard enough when the home side had the opportunity in first half, then reacted well to push away Dorgu effort. 6
Michael Kayode: Got in a tangle with Maguire at the far post at a corner but used strength legally. Sensational arcing run away from own box at start of second half. 7
Kristoffer Ajer: Solid and effective partnership in the middle with Ajer. Unfussy defending and home attack not good enough to exploit weaknesses. Late goal as well. 8
Sepp van den Berg: Helped out because home side didn't start with a conventional number nine but always seemed to be in control. 7
Keane Lewis-Potter: Solid in defence, lethal on the counter-attack. Very effective performance. 7
Mamadou Sangare: Returned to starting line-up and blazed early chance over but was a rare blemish on an otherwise excellent day. 8
Vitaly Janelt: Easy to go unnoticed but always seems to be in the right place, which keeps Brentford ticking over. 7
Dango Ouattara (off 87, Carvalho): Assist for the first and kept his cool for the second, cutting inside Martinez and pass through Maguire's legs for Wilson to score. 8
Mikkel Damsgaard: Had the vision to create the opener, via Ouattara's pass. Exceptional pass to release Ouattara for the second. Most effective creative player on the pitch. 9
Jaidon Anthony (off 87, Diouf): But for Lammens, would have put Brentford in front with instinctive overhead kick. Another effort flicked wide off Maguire. Big threat. 8
Callum Wilson: Clinical finish to put the visitors ahead. Tap-in for the second. Will hope second-half injury that forced him off is not serious. 8
Subs:
Kevin Schade (on 52, Wilson): Tried to make inroads from the left. Completed the scoring with late finish. 6
Mathias Jensen (on 70, Damsgaard): Brought on to ensure victory and did his job. 6

14d8e9f57d0017c2.title: Manchester United mauled by Brentford in Pochettino’s ugly Old Trafford debut
14d8e9f57d0017c2.text: Utter despair for Mauricio Pochettino’s new Manchester United project; sheer deserving delight for Brentford who ended an 89-year wait to win here. Keith Andrews’ team made this history for the club because they were ruthless – Callum Wilson’s double preying on the latest Senne Lammens, Lisandro Martínez and Harry Maguire errors and sending them on their way to a memorable triumph. Jamie Jackson’s full report will follow Continue reading...
14d8e9f57d0017c2.content:
Utter despair for Mauricio Pochettino’s new Manchester United project; sheer deserving delight for Brentford who ended an 89-year wait to win here.
Keith Andrews’ team made this history for the club because they were ruthless – Callum Wilson’s double preying on the latest Senne Lammens, Lisandro Martínez and Harry Maguire errors and sending them on their way to a memorable triumph.
For United, it was the latest in a sorry catalogue of horror-shows, from front to back. To paraphrase the famous cricket aphorism: Pochettino’s team can’t attack, can’t defend, and the midfield is a liability too.
With a high five for Fred the Red and a Stretford End showing a: “Welcome Poch, Keep Our Home Not Our Owners” banner in the Newton Heath green and gold (to further make the point), Pochettino’s first home match began with a bounce and ended abysmally.
His men are rooted in 19th place and if Crystal Palace beat Hull on Sunday, Pochettino’s team will be bottom. They have now gone 10 games without a league win, their longest winless top-flight sequence since the 11-game run of November 1989 to February 1990.
Further gloom can be found in Diogo Dalot’s hapless inability when rising to head late on, the ball going to Kristoffer Ajer, who lashed home for Brentford’s 82nd-minute third. Then, Kevin Schade’s added-time fourth, Dalot this time keeping the German onside. Wilson’s goals arrived in the opening half, making United the first team in Premier League history to concede two in six consecutive periods. And this was the Bees’ first away victory of the season in the competition.
When Ajer netted, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and his chief executive, Omar Berrada, were again heckled by furious home fans. “You’re going down with the City” sang the travelling number and, who knows, they may be correct.
- Jamie Jackson’s full report will follow

cbc29781656b1912.text: Manchester United sank to another frightening low in Mauricio Pochettino's first home game in charge, thrashed 4-0 by Brentford at Old Trafford.
cbc29781656b1912.content:
Manchester United vs Brentford; Premier League
Manchester United vs Brentford. Premier League.
Old TraffordAttendance74,026.
Man Utd 0-4 Brentford: Mauricio Pochettino's Old Trafford debut ends in nightmare after Bees thrashing
Report and free match highlights as Brentford win at Old Trafford for the very first time to condemn Mauricio Pochettino to nightmare home debut as manager; Callum Wilson scored twice, with goals in the second half from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade; United could finish weekend bottom
Saturday 28 November 2026 17:07, UK
Manchester United sank to another frightening low in Mauricio Pochettino's first home game in charge, thrashed 4-0 by Champions League-chasing Brentford at Old Trafford.
United have now lost half of their 12 Premier League games this season, and as a result, are consigned to another week in the relegation zone. They could conceivably be bottom by the end of the weekend.
If Pochettino did not know or understand the scale of the task in front of him, this latest non-performance captured the chaos perfectly.
The threat of relegation is real.
Harry Maguire kissed the crossbar with a header early on and Patrick Dorgu missed a sitter, but the difference in final third quality was striking. Callum Wilson scored twice in a miserable first half for Pochettino, whose presence on the touchline did little to improve how submissive his players were in and out of possession.

Amad was robbed for the opener before Senne Lammens allowed Wilson's strike to flash through his fingers. The 34-year-old's second was easier still, rounding off a quick break fashioned by a cutting Mikkel Damsgaard pass and a smart run from Dango Ouattara.
Defensive frailties continue to plague a team devoid of any confidence and the second half offered no respite. Leny Yoro, sent off at Liverpool last week before the decision was overturned, was lucky not to concede a penalty when Kevin Schade went racing through on goal. The substitute could have added a third moments later as gaps got larger and legs tired of chasing shadows.
But the visitors had plenty more opportunities to improve the scoreline and took two of them. Kristoffer Ajer netted an easy third from a corner and Schade made good on his earlier threat by chipping Lammens for a stylish fourth.
United have lost successive league games by at least four goals for the first time since Boxing Day 1963. Just three games into his tenure, the outlook for Pochettino already looks bleak.

3b28b0d4d10f0715.content: A section of the Old Trafford supporters have directed their frustration at Manchester United officials Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox during Saturday’s 0-4 defeat to Brentford. The Red Devils suffered yet another humiliating result in what is shaping up to be one of the most horrendous campaigns in the club’s history. The fallen Premier League giants had their moments, but they failed to make the most of their chances. On the contrary, Brentford were particularly clinical in front of goal. Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half, while Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two late goals, adding insult to injury. Man Utd fans roast Omar Berrada & Jason Wilcox (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Unfortunately for United, this game has seen them register new unwanted records. For instance, they have become the first Premier League club to concede two goals or more in seven straight halves. Moreover, Pochettino suffered back-to-back 0-4 defeats in his first two league outings as Man Utd boss. The Argentine has thus failed to record a victory in his first three games in charge after replacing Michael Carrick earlier this month. Saturday’s defeat left United 19th in the table, and they could find themselves at rock bottom if Crystal Palace win tomorrow. However, the Old Trafford matchgoers didn’t have a bad word to say to Pochettino, realising that the club’s issues run much deeper. Instead, the Man Utd supporters vented at the club’s CEO Berrada and Director of Football Wilcox, who were in attendance. A lot of supporters near the directors' box stood up and vented at Wilcox and Berrada. Some fans now singing 'You're not fit to wear the shirt'. #mufc — Samuel Luckhurst (@samuelluckhurst) November 28, 2026 The Sun’s correspondent Samuel Luchurst , who described the scene, added that the MUFC players also receive their share of the abuse. The United supporters chanted ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’ at the players, who tried to escape the ground as swiftly as possible after the full-time whistle, only to be instructed by Pochettino to do the traditional post-match lap and face the music. ae2cdb442f81caad.title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs Brentford: Mainoo among five players handed disastrous 1/10s
ae2cdb442f81caad.text: Manchester United endured a humiliating afternoon at Old Trafford, suffering a crushing 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino took a major gamble with his starting XI, leaving Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha on the bench. However, the decision backfired as United squandered several promising opportunities during the opening 15 […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
ae2cdb442f81caad.content: Manchester United endured a humiliating afternoon at Old Trafford, suffering a crushing 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino took a major gamble with his starting XI, leaving Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha on the bench. However, the decision backfired as United squandered several promising opportunities during the opening 15 minutes. Callum Wilson punished their wastefulness by scoring twice in the first half, leaving the Red Devils facing an uphill battle. United continued to make costly errors after the break, allowing Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade to add late goals and complete a miserable afternoon for the hosts. Player Ratings Senne Lammens – 2/10 Produced an outstanding point-blank save to deny Anthony but should have done better to prevent Brentford’s second goal. Diogo Dalot – 1/10 Delivered a good cross for Fernandes in the 10th minute but offered little in either attack or defence for the remainder of the game. Played two Brentford attackers onside for the fourth goal. Leny Yoro – 2/10 Poorly positioned for Brentford’s opening goal but produced a superb one-on-one tackle to deny Kevin Schade, despite already being on a yellow card. Harry Maguire – 2/10 Hit the post during the opening stages of the contest but was caught off guard for the second goal, which effectively sealed United’s fate. Lisandro Martinez – 2/10 Made a good block to deny Ouattara but was partly at fault for Brentford’s second goal. Kobbie Mainoo – 1/10 Amorim wanted him to become more athletic and the Portuguese was right. He was over run on almost every occasion and rarely produced a meaningful progressive pass. Youri Tielemans – 1/10 The Belgium captain played a good through ball to send Zirkzee through on goal and struck the crossbar with an effort from distance in the second half. However, he was badly outpaced by Kevin Schade and eventually lost his marker for the third goal. Bruno Fernandes – 3/10 Failed to hit the target after being picked out by a good cross from Dalot. Should have registered an assist, but Dorgu could only fire a simple effort straight at the goalkeeper. Amad Diallo – 2/10 Diallo should have done better with an early opportunity after Maguire hit the post. He was dispossessed in his own half in the build-up to the opening goal. Patrick Dorgu – 1/10 Dorgu missed a glorious opportunity in the 16th minute after Diallo picked him out with an excellent cross to the far post. His finishing let him down again after the interval, wasting further chances created by Fernandes and Zirkzee. Joshua Zirkzee – 1/10 Fired a tame effort straight at the goalkeeper when he should have squared the ball to Dorgu. Later, with United 2-0 down, he chose to pass to Dorgu despite Fernandes being in a much better position to score. Pochettino cannot give him another opportunity. Substitutions Luke Shaw – 2/10 Rare appearance this campaign. Bryan Mbeumo – 3/10 Should have started. Matheus Cunha – 3/10 Should have started. Shea Lacey – NA Too late to rate. Mason Mount – NA Too late to rate. Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .

23f6ced17f3706d1.content: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge. The Red Devils have now conceded four times in three consecutive Premier League games, leaving them in 19th position in the table. Relegation looks a very real possibility at this stage, with almost every player underperforming, including Senne Lammens . The Belgian was at fault for two of the goals, and his form is a real concern, given that the team are in a relegation scrap. Attacking selections did not help INEOS, whose summer recruitment has been a disgrace and is one of the main reasons for this mess, need to strengthen at the back in January. But the new head coach cannot be absolved of all blame tonight. With the chips down, he should have opted to start his big guns. Instead, he opted to drop Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha in favour of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu. This comes after his horror call to start Matthijs de Ligt against Liverpool. Both have scored a combined 16 goals in United colours over two seasons, while the Bees already have 24 to their name this season. Joshua Zirkzee v Patrick Dorgu Stat Joshua Zirkzee Patrick Dorgu Apps 88 58 Minutes 3345 3548 Goals 11 5 Pochettino needs to get his selection calls right The Dutchman’s link-up play can prove useful in Europe, where the pace of the game is a bit slower. But he always gets overwhelmed in the English top flight due to his tendency to take his time. And the Dane kept popping up in good areas, and as many as three glorious chances were spurned by him. The ball kept falling to him in the box, and he is certainly not the club’s best finisher. Amad has been a shadow of his former self since Ruben Amorim departed, and Shea Lacey has impressed in all his cameos. It is time to drop the Ivorian for the Carrington graduate. Pochettino needs to go all guns blazing next time, as for this particular United side, attack seems to be the best form of defence. aed31181007a8344.text: Man Utd suffered their sixth defeat of the Premier League season against Brentford on Saturday afternoon.
aed31181007a8344.content:
Angry Man United fans hurl insults at Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox after Brentford hammering
Man Utd suffered their sixth defeat of the Premier League season against Brentford on Saturday afternoon.
Manchester United supporters hurled insults at Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox as they left the Old Trafford directors' box after defeat to Brentford.
United CEO Berrada and sporting director Wilcox have been targeted by matchgoing fans this season, and they faced fresh insults on Saturday afternoon.
Brentford won 4-0 at Old Trafford, prompting the pair to face a barrage of insults from furious supporters around the directors' box.
United's security guards made their presence known in the directors' box when Brentford scored their third goal, but the anger among supporters reached boiling point following the full-time whistle.
Berrada and Wilcox were targeted by supporters as they left their seats to leave the directors' box. Expletives were hurled in their direction until they disappeared from sight into the executive suite.
Make sure you never miss the latest Manchester United news and opinion by making Manchester Evening News one of your Google preferred sources.
The Reds sit in the Premier League relegation zone, having last won a league game against Ipswich Town in August. United fans have continued to protest against the club's ownership, and anti-Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe banners were unfurled in the Stretford End before the Brentford game.
Berrada recently sat down for an interview with Sky Sports in which he accepted responsibility for the club's situation.
"We take the criticism. A lot of it is fair. It is our responsibility to run the club. And yes, you know, coaches have a very important role to play," he said.
"Players, of course, have to perform at the highest level consistently for any coach really, because they're part of a club that when you're wearing the shirt, you have an enormous amount of responsibility, and that responsibility means that you have to be giving your best every day in training, in the matches, and that's the same for executives.
"So I understand the frustration from the fans. It's absolutely normal. My commitment is that we are going to do everything we can to make sure that we put ourselves in a position where we're competing to win titles consistently. And I think we've made progress in improving the squad over the last, you know, seasons."

The post 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
a289ef2ce380ee82.content: Patrick Dorgu endured a game to forget as Manchester United suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Saturday. Thrashed Mauricio Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut proved to be a nightmare as he and his players were well and truly beaten by Brentford, marking their first victory at United’s iconic home since 1937. United started brightly as they dominated possession and created chances. But they failed to make it count and were ruthlessly punished. The deadlock was broken by Callum Wilson, who gathered the ball just outside the area, spun away from United’s defenders and fired past Senne Lammens. Wilson doubled Brentford’s lead not too long after with an easy tap-in from a cross. Pochettino made changes at half-time, bringing on Luke Shaw and Bryan Mbeumo in place of Lisandro Martinez and Amad. The substitutions failed to provide any spark, as United’s response was cumbersome and fruitless. In United’s search for a breakthrough, Joshua Zirkzee lifted his effort over, Dorgu had a shot batted away, and Youri Tielemans came closest of all with an effort that clipped the crossbar. A Harry Maguire header was also stopped on the line, while substitute Shea Lacey also tested the goalkeeper with a powerful shot. But Brentford went on to secure the win in the 82nd minute as Kristoffer Ajer reacted the quickest to slam home from a corner kick. Kevin Schade then piled further misery on United with a cheeky lobbed finish. Full-time. https://t.co/6hDiXpUebs — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 28, 2026 United remain in 19th place in the Premier League table and could end the matchweek at rock bottom if Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday. Dorgu’s performance Pochettino elected to deploy Dorgu on the left of the attack in preference to Matheus Cunha, a decision that did not prove beneficial. Dorgu wasted several opportunities, and it could be argued that had he converted at least one, the outcome might have looked different for United. In 70 minutes on the field, Dorgu attempted three shots, just one of them on target. He ought to have done much better with the opportunity provided by Fernandes but could not get past Kelleher. He managed an individual shot accuracy of just 33.3%. The Denmark international found a United teammate with 14 of the 17 passes he attempted (82.4% pass accuracy). Dorgu failed to complete the one dribble he embarked on. He also did not contribute a tackle or interception. However, he won six of the eight duels he delved into. He also won three fouls. a3d9c32feb1228a5.title: Bayern overcomes injuries, red card to stay unbeaten in Bundesliga, Man United jeered off in England
a3d9c32feb1228a5.text: Bayern overcomes injuries, red card to stay unbeaten in Bundesliga, Man United jeered off in England
a3d9c32feb1228a5.content:
Bayern overcomes injuries, red card to stay unbeaten in Bundesliga, Man United jeered off in England
BERLIN (AP) — Bayern Munich overcame an injury crisis and a red card for captain Joshua Kimmich to remain unbeaten in the Bundesliga on Saturday, while Manchester United was jeered off after another heavy loss.
Bayern’s 0-0 draw at Hamburger SV maintained its unbeaten league start but it could allow leader Borussia Dortmund to go four points clear on Sunday with a win at home over Bayer Leverkusen.
United fans left early as Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge ended in 4-0 loss to Brentford. It's the second 4-0 defeat in as many games under the new coach and means the storied club will remain on the bottom of the Premier League table.
Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, Lazio and Inter Milan were all playing later.
Bayern's bruising time in Bundesliga
Bayern was without injured stars Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari among others, forcing coach Vincent Kompany to give the 19-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora his first start up front.
His team was reduced to 10 men before the break when Kimmich was run into off the ball and he retaliated by pulling the hair of the opponent.
Kompany sent on Luis Diaz for Bara Sapoko Ndiaye after the interval, while midfielder Konrad Laimer followed for the 18-year-old Lennart Karl soon after. Laimer hobbled off late to become the next injured player, however.
Hamburg defender Mario Vuskovic played the whole game in his first start since returning from a doping ban.
Paderborn and Cologne enjoyed big wins over Schalke and Elversberg, respectively. Paderborn defeated Schalke 8-1 for its biggest-ever Bundesliga victory and Marius Bulter scored a hat trick as Cologne routed Elversberg 5-0.
Urs Fischer’s Mainz scored two late goals to beat his former side Union Berlin 2-1. Fischer led Union to Bundesliga promotion in 2019 and later the Champions League, but now the Köpenick-based club is in a battle for survival.
Stuttgart was hosting Eintracht Frankfurt later.
Rayo shines in Spain
Jorge de Frutos pounced with the winner for Rayo Vallecano to stun Champions League participant Real Betis with a 1-0 victory in Seville. It was the fourth victory of the campaign for the modest but fiercely proud left-wing club from Madrid’s gritty neighborhood of Vallecas.
Rayo’s bigger city rivals, Real and Atlético Madrid, were playing later and looking for wins to pressure La Liga leader Barcelona. Real could draw level with Barcelona with a win at home over Alaves, while Atlético was not far behind before its trip to Elche.
Athletic Bilbao held on to win at Malaga 403.
Also later, Serie A leader Lazio was playing at Torino, Inter Milan was welcoming Genoa, and Ligue 1 leader Paris Saint-Germain was hosting Lorient among other games in France.
